npc:theocritus.text: Theocritus. At the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn, Theocritus watches over the kingdom and opposes Morganth. The eccentric human archmage lives apart from others, surrounded by servants and magical scrying devices. Archmage Theocritus keeps his own stronghold in the kingdom of Stormwind. He lives in the Tower of Azora, near the eastern road to Redridge. Eccentric in his habits, he enjoys a comfortable life with a large household staff, including gnomish attendants and his clothier, Morley Eberlein. He keeps apart from the everyday concerns of local villagers, yet his magic guards eastern Elwynn. The fallen mage Morganth is Theocritus's greatest concern. Morganth works from the Tower of Ilgalar in the nearby Redridge Mountains, and Theocritus sees him as both a personal enemy and a danger to Stormwind. For months, Theocritus has used arcane research to undermine him. With scrying devices such as the Eye of Azora, he watches Morganth's actions and probes his thoughts. He also studies the magical pendants worn by Morganth's Shadowhide gnolls, hoping to turn their master's creations against him with an arcane pulse that can immobilize the entire pack.

npc:thyn-tel-bladeweaver.text: Thyn'tel Bladeweaver. At Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver searches for the vanished Priestess Velinde Starsong. She sends trusted Alliance adventurers after clues to Velinde's whereabouts and the mystery of the Scythe of Elune. On the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver keeps watch as a night elf sentinel. Priestess Velinde Starsong vanished without a word, and Thyn'tel refuses to let her trail go cold. Believing grave forces may be involved, she sends trusted adventurers to search Velinde's belongings and learn where her journey led.

npc:tirion-fordring.text: Tirion Fordring. Tirion Fordring is a legendary paladin and former lord of Mardenholde Keep, now living in quiet exile in the Eastern Plaguelands. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, he was stripped of his title and lands for honoring a debt of honor to an enemy orc. From his modest cabin along the Thondroril River, he watches over the tragedy unfolding across Lordaeron and worries for his son. Before the ruin of Lordaeron, Tirion Fordring was renowned as one of the kingdom's finest knights. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the order Archbishop Alonsus Faol founded during the Second War, Tirion fought the Old Horde with plate, hammer, and holy devotion. He was revered as an unyielding paragon of the Holy Light. Following the Second War, Tirion governed the region of Hearthglen from Mardenholde Keep with his wife Karandra and young son Taelan. His reign ended when he encountered an aged orc warrior named Eitrigg living as a hermit. Recognizing the veteran's deep honor, Tirion gave his word to protect him. When Alliance authorities discovered Eitrigg, Tirion fought his own countrymen to uphold his oath. For this treason against the Alliance of Lordaeron, Tirion was stripped of his nobility, excommunicated by the Silver Hand, and banished into exile; Uther spared his wife and son from the sentence.

npc:tiza-battleforge.text: Tiza Battleforge. In Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge guides young dwarven paladins in the Hall of Mysteries. She teaches that the Light calls for virtue, charity, and self-sacrifice, and tests initiates before they may wield its gift of resurrection. Tiza Battleforge guides paladins in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries. Across the Alliance, tutors send initiates to her for deeper spiritual study. Brandur Ironhammer sends them from Ironforge, Azar Stronghammer from Dun Morogh, and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker from Stormwind. Tiza teaches that the Holy Light asks more than martial skill. Its servants must offer humble service, show compassion, and stand firm against the Scourge and other threats.

npc:tyrande-whisperwind.text: Tyrande Whisperwind. Tyrande Whisperwind keeps watch over the night elves from Teldrassil. She is Elune’s High Priestess and the supreme leader of her people, who endured the War of the Ancients and the ten millennia of the Long Vigil under her guidance alongside Malfurion Stormrage. Now she commands the Sisterhood of Elune and directs the Sentinel army in Kalimdor’s defense. Born in the ancient kaldorei empire, Tyrande grew up with the twin brothers Malfurion and Illidan Stormrage. The brothers turned to druidism and sorcery, while she became a priestess of Elune. When the Burning Legion first invaded Azeroth in the War of the Ancients, Tyrande stood against it beside Malfurion. The Moon Goddess granted her direct favor, and Tyrande shaped the Sisterhood into a fighting force. Her priestesses wielded divine healing and lunar wrath as the kaldorei faced annihilation. After the Great Sundering and the sealing of the Well of Eternity, Malfurion and the druids entered the Emerald Dream for long hibernations. Tyrande took on the lonely task of defending their recovering realm. She formed the Sentinels, an elite cadre of warrior-women who patrolled Kalimdor’s forests through ten thousand years. During the Long Vigil, they kept watch over ancient evils and lingering demonic remnants. Tyrande held to her faith in Elune while centuries passed between brief reunions with Malfurion. When the Burning Legion returned during the Third War, Tyrande woke the sleeping druids to face the danger. Though she mistrusted the newly arrived orcs and humans, she helped forge a desperate coalition at Mount Hyjal. The night elves gave up their immortality at Nordrassil to destroy Archimonde. Mount Hyjal now bears the scars of that battle, and Malfurion is again occupied with guarding the Emerald Dream. From the grand Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, Tyrande governs the kaldorei and watches for Horde incursions as her people take their place in the Alliance.

npc:verner-osgood.text: Verner Osgood. Outside Lakeshire’s smithy, Verner Osgood keeps the forge working. He balances local trade with the Stormwind Guard’s demands for horseshoes, weapons, and armor as gnolls raid the hills. At Lakeshire’s forge, Verner Osgood makes horseshoes and other supplies for the town. His stock is constantly taken to make weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard. With the kingdom’s forces stretched thin and local garrisons short on supplies, Verner carries much of the burden of keeping Redridge’s defenders equipped. Gnoll raids threaten Verner’s work as well as the town’s horses. Packs ambush livestock in the Redridge hills and seize working horses that stray beyond Lakeshire. Verner recruits travelers to hunt the marauders and their packleader, Yowler.

npc:viktori-prism-antras.text: Viktori Prism'Antras. Above Darkshire, Viktori Prism'Antras keeps his gaze on the stars. Up the slope beyond the gryphon roost, Viktori Prism'Antras peers out from Duskwood's gloom. Undead incursions, ravenous spiders, and creeping shadows surround him, but his attention is fixed beyond the suffocating canopy. He hopes to build a fine optical telescope that will bring the stars into clear focus, giving him a quiet refuge from the dread engulfing the hamlet. In this cursed forest, even a delicate telescope takes work to build. Viktori follows blueprints from his gnomish friend, Cog Glitzspinner. He asks passersby to find rare lens-crafting materials and mechanical housings, including finely cut glass and metal lenses scattered across perilous ground.

npc:warden-thelwater.text: Warden Thelwater. In Stormwind, a prison riot has left Warden Thelwater besieged at the Stockade entrance. He calls for capable adventurers to stop the Defias prisoners before the uprising reaches the city above. Beneath Stormwind's canals, the Stockade holds the kingdom's most dangerous miscreants, petty thieves, and political conspirators. Warden Thelwater was charged with keeping them locked away, but an organized revolt caught the guards off guard. The prisoners overwhelmed security and seized the cells, leaving Thelwater barricaded at the entrance as he struggles to contain an armed uprising beneath the capital's streets.

npc:william-pestle.text: William Pestle. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle gathers supplies for Stormwind's apothecary. He and his brother Morgan run the shop in the Trade District, and William hires travelers to find candles, kelp, and herbs. William works from Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn while his brother Morgan Pestle tends the counter at Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind City's Trade District. From Elwynn Forest, William works with local gatherers to secure raw materials the city shops need. He sends regular shipments to the capital, where Stormwind's citizens rely on a steady supply of restorative salves, draughts, and powders. William often needs more than common garden herbs for his craft. He hires newcomers to gather wax candles carried by Elwynn's kobolds and crystal kelp from the murlocs of Crystal Lake, just east of Goldshire. The ingredients may seem strange to those unfamiliar with alchemy, but William believes they have potent virtues in a mixture.

npc:wizbang-cranktoggle.text: Wizbang Cranktoggle. On Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle keeps a network of buzzboxes working from Auberdine. The eccentric gnome engineer lives upstairs at the inn, far from the halls of Gnomeregan and Ironforge. Wizbang Cranktoggle brings Alliance ingenuity to Auberdine. The gnome engineer works on the inn’s upper floor, among tools and spare parts. The night elves here seek harmony with nature and follow ancient customs. Wizbang turns instead to practical mechanical problems, far from the solemn druidic traditions of Kalimdor. Along Darkshore’s rugged coast, Wizbang maintains a network of buzzboxes. His devices send automated reports and carry messages over long distances. Coastal weather and hostile wildlife often damage them. Wizbang asks travelers to find parts, salvage tools such as gaffer jacks, and recover electropellers so the network can keep working.

subzone:addle-s-stead.text: Addle's Stead. In southwestern Duskwood, Addle's Stead lies abandoned south of Raven Hill. Its first homesteaders fled long ago, and the Defias Brotherhood now uses the farm as a hidden staging ground. Addle's Stead fell into ruin when darkness overtook Duskwood. The Defias Brotherhood now uses the old farm. Its agents watch the perimeter and lurk in the farmhouse, while supplies fill the barn. Southwestern Duskwood's shadows help them evade the Night Watch and Stormwind authorities.

subzone:aldrassil.text: Aldrassil. Young kaldorei gather beneath Aldrassil’s vast boughs in Shadowglen. The settlement shelters trainers, merchants, and local leaders in hollows carved through the great tree. Aldrassil shelters young night elves in Shadowglen. Ramps wind through its immense trunk, passing trainers and artisans on the way to the high roost. Tenaron Stormgrip watches over the glade’s protection from there. Beyond the tree, Teldrassil stretches across the horizon, while novices learn their arts beneath Aldrassil’s canopy before venturing into Kalimdor’s troubled wilds.

subzone:alexston-farmstead.text: Alexston Farmstead. At Alexston Farmstead, wild Harvest Watchers prowl the ruined fields. Baros Alexston grew up here before becoming Stormwind's city architect. Alexston Farmstead lies amid Westfall's dry plains, abandoned like the neighboring estates. Its caretakers fled when banditry spread across the countryside. Now the fields have grown wild, and the Harvest Watchers left to tend the crops attack anyone who comes near the barren farmhouse. Baros Alexston spent his youth working these fields before leaving to pursue masonry and construction. He became one of Stormwind's most prominent citizens, helping design parts of the rebuilt capital. Something from his early life remains among the ruins.

subzone:algaz-station.text: Algaz Station. At Algaz Station, Mountaineers guard the northern road from Loch Modan toward the Wetlands. The outpost lies south of Dun Algaz, where the pass leads through the mountains. At Algaz Station, dwarven Mountaineers watch the road north from Loch Modan. The post lies east of North Gate Pass and south of Dun Algaz, guarding the route between the kingdom of Ironforge and the northern lowlands. The road carries trade and troops through the mountain tunnels, but the hills bring danger from wandering beasts and troggs. Mountaineers keep the way open and offer weary travelers a place for respite, repairs, and martial support before they enter the pass.

subzone:alterac-mountains.text: Alterac Mountains. The Alterac Mountains are a rugged, snow-capped range rising directly above the rolling pastures of Hillsbrad. Once the heart of a proud human kingdom, the slopes now harbor ruined settlements, bandit factions, and dangerous wilderness where travelers rarely walk unguarded. Long before the hills fell into chaos, these highlands formed the sovereign nation of Alterac, one of the seven kingdoms born from ancient Arathor. That legacy shattered during the Second War when King Aiden Perenolde struck a clandestine pact with the Old Horde, allowing orcish forces passage through the peaks in exchange for his kingdom's safety. The Alliance of Lordaeron uncovered the betrayal and deposed Perenolde, leaving the region fractured by martial law and territorial disputes. Following the devastation of the Third War, the mountains collapsed into complete lawlessness. The disinherited nobles of the realm banded together to form the Syndicate, operating out of the ruins of Strahnbrad and plotting to reclaim their lost dominion through sabotage and assassination. Between ruthless Crushridge ogres occupying the shattered capital, marauding gnolls, and the shattered magical ruins around Dalaran, the passes of Alterac remain some of the most perilous pathways in Lordaeron.

subzone:alther-s-mill.text: Alther's Mill. In the Redridge Mountains, Alther's Mill lies in ruins northeast of Lakeshire. Once it supplied timber to local builders, but now scavengers and predators haunt its grounds. Travelers heading east toward Stonewatch pass this grim mark of the frontier. Alther's Mill once supplied timber for Lakeshire and the nearby settlements. The clearing northeast of Lake Everstill gave millers access to timber in the mountains. Trouble spread across Stormwind's kingdom, and the Blackrock clan came down from the heights of Stonewatch. The millers abandoned their work, leaving the timber buildings and wheel to decay. With the workers gone, monstrous tarantulas, carrion vultures, and raiders took over the mill. Travelers on the path to the eastern passes must skirt its shadowed grounds carefully. Shadowy operatives and thieves also use the abandoned compound. Its discarded storage boxes and hidden corners let them practice lockpicking and carry out covert trades beyond the Lakeshire Town Watch's gaze.

subzone:amberstill-ranch.text: Amberstill Ranch. At Amberstill Ranch, the family tends the mountain rams and guards them from hungry predators. The homestead lies north of Gol'Bolar Quarry, along the snowy road to Loch Modan. Amberstill Ranch raises mountain rams prized across Khaz Modan for their strength. The Amberstill family tends the stables and paddocks, training the sure-footed beasts for snowy passes and steep cliffs. The ranch supplies riding mounts and livestock, while the family fends off wendigos drawn to the flock.

subzone:ameth-aran.text: Ameth'Aran. In Ameth'Aran, broken colonnades mark the ruin of a once-great Highborne city in southern Darkshore. Queen Azshara's nobles practiced arcane sorcery here before the Great Sundering shattered the ancient world. Now the vengeful ghosts of the elves who died here haunt the stones. Before the Great Sundering, Ameth'Aran and its sister settlement, Bashal'Aran, were twin centers of Highborne influence along the ancient coastline. Favored by Queen Azshara, Ameth'Aran's ruling nobles devoted themselves to unrestrained arcane experiments. The sorcerer Athrikus Narassin governed from afar in the Tower of Althalaxx. The city thrived until the Well of Eternity collapsed and tore the Kaldorei Empire apart.

subzone:angerfang-encampment.text: Angerfang Encampment. Dragonmaw orcs gather at Angerfang Encampment in the central Wetlands, threatening nearby dwarven settlements. Chieftain Nek'rosh Skullcrusher leads the renegades as they prepare to strike Menethil Harbor. Dragonmaw warriors hold the marsh around Angerfang Encampment in the central Wetlands. Barricades and watchtowers guard the camp, where warriors, bonewarders, and dark spellcasters loyal to the old ways gather. From these defenses, the clan raids travelers on the roads and menaces nearby dwarven digs, including Whelgar's Excavation Site.

subzone:anvilmar.text: Anvilmar. In Anvilmar, young Bronzebeard dwarves and displaced gnomes gather to train and prepare for the road ahead. The fortified outpost stands in snowy Coldridge Valley, in Dun Morogh, around a great stone forge. At Anvilmar, a central forge burns within sturdy stone walls in the northern crags of Coldridge Valley. Class mentors and supply vendors are here, alongside veteran mountain mountaineers who drill recruits before they set out into the wider kingdom. Snowdrifts shelter the outpost, but Frostmane trolls and wild beasts prowl the frozen valley, keeping its defenders on guard. Anvilmar may take its name from High King Modimus Anvilmar, who ruled the dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. The garrison keeps watch today, tending the forge fires as trolls and beasts roam the valley.

subzone:astranaar.text: Astranaar. Astranaar holds the Night Elves’ ground in central Ashenvale, across an island in the forest lake. The ancient forest road runs beside it, and Alliance travelers find refuge there as furbolgs, satyrs, and the Horde threaten the region. Wooden footbridges link Astranaar’s island to the mainland, crossing the forest lake. It is Ashenvale’s largest night elven settlement, where sentinels, priests, and artisans keep watch over the woodlands. Travelers find an inn, traders, and an expert leatherworker. On the high perches, a flight master sends hippogryphs to distant outposts across Kalimdor. Lanterns glow over Astranaar’s tranquil waters, but the town stays ready for attack. Raene Wolfrunner and other local leaders coordinate patrols and defenses against the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs advancing from the north. The Sentinels fear the furbolgs may assault the settlement.

subzone:auberdine.text: Auberdine. Ships crowd Auberdine's docks, linking Darkshore with Teldrassil and the Eastern Kingdoms. The night elven town is the Alliance's main port in northern Kalimdor, set between the Veiled Sea and pine-covered bluffs. Auberdine sits on the Veiled Sea, the only major settlement still thriving in Darkshore. Its ships sail to Stormwind Harbor and, by way of Southshore, to Menethil Harbor. Ferries cross to Rut'theran Village beneath the boughs of the World Tree. Unlike Teldrassil's secluded treetop cities, Auberdine welcomes travelers from across the sea. Lamps light its stone streets, and dwarves and gnomes mingle with merchants among low, arched timber houses. Elder Thundris Windweaver and the Auberdine Village Council govern the town, coordinating Darkshore's defense with the local Sentinels. Auberdine is a vital trade hub, though its name is rarely spoken in Darnassus, where memory dwells on the great cities lost to the Sundering. Trouble presses in from every side: aggressive murlocs raid fishing boats along the strand, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs push from the south, and foul magic drifting down from Felwood agitates the wildlife.

subzone:azurelode-mine.text: Azurelode Mine. In southwestern Hillsbrad, Azurelode Mine sends iron to the Alliance war effort. Southshore's militia guards the human laborers who work its tunnels. Southwest of the open farmland and just west of Southshore, Azurelode Mine cuts into the ridges along the coast. Human miners work deep underground under Foreman Bonds's watch, drawing iron for arms and armor. That iron helps Alliance defenders hold the region against the Undercity. Southshore's garrisons and town militia rely on Azurelode Mine for most of their raw iron. Tarren Mill targets the mine's workers and guards, seeking to break the supply lines that sustain Hillsbrad's human strongholds.

subzone:ban-ethil-barrow-den.text: Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den beneath Teldrassil's roots. The sacred chambers were made for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, whose spirits commune with the Emerald Dream. Now the den is a dangerous warren, and the druids within are at risk. Ban'ethil Barrow Den lies beneath Teldrassil's roots, with upper and lower chambers. Barrow dens shelter night elf druids as they sleep and send their spirits into the Emerald Dream. This den was made for the Druids of the Talon to commune with nature. Its halls once held quiet meditation, but the corruption spreading through Teldrassil's wildlife reached the Gnarlpine furbolgs. They invaded the den and made its hollowed chambers a fortified warren. The Gnarlpine tribe has gone mad under a mysterious corruption spreading across the World Tree. Its furbolgs drove out or endangered the sleeping druids, and now guard the winding tunnels fiercely, attacking any night elf who approaches. Teldrassil's defenders must drive them back to protect the vulnerable druids and the sacred relics trapped in the den's lower depths.

subzone:ban-ethil-hollow.text: Ban'ethil Hollow. South of the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus, furbolgs threaten travelers in Ban'ethil Hollow. The ravine also hides the entrance to Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Furbolgs roam the rocky descent into Ban'ethil Hollow. Their strange affliction has driven them mad, and they stalk the nearby road, ambushing couriers and wandering sentinels. The hollow lies just south of the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus, a reminder that Teldrassil's woodland is not wholly safe. At the ravine's back stands the entrance to Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Slumbering druids and ancient tunnels lie within, threatened by the maddened beasts outside.

subzone:baradin-bay.text: Baradin Bay. In Baradin Bay, reefs and wrecks make each crossing perilous. Its waters lie between Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. Kul Tiras once patrolled the bay with a powerful navy during the Second War. Baradin Bay links the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. Menethil Harbor lies on its Wetlands shore, and Southshore stands in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Shallow sandbanks and jagged shoals threaten ships, as do murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks. During the Second War, Kul Tiras and the Horde fought across Baradin Bay. The broken hulls of the Kul Tiran Third Fleet, called the Lost Fleet, lie half-submerged along the Wetlands coast. Other ships sank at Drowned Reef. Hostile spirits, salvagers, and sea beasts haunt the waters around the ruined ships.

subzone:bashal-aran.text: Bashal'Aran. Bashal'Aran lies in northern Darkshore, east of Auberdine, where satyrs and grells feed on lingering magic. A solitary elven ghost remains trapped by a centuries-old curse. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne in Bashal'Aran and its twin, Ameth'Aran. The powerful mage Athrikus Narassin governed both towns, whose splendid markets and temples honored Elune. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the cataclysm destroyed the settlements. For reasons lost to time, Athrikus used his arcane mastery to bind his second-in-command, the mage Asterion, in a moonstone seal within Bashal'Aran. Asterion's body perished, but his ghost remained shackled to the ruined shrine. Deth'ryll satyrs and grells now claim Bashal'Aran's crumbled stones. Drawn by magic lingering in the ancient masonry, these corrupted beings feed on its energy to strengthen their foul arts. They swarm the broken courtyards and terrorize travelers on Darkshore's forest paths, yet keep clear of the central shrine, where Asterion endures his endless vigil.

subzone:bathran-s-haunt.text: Bathran's Haunt. Forsaken herbalists now harvest rare plants at Bathran's Haunt, east of the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Their work is withering the woodland around the ancient kaldorei ruin. At Bathran's Haunt, crumbling night elf pillars stand north of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, tangled in Ashenvale's thick foliage. Once a tranquil kaldorei relic, the ruin now shelters Forsaken herbalists and their enforcers. They work among the broken marble in an open-air laboratory, harvesting rare woodland reagents for their experiments. The grass rots brown, blossoms wilt, and decay creeps through the grove as their work blights the ancient soil. Bathran's Hair, a unique remedial herb, grows only among these stones. Night elf and Alliance scouts see its harvest as a desecration of sacred elven soil, while Forsaken herbalists seek the plant's potent properties. The Horde has an interest in the herb's yield, but the Forsaken keep their methods secret. The corruption of the earth draws suspicion from outsiders and allies alike.

subzone:beggar-s-haunt.text: Beggar's Haunt. At Beggar's Haunt, Forsaken agents watch the eastern approaches from an old Stormwind tower. It rises on a hillside in northeastern Duskwood, near the mountain road to Deadwind Pass. Beggar's Haunt overlooks the hills east of Manor Mistmantle. Stormwind once kept guards in this tower to watch the kingdom's eastern approaches. As Duskwood fell into gloom, patrols withdrew to Darkshire and left the tower to the elements. Forsaken agents now use the ruins to study the region and watch it from within Alliance territory. They include members of the Royal Apothecary Society and the Deathstalkers. A twisting path behind the tower descends to Knight's Hollow, a secluded pool and waterfall. An unmarked grave lies there between two hooded stone statues like the guardians beside the Dark Portal. Nearby graves include the burial place of an Unknown Soldier. They recall forgotten clashes along this frontier, fought long before the Forsaken took the watchtower.

subzone:blackwolf-river.text: Blackwolf River. Blackwolf River runs from Cragpool Lake through Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. The Venture Company's logging and industrial work has fouled its waters. Blackwolf River runs through Windshear Crag, fed by Cragpool Lake. Venture Company loggers cut the surrounding woods with heavy machinery and buzzsaws. Sludge, oil, and logging waste drain into the current. The river carries the cost of the company's work through the basin.

subzone:blackwood-den.text: Blackwood Den. Blackwood Den lies under the Blackwood furbolgs’ corruption in southern Darkshore, near Ashenvale. The cave and camps that were once their peaceful home have fallen into madness. Volcor, a night elf scout, is trapped in the cavern and awaits aid from Auberdine. Blackwood furbolgs hold a rocky cave and crude camps near the southern border of Darkshore and Ashenvale. Corruption has taken hold of the tribe, and its members attack outsiders. Deep inside the cave, the night elf Volcor is pinned down and in danger. Scouts and travelers from Auberdine are needed to help him.

subzone:bloodtooth-camp.text: Bloodtooth Camp. In central Ashenvale, Bloodtooth Camp lies west of the Falfarren River. Ran Bloodtooth leads the corrupted furbolgs, who attack anyone who approaches. Alliance scouts target the camp as they work to cleanse the surrounding woodlands. Bloodtooth Camp lies southwest of the southern Moonwell and west of the Falfarren River. Its furbolgs were once bound to Kalimdor's sacred wilderness, but a lingering spiritual corruption has consumed their tribe. Ran Bloodtooth commands the crude settlement. His followers attack travelers and night elven protectors alike.

subzone:bough-shadow.text: Bough Shadow. In northeastern Ashenvale, Bough Shadow lies east of Forest Song beneath a colossal Great Tree. Its roots surround an ancient portal into the Emerald Dream. Bough Shadow gathers beneath a Great Tree whose roots wind around a natural crossing into the Emerald Dream. The Green Dragonflight guards the quiet grove. Emerald drakes such as Phantim and Dreamstalker circle above the canopy, while Emeraldon dragonspawn and oracles patrol the swirling green portal at the tree’s base. Mortals who approach without permission are turned away.

subzone:boulderslide-cavern.text: Boulderslide Cavern. Boulderslide kobolds dig deep in Boulderslide Cavern, at the far end of Boulderslide Ravine. They search the stone for glowing mineral formations. Boulderslide kobolds have carved a stronghold into the Stonetalon crags. They dig frantically for resonite, a rare purple crystal embedded in the stone. Its glow carries traces of earthen magic, and the kobolds turn fiercely against anyone who approaches their excavation.

subzone:boulderslide-ravine.text: Boulderslide Ravine. Along Webwinder Path, secluded Boulderslide Ravine cuts through the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains. The ravine has seen little of the fighting between Horde and Alliance. Its rocky slopes lead toward Boulderslide Cavern, while wild mountain beasts still roam there. Boulderslide Ravine lies off Webwinder Path in the Stonetalon heights. Loggers, night elves, and the Horde battle over timber and sacred glades elsewhere in the region, but military forces rarely disturb this narrow pass. Mountain rams and crag beasts such as Cliff Stormers roam its ledges and sheer stone walls. Prospectors watch the slopes, where rich mineral veins often surface along the way toward the deeper cavern network. Across from Boulderslide Cavern's entrance, a small cave overlooks the ravine. Rough torches light its weathered supply barrels and primitive tribal paintings. The crude designs resemble ancient tauren art, suggesting native tribes once traveled through these crags or found temporary shelter here, long before modern conflict reached the mountains.

subzone:brackwell-pumpkin-patch.text: Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. Defias brigands have taken over Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in southeastern Elwynn Forest. The farm once belonged to the Brackwell family, but now its cottage and fields serve as a hideout where conspirators meet and stolen mine gold is received. You find the Brackwell farm southeast of the Stonefield homestead, its fields no longer tended. The Brackwell family has vanished, driven away or worse as crime spread through the area. The Defias Brotherhood now occupies the sturdy cottage and overgrown fields. Brigands regroup here beyond the reach of Goldshire's patrols. Morgan the Collector and other prominent conspirators use the isolated farm to receive illicit gold taken from the forest's mines.

subzone:brewnall-village.text: Brewnall Village. Brewnall Village sits in Chill Breeze Valley, near the entrance to Gnomeregan. The Barleybrew family keeps this dwarven camp for brewing experiments and defense against wild beasts. Brewnall Village shelters the Barleybrew clan in Chill Breeze Valley, among the gnomish reaches of western Dun Morogh. The dwarven brewers work to perfect old recipes and make the finest stout. Tents and brewing gear fill the camp, with no permanent stone buildings. The Barleybrews test new ales while wolves and bears threaten the valley. Wandering mountaineers help gather rare ingredients and keep the area safe.

subzone:brightwood-grove.text: Brightwood Grove. West of Darkshire, Brightwood Grove's ruined farms shelter savage Nightbane worgen. Brightwood Grove lies within sight of Darkshire, where ruined farms and fences mark the town's edge. Nightbane worgen have made crude camps among the overgrown clearings and prowl close to town. Their presence threatens Darkshire, so the Night Watch and travelers passing through keep their numbers down to protect the settlement.

subzone:calmbreeze-inn.text: Calmbreeze Inn. Calmbreeze Inn refers to the primary establishments offering shelter and services across Zephras Isle, found in both Shen'dar Village and Valaanar. They serve as essential rest stops for travelers exploring the island, housing local trade trainers, innkeepers, and historical artifacts. The Calmbreeze Inns provide sanctuary amid the winding trails of Zephras Isle. In Shen'dar Village, the inn operates under Coriella Calmbreeze and doubles as a central hub where island tradesfolk gather, including mentors in herbalism, skinning, and enchanting. Across the way in Valaanar, another Calmbreeze Inn accommodates local wayfarers and shelters rare curios, including an audio crystal recording the history of the ancient rebellion in Eldre'Thalas.

subzone:camp-aparaje.text: Camp Aparaje. Grimtotem warriors hold Camp Aparaje in the eastern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. The tribe slaughtered the peaceful tauren who settled there and claimed the outpost. Camp Aparaje lies among the Stonetalon crags, where peaceful tauren once sought a quiet life in the highlands. Raiders from nearby Grimtotem Post struck under Grundig Darkcloud's lead. The attackers butchered villagers or drove them away. Survivors such as Makaba Flathoof mourn the loss of their home and fear for kin taken captive. Grimtotem warriors now occupy Camp Aparaje as a forward base for their aggressive tribe in the region. Many Grimtotem settlements bear blue markings, but the great totem here is carved with deep crimson paint.

subzone:canals-stormwind-city.text: Canals (Stormwind City). Stormwind's Canals wind between the city's districts, where walkers and anglers share the waterside paths. You can follow the Canals between Stormwind's districts, from the Trade District's markets to Old Town's aged alleys, the cathedral gardens, and the Dwarven District. Stone bridges, archways, and waterside walks pass the Gallina Winery, tailor shops, and quiet homes. Merchants and fishermen use the waterways, while the fortified Stockade entrance lies beneath the streets, holding Stormwind's most dangerous criminals and rebels. Stormwind's Canals were left in ruins when the Horde sacked the city during the First War. The waterways were restored as the capital rose again after the Second War. They are clean and repaired now, though rumors speak of a massive albino crocolisk beneath the docks.

subzone:cathedral-of-light.text: Cathedral of Light. The Cathedral of Light rises over Cathedral Square as Stormwind's chief sanctuary of the Church of the Holy Light. It is the spiritual heart of the city and the center of human priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Archbishop Benedictus leads the faithful from the Cathedral of Light, rebuilt after the First War's devastation. Archbishop Alonsus Faol and Bishop Benedictus guided its restoration, and its towering form remains a beacon of resilience. After the Scourge took Lordaeron during the Third War, the Church moved its seat south to Stormwind. From this great hall, Benedictus gives spiritual guidance to the Alliance. The Cathedral of Light is both a place of prayer and healing and the main headquarters of the Knights of the Silver Hand in the southern kingdoms. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker and Duthorian Rall train promising squires through the sacred trials of the Tome of Valor and the Tome of Divinity. High Priestess Laurena guides devout acolytes in the deepest tenets of the Light, preparing holy champions to defend the realm from the growing threats of the Defias Brotherhood and the Scourge.

subzone:cathedral-square.text: Cathedral Square. In Cathedral Square, faith and civic life meet beneath the Cathedral of Light. City Hall, the orphanage, and the Argent Dawn's Stormwind headquarters all stand here. Northwest of the Trade District and southeast of the Dwarven District, Cathedral Square draws the faithful from across the Kingdom of Stormwind. The Cathedral of Light rises above it, the foremost sanctuary of the Holy Light across Azeroth. Priests, paladins, and healers come to study, pray, and train. Citizens and pilgrims mingle with local schoolchildren, led by School Mistress Danna, in the square. Prayer shares the district with the work of the kingdom. City Hall and the Stormwind Orphanage anchor its civic life. Along the avenues, armorers and weaponsmiths serve holy crusaders, including Righteous Plates and Just Maces. The Argent Dawn keeps its Stormwind base here, where recruiters and representatives coordinate relief efforts and rally champions against the Scourge in the northern kingdoms.

subzone:cenarion-enclave.text: Cenarion Enclave. The Cenarion Circle gathers in Darnassus beneath Fandral Staghelm’s leadership of the night elven druids. The Cenarion Enclave is their central gathering place and seat of power in the capital, among its great hollows and living boughs. High above the Temple Gardens, the Cenarion Enclave gathers the Cenarion Circle beneath ancient oaks and ashes marked with runic bark. Its halls take shape from living wood and stone. With Malfurion Stormrage absent in the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm oversees affairs here and presses his ambitious vision for Teldrassil despite political friction with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Druids meditate by the streams, while the capital’s elven hunters gather here too. At the stables, skilled riders learn to tame Darnassian nightsabers. The Cenarion Enclave is known as a tranquil sanctuary, yet quiet business takes place beneath its westernmost bough. A refuge lies under the hollowed roots, where Darnassus’s clandestine rogues work shielded by the canopy above.

subzone:champions-hall.text: Champions' Hall. In Stormwind's Old Town, Champions' Hall is guarded and reserved for Alliance officers. Its quartermasters supply weapons, armor, and regalia to veterans who have proven themselves in battle. Champions' Hall stands behind a guarded entrance in Old Town, reserved for the Alliance's distinguished combatants. Military commanders gather around maps of Azeroth to discuss ongoing campaigns, among arms and the insignias of rank. Only Alliance soldiers who have earned the rank of Knight or higher may enter. Inside, quartermasters supply battle-hardened soldiers with elite weapons, armor, and mounts made to aid them against the Horde in contested lands.

subzone:charred-vale.text: Charred Vale. In southwestern Stonetalon, flames and smoke consume the Charred Vale. The Venture Company's logging left a once thriving woodland in ruins, where fire elementals roam and Bloodfury harpies guard their territory. The Charred Vale was once a thriving woodland in a basin of southwestern Stonetalon. Majestic treants guarded it, while native chimaeras and harpies made their home among the trees. The Venture Company brought the ruin. Its goblins clear-cut the forest with explosive machinery, corrupting the treants and waking chaotic fire elementals. The treants eventually drove the goblins back, but the loggers left the land broken and scarred by fire. Whatever foul devices they used as they retreated also tainted the valley. Blackened ancients wander blindly through smoke and ash, among enraged elementals. Bloodfury harpies roost in skeletal snags and defend what remains of their territory. Druids from Sun Rock Retreat refuse to abandon the valley. They send travelers to sow enchanted seeds and tend the corrupted ancients as they work to reclaim the scorched earth.

subzone:chill-breeze-valley.text: Chill Breeze Valley. In western Dun Morogh, travelers cross Chill Breeze Valley between Kharanos and Gnomeregan. Refugees and young travelers follow its main trail, while dangerous beasts haunt its secluded reaches. Chill Breeze Valley cuts through the mountains of western Dun Morogh. The main trail runs east to west, carrying young dwarves and gnomes between Kharanos and the outskirts of Gnomeregan. A north-south branch leads into more dangerous ground. Blood stains the snow among mangled carcasses, and savage wendigos make their dens in deep ice caves. They prey on anyone who wanders into their hunting grounds.

subzone:clean-zone.text: Clean Zone. Gnomes hold the Clean Zone as a refuge inside ruined Gnomeregan. Beyond the upper Hall of Gears, this fortified enclave remains safe amid the irradiated city, where medics, technicians, and Sparklematic machines support the defenders and salvage work. The Clean Zone remains untainted while most of Gnomeregan fell to Mekkatorque's disastrous venting of radioactive waste. It lies between the trogg-infested Dormitory below and the contested corridors of the Hall of Gears above. Gnome defenders, technicians, and field medics hold its barricades day and night. Alliance expeditions can regroup here, tend their wounds, and maintain their machinery. The Clean Zone also supports salvage from Gnomeregan's ruined capital. Gnomish engineers installed Sparklematic 5200 units to scrub and wash grime-encrusted relics brought up from the city's radioactive depths. Technicians and merchants such as Tink Sprocketwhistle process the reclaimed gears and baubles, outfit adventurers, and study the toxic fallout in the deep tunnels.

subzone:cleft.text: Cleft. Gnarlpine furbolgs ambush travelers in the Cleft, northwest of Dolanaar. The Cleft lies off the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus, where Gnarlpine furbolgs have made their den. Teldrassil’s spreading corruption has driven them mad, and they have fortified the hollow. From there, they threaten travelers on the main road and risk cutting Dolanaar off from Darnassus.

subzone:cliffspring-falls.text: Cliffspring Falls. Cliffspring Falls pours from Darkshore’s eastern cliffs into the forest below. Its waters feed the Cliffspring River and once supplied nearby night elf settlements, but a foul taint now spreads through the river basin. Cliffspring Falls pours from caves high in Darkshore’s eastern bluffs and feeds the Cliffspring River. The river winds west through the woods before emptying into the sea. Its clear waters once gave nearby night elf settlements their purest drinking water. Now they run murky and foul, spreading sickness and decay through the river basin. Naturalists investigating the falls have found the caves overrun by naga and cultists. They plot in the shadows, while demonic corruption from neighboring Felwood threatens to seep through the highland bedrock.

subzone:coldridge-pass.text: Coldridge Pass. Troggs now bar the road through Coldridge Pass, the way out of Coldridge Valley. Coldridge Pass carries recruits from Coldridge Valley toward Kharanos. The tunnel cuts through Dun Morogh’s southern mountain ridge, linking the sheltered training grounds to the wider kingdom. Troggs have overrun the passage and threaten anyone crossing between the valley and the rest of Dun Morogh.

subzone:command-center.text: Command Center. In Stormwind's Old Town, the Command Center trains recruits while most of the army serves abroad. Also called the Stormwind Barracks, it houses the city's military officers and a seasoned skeleton crew focused on drilling recruits and local militia. In Old Town, Stormwind's Command Center is a garrison and training ground for the kingdom's soldiers. Its halls are quieter than usual, with much of the royal army committed to campaigns abroad. Veteran instructors, including Ander Germaine and martial artist Wu Shen, train fresh warriors to strengthen the city's defenses. When you ask for instruction in heavy arms or tactical combat, Stormwind's guards may point you to the Barracks. The building sits near the Pig and Whistle Tavern and the shadowy operations elsewhere in Old Town. It helps keep order in a district known for tavern brawls and roguish activity.

subzone:commons.text: Commons. Travelers and traders crowd the Commons, just inside Ironforge's gates. The district links the entrance to the mountain city's great caverns and draws merchants, travelers, and bankers from across the Alliance. The Commons greets you just northeast of the Gates of Ironforge. Carved from the mountain stone, its market street holds the Alliance Auction House, Stonefire Tavern, and the city's central bank in the Vault of Ironforge. Broad roads lead from here to the Great Forge, the Mystic Ward, and the Military Ward. Nearly everyone crossing the mountain city passes its shops. The Commons draws trade from across the Eastern Kingdoms. Ironforge's central position and the underground Deeprun Tram link to Stormwind bring travelers and merchants here. Adventurers trade goods from across Azeroth, buy weapons at Steelfury's Weapon Emporium, or purchase reagents from Barim. Some meet beneath the inn's warm lanterns before setting out into the snows of Khaz Modan.

subzone:craftsmen-s-terrace.text: Craftsmen's Terrace. Craftsmen's Terrace gathers Darnassus's trades along the city's northern edge. Its workshops, trainers, inn, and Argent Dawn embassy draw artisans and visitors alike. Woodworkers, leathercrafters, alchemists, and other artisans work along the northern edge of Darnassus. Their shops bring together many of the trades that keep the city running, using night elven methods for practical crafts. You can also find an inn, a guild master, and guild petition vendors here. Bridges lead west to the Cenarion Enclave and south to the Warrior's Terrace. The Argent Dawn keeps an embassy in the Craftsmen's Terrace, coordinating with northern allies against the Scourge. The district's workshops also hold scattered scholarly volumes. Among them are histories of the War of the Ancients, chronicles of the Second War, and treatises on the Old Gods.

subzone:cragpool-lake.text: Cragpool Lake. At Cragpool Lake, the Venture Company’s timber structure looms over the dark water in Windshear Crag. Cragpool Lake lies beneath a vast timber structure built by the Venture Company in Windshear Crag. Platforms cross above the water, where Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle watches operations across the mountain valley. Venture Company workers occupy the platforms overhead.

subzone:crystal-lake.text: Crystal Lake. East of Goldshire, Crystal Lake draws travelers toward a shore claimed by murlocs. Their attacks make the water a danger to villagers and passersby. Crystal Lake lies east of Goldshire, within walking distance of the Lion's Pride Inn. Freshwater murlocs now claim its shore and shallow shoals, attacking anyone who comes too close. William Pestle, an alchemist at the inn, hires travelers to drive them back and gather the crystal kelp they carry for his experiments.

subzone:cut-throat-alley.text: Cut-Throat Alley. Behind the canal shops, Cut-Throat Alley lies quiet and empty in Stormwind City. Reach it through the Shady Lady near the Dwarven District, where a paved courtyard ends at an unoccupied residence. Cut-Throat Alley lies in a quiet corner of Stormwind, charted with the Dwarven District but apart from its forge fires and soot. No main avenue leads here; the only footpath passes through the Shady Lady, a small canal-side shop just south of the bridge from Cathedral Square. Beyond its door, a paved dead end holds stacked crates, forgotten barrels, and one empty two-story residence. Passing guards and ordinary citizens cannot see the alley, which stays silent amid the capital.

subzone:dagger-hills.text: Dagger Hills. Bandits hold the Dagger Hills, the rocky heights behind Moonbrook in southern Westfall. With royal patrols gone, the ridge threatens travelers and the plains below. The Dagger Hills rise above Moonbrook in southern Westfall, where Defias outlaws watch the rocky ridges. Stormwind's royal patrols are gone, leaving the dry highland as a natural stronghold for the Defias Brotherhood. Knuckledusters, pathstalkers, and highwaymen hide among the crests and scrub. They ambush travelers and watch the approaches to their strongholds below. Darkness brings its own danger to the Dagger Hills. Leprithus, a wandering ghoul, has been seen stalking the desolate heights after sunset. Outlaws and lingering undead roam the ridge, while Grimbooze Thunderbrew, a dwarven brewer, sets up his distilling equipment in the rugged wilderness despite the dangers nearby.

subzone:darkcloud-pinnacle.text: Darkcloud Pinnacle. Darkcloud Pinnacle is a fortified tauren settlement perched atop several interconnected mesas east of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles. Held by the aggressive Grimtotem clan, the aerial stronghold serves as a base of operations for regional disruption and shady dealings. Spanning three main mesas joined by rope bridges, Darkcloud Pinnacle commands the canyon basin below. The heights are accessible only by a steep natural slope leading from the canyon floor across wooden bridges, or via a high crossing near Razorfen Downs. From these windswept rocks, the Grimtotem watch the valley, safe from casual assault and isolated from the broader tauren tribes.

subzone:darkened-bank.text: Darkened Bank. At Duskwood’s northern edge, Darkened Bank follows the river beside Elwynn Forest. Its shore runs east toward the Redridge Mountains, between the safer north and the forest’s terrors. Darkened Bank follows the river that separates Duskwood from Elwynn Forest. The shore runs from western river bends east toward the stone span leading to the Redridge Mountains. Under Duskwood’s gloomy canopy, it is often the first ground travelers reach when coming south from Elwynn. Near its western tip, a makeshift camp shelters displaced refugees Sven Yorgen and Lars, just beyond the deep woods.

subzone:darkshire.text: Darkshire. In Darkshire, the Night Watch holds the line as the town endures Duskwood's unnatural gloom. Stormwind offers little aid, leaving the people to guard their homes. Darkshire was once the peaceful woodland settlement of Grand Hamlet. The Old Horde razed it during the First War, and the village was rebuilt. After Medivh fell at Karazhan, the death throes left in the surrounding woods turned them into the shadowed wilderness of Duskwood. Though Darkshire belongs to the Kingdom of Stormwind, the crown sends virtually no aid to its town hall. Political paralysis in Stormwind City has left the garrison unstaffed and the borders unpatrolled. Mayor Ello Ebonlocke and the local council are left to govern on their own, enforcing harsh, insular justice in the shadows. Walking dead from the western graveyards and feral worgen in the woods press against Darkshire's palisades. The Night Watch, a voluntary civilian militia led by Althea Ebonlocke, is the town's chief defense. From the town square, its weary sentries patrol the pitch-black roads, keep them open, and turn back terrors at the tree line. Travelers at the Scarlet Raven Tavern meet locals who are suspicious, frightened, and desperate for anyone able to wield a blade.

subzone:darkshire-town-hall.text: Darkshire Town Hall. Darkshire Town Hall anchors a town besieged by darkness and undead. Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke and his council govern from its dim halls. Darkshire Town Hall stands just west of the main square, where the town's leaders meet to govern an increasingly isolated territory. Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke struggles to keep order and protect the people while Stormwind sends little military aid. Clerk Daltry and other officials track town records and the travelers who brave Duskwood's dangerous roads. With danger all around, keeping those ledgers current is a grim task.

subzone:dawning-wood-catacombs.text: Dawning Wood Catacombs. Undead fill the Dawning Wood Catacombs beneath Raven Hill Cemetery in western Duskwood. Their stone tunnels hold skeletal guards and ravenous ghouls. The Dawning Wood Catacombs lie beneath the ruined Raven Hill Cemetery. Before the twilight curse came over the forest, the dead of the surrounding woods rested in these stone corridors. Now the catacombs hold some of the region’s deadliest undead, and their depths are dangerous for lone travelers. Two subterranean wings divide the catacombs. Ranks of animated skeletons guard ancestral tombs in the western passages. To the east, the tunnels descend into a foul warren overrun by ravenous, disease-bearing ghouls.

subzone:dead-acre.text: Dead Acre. The Dead Acre lies burned and abandoned in southeastern Westfall, near the bridge to Duskwood. The Defias Brotherhood torched the farm during their uprising, and rogue harvest golems now stalk its blackened fields. You find the Dead Acre just north of the road from Sentinel Hill to Duskwood. Once a productive homestead among Westfall’s breadbasket farms, it met a violent end when the Defias Brotherhood rose in revolt and drove out the local landowners. The farm and its crops went up in flames. Scorched timber and smoking earth remain, while mechanical Harvest Watchers still reap the barren soil.

subzone:deeprun-tram.text: Deeprun Tram. The Deeprun Tram carries travelers beneath the earth between Ironforge and Stormwind City. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned it after the Second War, and its twin tracks now carry citizens, soldiers, and goods between the Alliance capitals. King Magni Bronzebeard wanted dwarven aid and supplies to reach Stormwind faster after the Second War. Mountain passes slowed the journey, so he asked High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to design an underground railway. Gnomish engineers cut the route beneath a mountain and through a vast subterranean lake. Rats plagued the excavation, but the tram was completed. It carries thousands of travelers between Ironforge and Stormwind without charge.

subzone:deepwater-tavern.text: Deepwater Tavern. At Menethil Harbor, the Deepwater Tavern gives travelers a place to rest and find work. The inn is a meeting spot and resupply stop, where harbor rumors mingle with the chance of a brawl. In Menethil Harbor, the Deepwater Tavern shelters travelers from the marsh's rain and difficult roads. Sailors, dockworkers, merchants, and weary adventurers gather beneath its timber beams to trade news, meet, warm themselves, and patch their wounds. Local merchants and a resident first aid trainer serve those bound for the marsh or setting out across the Great Sea. The tavern is lively, and disputes over spilled ale can turn into brawls. Tapoke 'Slim' Jahn is known to spark them.

subzone:defias-hideout.text: Defias Hideout. Defias thugs and vagrants linger in a ruined house on Moonbrook’s southern edge. Its upper floor hides a route into the chambers beneath the town.

subzone:demon-fall-canyon.text: Demon Fall Canyon. Demon Fall Canyon bears the scars of the battle that freed the orcs from the blood curse. Here, Thrall and Grommash Hellscream faced Mannoroth in southern Ashenvale. In southern Ashenvale, the canyon lies near Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Ridge, its land scarred by the Third War. Warchief Thrall and chieftain Grommash Hellscream tracked the pit lord Mannoroth here to break his hold over the Horde. Mannoroth struck Thrall down, and Grom seized the chance to drive his axe, Gorehowl, into the demon’s chest. The infernal blast shattered Mannoroth and killed Grom. With the pit lord’s death, the orcs were free of their lingering demonic servitude. The Horde named the canyon for Grom’s final stand and raised a monument nearby to honor his redemption. Mannoroth’s death unleashed demonic power that tainted the surrounding land. Fel magic still saturates the canyon, where lesser demons roam. Pilgrims who come to this hallowed ground face danger at every turn.

subzone:demon-fall-ridge.text: Demon Fall Ridge. In southeastern Ashenvale, demons hold the high ground above the place where Mannoroth fell. Lingering fel magic stains the ridge, and the Burning Legion has claimed a night elf barrow den. Demon Fall Ridge rises west of Demon Fall Canyon, its cliffs stained by fel left from the Third War. Below, the canyon marks the clash between Grommash Hellscream and the pit lord Mannoroth. Surviving demons use the ridge as a staging ground. Lesser demons patrol the rocky heights, defiling the woodland and threatening travelers along Ashenvale's southern border. A night elf barrow den lies abandoned in the ridge's side, its passages turned into a stronghold of dark sorcery. Fel fiends fill the halls where druids once slept. In the deepest reaches, Diathorus the Seeker, a cunning dreadlord, rules the conclave and directs the remaining demons across the forest.

subzone:demont-s-place.text: Demont's Place. Outlaws hold Demont's Place, a ruined farm west of Moonbrook in southwestern Westfall. The farm once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind, but economic collapse and the Defias Brotherhood drove its caretakers away. Its fields remain empty and its fences weathered. Demont's Place lies within sight of Moonbrook, among the family holdings that once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Economic collapse and outlaw brigands stripped the farm of its livelihood and drove out its caretakers. Like the neighboring fields, it has fallen into a rough hideout, where outlaws use its grounds as an extension of the Defias stronghold in Moonbrook. Demont's Place is an outpost for the Defias Brotherhood on the outskirts of Moonbrook. Thugs, cutpurses, and displaced laborers linger among its fences and shattered buildings, ambushing travelers who stray from the southern roads. Until Moonbrook is reclaimed and the outlaws are broken, the farm remains too dangerous for peaceful farming to return.

subzone:dolanaar.text: Dolanaar. Dolanaar gathers travelers and guides beneath Teldrassil’s boughs. Southwest of Shadowglen, the town is the first place young night elves find after leaving their sheltered training grounds. Rangers, druids, and craftsmen help newcomers while strange afflictions spread through the World Tree. Dolanaar is a crossroads for travelers crossing Teldrassil. Beneath the canopy southwest of Shadowglen, its homes and platforms follow the traditional night elven way, woven into the woodland. Young night elves come here for their first broad training in trades, martial arts, and nature crafts. The road west leads toward Darnassus, the capital. From the surrounding boughs come reports of corrupted wildlife, aggressive furbolgs, and foul mosses, all brought before Dolanaar’s council.

subzone:dor-danil-barrow-den.text: Dor'Danil Barrow Den. In central Ashenvale, south of Splintertree Post, Dor'Danil Barrow Den lies under Forsaken shadow. Druids once slept here while their spirits roamed the Emerald Dream, but now the sanctuary is filled with horror. Night elven druids have slept for centuries in barrow dens across Kalimdor, their bodies sheltered underground as their spirits traveled the Emerald Dream. When the Horde pushed into Ashenvale, Dor'Danil lay deep behind enemy lines. The orcs mostly left the sleeping elves alone, but the newly allied Forsaken saw an opportunity. Their agents entered the depths and began experiments to sever the druids from their spirits. The ordeal fractured the dreamers' minds and drove them mad. Now sinister Forsaken assassins prowl the dark hollows, alongside the tormented spirits of druids who cannot return to their bodies.

subzone:dormitory.text: Dormitory. In Gnomeregan, the Dormitory lies overrun by troggs and choked with radiation. Gnomes once lived here, but the fallen city's residential halls now belong to the creatures that drove them out. Past the decontamination chambers of the Clean Zone, the Dormitory once housed Gnomeregan's inventors, laborers, and families. When High Tinker Mekkatorque opened the emergency radiation vents to fight the invading troggs, this crowded sector became a trap. No gnomish life remains in its communal halls or living quarters. Mutated troggs now thrive in the radioactive air. Travelers heading deeper through the city must fight through this reminder of the catastrophe to reach the lower Hall of Gears. The abandoned living quarters still hold working machines from Gnomeregan's administration. Matrix Punchograph 3005-B terminals process security punch cards. Their cards grant access to higher-security data terminals deeper in the city, helping recover important records left behind when the gnomes fled.

subzone:dun-algaz.text: Dun Algaz. Dragonmaw orcs have laid siege to Dun Algaz, cutting easy passage between Ironforge’s lands and Menethil Harbor. The fortified pass and its tunnels link Loch Modan with the Wetlands. Dun Algaz cuts through the jagged peaks between Loch Modan and the Wetlands. The pass predates the War of the Three Hammers. After the Wildhammer clan was driven from Ironforge, its people used this route to migrate north. Stone tunnels, bastions, and watchposts guard the way. Whoever holds Dun Algaz controls the only overland road from the dwarven heartlands to Menethil Harbor on the western sea. During the Second War, the Old Horde retreated to Dun Algaz after its defeat at Dun Modr. The pass became its final southern bulwark against Sir Anduin Lothar’s forces. The Alliance reclaimed it for a time, but Dragonmaw orcs have overrun the stronghold again. Dwarven Mountaineers have fallen back to the upper tunnels, leaving the mountain corridor a deadly gauntlet for travelers.

subzone:dun-garok.text: Dun Garok. Dun Garok guards the southeastern heights of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Captain Ironhill commands its dwarven garrison, which defends Alliance interests and nearby operations such as the Azurelode Mine. To the Forsaken of Tarren Mill, the stronghold is a military threat on their border. Dun Garok holds the crags in the southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills. Captain Ironhill commands the Ironforge mountaineers and riflemen who defend the outpost. They guard human settlements in Hillsbrad and protect Alliance operations at the Azurelode Mine. Stone walls and deep entrenchments help the garrison hold against nearby threats. Dun Garok lies close to Tarren Mill, and the Forsaken see it as an intrusion on their southern border. Sylvanas Windrunner's forces resent the armed dwarven troops near their stronghold. They plot to enter the fortress, break its defenses, and kill Captain Ironhill's garrison to secure Forsaken control of Hillsbrad.

subzone:dun-modr.text: Dun Modr. Dun Modr has fallen to Dark Iron dwarves, leaving the Thandol Span's southern approach in hostile hands. The fortress once changed hands in a fierce struggle during the Second War. At Wetlands' northern edge, Dun Modr commands the main road between Khaz Modan and the northern human kingdoms. That route has drawn armies to the fortress across the decades. During the Second War, the Orcish Horde seized the dwarven stronghold and used it to launch raids and resist Alliance armies. Stromgarde warriors sailed from Tol Barad to reclaim it, and the Orcs struck back in a bloody struggle. Alliance forces under Lord Anduin Lothar eventually drove the invaders south across the Thandol Span, returning the fortress to dwarven hands. Dun Modr lay exposed while Ironforge's attention was divided and many of its finest mountaineers served the Alliance abroad. Dark Iron invaders took advantage, sabotaged the Thandol Span with explosives, then swarmed the fortress. Led by the warlock Balgaras the Foul, they overcame the defenders and drove out the Bronzebeard garrison. Mountaineers now hold a grim perimeter just down the road, seeking aid to drive out the occupiers.

subzone:durnholde-keep.text: Durnholde Keep. Outlaws hold Durnholde Keep, a shattered fortress east of Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Once the Alliance headquarters for the southern orc internment camps, it is now a Syndicate refuge. After the Second War, the Alliance made Durnholde Keep its headquarters for the southern internment camps. Lieutenant General Aedelas Blackmoore commanded the fortress and its arena, where orcs fought for sport and profit. Blackmoore raised the orphaned infant Go'el as a slave, named him Thrall, and trained him to fight. With Taretha Foxton's aid, Thrall escaped captivity and later united the scattered orc clans beneath the new Horde. He returned to Durnholde, besieged the keep, slew Blackmoore, and called on the earth spirits to shatter its walls. Durnholde Keep has lain in ruins since its collapse before the Third War. After Lordaeron fell, the Syndicate took refuge among its broken ramparts. These bandits are dispossessed Alterac nobles and cutthroats. From the ruined bailey and towers, they prey on travelers across the Hillsbrad Foothills, using the old fortress as a fortified outpost.

subzone:dust-plains.text: Dust Plains. Gnoll packs hold the Dust Plains, Westfall’s dry southern frontier. The plains stretch toward the coast and eastern hills, where Klaven’s Tower overlooks the wastes. Across southern Westfall, the Dust Plains run from troubled farmland toward desolate wilderness. Feral gnolls have long claimed this arid ground, ambushing travelers and challenging anyone bound for the coast or nearby hills. Klaven’s Tower stands on the eastern boundary. The old mage tower is held by Klaven Mortwake, a Defias rogue, and offers no shelter from the gnolls prowling the surrounding wastes.

subzone:dwarven-district.text: Dwarven District. Dwarven craftsmen keep their furnaces and workshops working in Stormwind's northern quarter. The district brings a piece of Khaz Modan to the human capital, with the Deeprun Tram linking it to Ironforge. Dwarven artisans, smiths, and engineers make their home in Stormwind's northern quarter. Heavy stonework, smelting works, and craft shops recall Ironforge. At Potts' Plates, craftspeople from Khaz Modan find familiar company. On the district's eastern side, an open, arched tunnel leads to the Stormwind station of the Deeprun Tram, linking the human capital directly to Ironforge.

subzone:eastvale-logging-camp.text: Eastvale Logging Camp. At Eastvale Logging Camp, timber orders from Stormwind meet the dangers of Elwynn’s eastern woods. Wolves and bears drive lumberjacks from their work, while the camp keeps timber moving toward Stormwind and nearby settlements. Timber buyers across the Kingdom of Stormwind send orders to Eastvale Logging Camp, each with a strict deadline. Wolves and bears prowl the woods around the work sites, driving lumberjacks away and leaving cut timber behind. Supervisor Raelen directs the camp’s work, and travelers help drive off the beasts and recover the abandoned wood before deliveries fall behind schedule. Eastvale Logging Camp has homes and horse stables where travelers can buy fine mounts. On a nearby hill above the work site, retired Marshal Haggard lives in a quiet manor. He once led the Stormwind Guard and left its service to retire far from the politics of the capital.

subzone:echo-ridge-mine.text: Echo Ridge Mine. In Northshire Valley's northwestern cliffs, Echo Ridge Mine lies rich in stone and ore, but kobolds have seized it. Echo Ridge Mine was cut into the hills above Northshire Abbey to supply the valley with stone and metal. Kobolds poured through its tunnels and drove out the workers. Marshal McBride sees them as a danger to Northshire's safety and its recruits. He sends new recruits into the mine to thin their numbers and take the site back. Kobolds have been pushing into Elwynn Forest beyond Echo Ridge Mine. From the northwestern ridge, they threaten Northshire's training grounds and the flow of resources to the abbey.

subzone:engineering-labs.text: Engineering Labs. Deep within Gnomeregan, the Engineering Labs lie in ruin, their tiers linked to the Workshop Entrance and Launch Bay. Once a busy center of gnome innovation, they were overrun in the city's radioactive cataclysm. Crazed leper gnomes and rogue mechanical contraptions now fill the chambers. The Engineering Labs were once a busy center of gnome innovation. Built around a central mechanical structure, they span two main tiers joined by a central cargo lift. At Gnomeregan's height, tinkerers developed schematics and refined clockwork inventions here. Radiation drove the remaining researchers mad, turning them into deranged leper gnomes who mindlessly guard malfunctioning machinery alongside rogue constructs. The Engineering Labs also link routes through the lower reaches of the ruined city. Passages lead toward the Launch Bay, Tinkers' Court, and the Workshop Entrance back door. On the lower floor, Matrix Punchograph 3005-D terminals process coded punch cards carried by gnome engineers.

subzone:falfarren-river.text: Falfarren River. The Falfarren River cuts through central Ashenvale, from Mount Hyjal toward the northern mountains of the Barrens. Its banks mark the divide between night elven lands and Horde outposts, where travelers face wild dangers and open conflict. The Falfarren River descends from Mount Hyjal, spilling over waterfalls into Xavian before winding between Splintertree Post and Night Run. In ordinary weather, its waters are neither especially deep nor impassable. The river marks a rough boundary through central Ashenvale. Astranaar and the heart of the Kaldorei lands lie west; Horde camps and lumber operations lie east. The wooden bridges on the main road carry travelers into the contested forest, where patrols clash along the banks. The Falfarren River holds dangers beyond clashes between sentinels and grunts. Near Felfire Hill, corrupted bog beasts and aggressive water creatures prowl the muddy shallows. Rain can swell the currents. Dense canopies line both shores, where ambushes and skirmishes often spill into the stream.

subzone:fallen-sky-lake.text: Fallen Sky Lake. In eastern Ashenvale, Fallen Sky Lake lies between Silverwing Outpost and the Warsong Labor Camp. Shadethickets defend its shores and central isle. Fallen Sky Lake lies south of Silverwing Outpost and west of the Warsong Labor Camp. Shadethickets, hulking bog beasts, roam its shores and the small isle at its center, treating intruders as threats. A powerful Shadethicket Oracle rules from the isle's heart. The Oracle hoards the fallen moonstones once gathered at the lake and keeps the shadethickets bound to the waters, ever watchful for travelers.

subzone:fargodeep-mine.text: Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds now swarm through Fargodeep Mine, south of Goldshire in central Elwynn Forest. The mine once brought gold to Stormwind, but its tunnels are now a kobold warren. Gold once flowed from Fargodeep Mine into Stormwind's treasury. As the Kingdom's military presence in Elwynn dwindled, outlying resources became vulnerable. Kobolds soon filled the mine's dark tunnels and made a warren beneath the hills. Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's authorities fear the lost ore and the danger to nearby farms, including the Stonefield and Maclure holdings. Fargodeep Mine runs through several levels, with lower shafts reaching deep beneath the forest floor. Kobold laborers and vermin hurry along wooden scaffolds, guarding the wax and gold dust they have scavenged. Goldtooth, a cunning kobold leader, lurks in a den above the main tunnels. He hoards trinkets stolen from travelers and nearby residents.

subzone:farstrider-lodge.text: Farstrider Lodge. Hunters and travelers come to Farstrider Lodge in southeastern Loch Modan for training, supplies, and work in the wilds. Its high elven style sets it apart, though dwarves and humans live there too. Farstrider Lodge has an unusual look among the stone buildings of Khaz Modan. Its design suggests high elven craft. Vyrin Swiftwind is the only known high elf who still lives there, among dwarves and humans. No one knows who founded the lodge or when it was built. In the southeastern hills of Loch Modan, Farstrider Lodge offers a stopping place for hunters and travelers bound for the surrounding wilds. Hunter and pet trainers work there, alongside merchants and people seeking help with local wildlife.

subzone:fel-rock.text: Fel Rock. North of Dolanaar, Fel Rock has fallen under a spreading corruption. Lord Melenas and his grells have turned the once-tranquil cavern into a threat within Teldrassil’s woods. North of Dolanaar, Fel Rock lies among Teldrassil’s forested hills. Once a peaceful cavern in wood and stone, it is now overtaken by twisted roots, unnatural shadows, wild grells and grellkin. The taint reaches into the world tree’s boughs. Lord Melenas, a satyr, has claimed Fel Rock as his stronghold. From within the cavern, he spreads corruption beneath the watch of the night elf sentinels. Druids in Dolanaar, including Tallonkai Swiftroot, seek defenders to cleanse the cave and slay Melenas before the blight reaches farther into the surrounding woodlands.

subzone:felfire-hill.text: Felfire Hill. In eastern Ashenvale, Felfire Hill remains a blighted rise crawling with demons. Infernals struck it during the Third War, and its soil still burns with fel power. Horde guards hold the bridges leading to the hill, near their settlements. During the Third War, the Burning Legion sent flaming meteors across Kalimdor, carrying its fearsome infernals. Several struck this ridge in Ashenvale, burning away the ancient woodland and corrupting the earth. The Legion fell at Mount Hyjal, but demons that survived its defeat still prowl the scorched slopes. Fel energy saturates the land they haunt. Felfire Hill lies southeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of the Warsong Lumber Camp, close to vital Horde operations. Demonic remnants threaten to spill into the surrounding forest. Horde forces have raised fortified barricades and guard towers at both bridges leading to the hill, keeping the creatures within their blighted haven.

subzone:fire-scar-shrine.text: Fire Scar Shrine. At Fire Scar Shrine, fel corruption scars the forest southwest of Astranaar. Once a night elf place of worship, the shrine now draws demons to its altar stones. Fire Scar Shrine lies southwest of Astranaar and west of the Ruins of Stardust. Demonic corruption has seized the shrine, fed by servants of the Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council. Fel magic has scorched the earth around it, and demons gather openly among the trees, defying the forest's defenders. Agents of the Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council brought corruption to Fire Scar Shrine. The orc warlock Ilkrud Magthrull acted under Athrikus Narassin's orders. Summoned fiends now patrol the altar stones unchecked. A tear in the veil sometimes draws greater horrors, including the towering doomguard Akkrilus.

subzone:forest-s-edge.text: Forest's Edge. Riverpaw gnolls under Hogger threaten travelers at Forest's Edge, along Elwynn's southwestern frontier. At Forest's Edge, woodland runs southwest from Stormwind City between Mirror Lake Orchard and the rivers that border Westfall. Westbrook Garrison lies nearby, but Stormwind's thin ranks leave the woods open to wild beasts and raiding parties. Boars roam among the trees and along the banks. Riverpaw gnolls gather here in force, using the woods as a staging ground. Hogger and his pack hunt through the woods of Forest's Edge. A massive, brutal gnoll chieftain, he leads raids on nearby farms and harasses travelers. The Stormwind Army has placed a bounty on his head. His pack makes the timberland dangerous for anyone who crosses it.

subzone:forest-song.text: Forest Song. Forest Song watches over northeastern Ashenvale, near Satyrnaar and Bough Shadow. The ancient kaldorei ruins are largely deserted, with the druid Kayneth Stillwind guarding the eastern border. Forest Song's white columns and broken arches rise among the trees of northeastern Ashenvale. Once an elegant kaldorei settlement, the ruin now lies overgrown with ivy and wild ferns. Satyrnaar lies to the southwest, and the Warsong Lumber Camp presses in from the south. From here, eastern trails lead toward Azshara and Bough Shadow. Demonic corruption and Horde incursions trouble the surrounding woods, while the ruins remain quiet. Kayneth Stillwind keeps watch over Forest Song alone. From the crumbling outpost, the druid watches for enemies entering the wilderness, including the Forsaken in the eastern forests. Astranaar lies far away, and Forest Song has no garrison fortifications. Still, Alliance travelers heading north toward Felwood or seeking the corruption spreading through the canopy can gather here.

subzone:forlorn-cavern.text: Forlorn Cavern. Along Ironforge's northern underground lake, the Forlorn Cavern shelters those who keep to the shadows. Thieves, cutpurses, and practitioners of the dark arts conduct business there, far from the Great Forge and prying dwarven guards. The Forlorn Cavern is cold, damp, and hushed beneath Ironforge's clang of anvils and the Great Forge's heat. Its winding paths follow the northern edge of the underground lake, out of sight between the Mystic Ward and the Hall of Explorers. Rogues and warlocks train there, and vendors serve them. Weapon merchants and fishermen work beside the lake as well.

subzone:forlorn-rowe.text: Forlorn Rowe. At the northern edge of Raven Hill Cemetery, Forlorn Rowe lies under a shadow of dread. Morbent Fel makes his home on the hill, and his magic raises the restless dead across Duskwood. Forlorn Rowe rises along the northern edge of Raven Hill Cemetery, its slope lost in gloom. Morbent Fel makes his home atop the hill. The necromancer is responsible for much of the walking dead that haunt the surrounding wilderness. From this height, he directs his skeletal servants with foul enchantments, making Duskwood’s northwestern corner perilous for travelers.

subzone:freewind-post.text: Freewind Post. Freewind Post is the primary Horde outpost in Thousand Needles, perched high atop one of the canyon's dramatic stone mesas. Accessible primarily by tauren lift and winding rope bridges, it serves as a defensive refuge against centaur warbands and a vital frontier staging ground. Built directly upon the canyon mesas, Freewind Post relies on ingenuity and height to safeguard its people. The Galak centaur dominate the arid canyon floor below, but they cannot effectively scale the towering cliffs or breach the heavy wooden elevators that haul Horde travelers up into the sky. A labyrinth of rope and plank bridges connects Freewind to neighboring spires, forming a secure aerie. Beyond keeping centaur raiding parties at bay, the outpost also helps manage the screeching harpies nesting along the bluffs and tends to the nearby wyvern grounds at Highperch, where wild eggs are culled and trained as loyal wind rider mounts for the Horde.

subzone:frostmane-hold.text: Frostmane Hold. Frostmane trolls hold the cliffs south of Gnomeregan in western Dun Morogh. The Ironforge Guard watches their camp and caverns as raiders press into dwarven lands. Frostmane Hold cuts into the cold cliffs of western Dun Morogh. Rough structures stand outside its winding caves, where hideskinners and headhunters guard the tribe's stronghold. Frostmane raiders leave from here to strike the valleys, threaten travelers on the mountain passes, and test the defenses around Kharanos. Dwarven commanders in Kharanos fear the Frostmane buildup. Young mountaineers and adventurers scout the caverns, map their defenses, and thin the warbands before the tribe can gather for an organized assault on dwarven outposts.

subzone:frostmane-hovel.text: Frostmane Hovel. Frostmane Hovel is a rugged cave den tucked into the southern crags of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. It serves as an entrenched shelter for aggressive Frostmane trolls pressing directly into dwarven training grounds. Carved into the southern mountains flanking Coldridge Valley, the Frostmane Hovel shelters indigenous Frostmane trolls who refuse to yield the high snows to Ironforge. Operating out of crude caverns like this, the trolls mount continuous raids against local dwarven camps and disrupt supply lines into the valley.
