subzone:furlbrow-s-pumpkin-farm.text: Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm. Bandits and harvest golems hold Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm in northern Westfall, off the road from Elwynn Forest. Farmer Furlbrow and Verna have lost their home to the Defias Brotherhood. Near Westfall's northern border, Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm once grew crops to feed the kingdom. The Defias Brotherhood drove Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna from their land. Mechanical harvest golems now roam the fields, attacking anyone who approaches. Bandits occupy the farm buildings, while the rightful owners camp beside the road near the Jansen Stead, mourning their lost home and livelihood. The Defias Brotherhood has claimed homesteads like Furlbrow's as Stormwind's military garrison struggles to protect Westfall's rural farmers. Bandits camp at the farm and use it as a staging ground. Lethal harvest watchers guard the perimeter, leaving travelers on the nearby highway vulnerable to ambush.

subzone:galardell-valley.text: Galardell Valley. Gnolls prowl Galardell Valley beneath the Tower of Ilgalar in northeastern Redridge. The canyon is a danger to the settlements nearby. Redridge gnolls prowl Galardell Valley, beyond the reach of Lakeshire's defenders. They roam the lowlands and camp along the canyon floor under brutal pack leaders such as Lieutenant Fangore. Above the ravines rises the Tower of Ilgalar, stronghold of the renegade mage Morganth. The gnolls and the tower keep the valley a source of dread for nearby settlements.

subzone:gates-of-ironforge.text: Gates of Ironforge. Travelers climb from Dun Morogh to the Gates of Ironforge, where a stone king guards the way into the dwarven capital. The gates open in the mountain face, with High King Modimus Anvilmar's statue just inside. The Gates of Ironforge rise above the snowy lowlands at the end of a winding, fortified ramp from central Dun Morogh. Beyond the massive portal, you enter the city proper beneath an enormous stone likeness of High King Modimus Anvilmar. He united the dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. The passage opens directly into the Commons, where Ironforge's trade and banking are centered.

subzone:goblin-foundry.text: Goblin Foundry. In the Deadmines, goblins keep the Goblin Foundry working for the Defias Brotherhood. Gilnid oversees craftsmen and engineers around a great smelting cauldron. Deep beneath Moonbrook, goblin craftsmen and engineers work at the Goblin Foundry for the Defias Brotherhood. Smelters and iron ramps fill the chamber as they make anchors and cannonballs. Gilnid oversees the goblin workforce at the foundry. Craftsmen keep production moving, while engineers use remote-controlled golems to defend the workshop. Narrow ramps and molten metal make the chamber dangerous for intruders.

subzone:gol-bolar-quarry.text: Gol'Bolar Quarry. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, troggs have driven the miners from their work in the snowy hills of southeastern Dun Morogh. The Ironforge dwarves came for stone and ore, but the excavation has fallen silent. Gol'Bolar Quarry lies southeast of Kharanos, where Ironforge dwarves came to draw stone and minerals from the mountains. Deep digging opened underground warrens, and hostile troggs drove the miners out. Now the upper camp is a staging ground under siege. Overseers, tradesfolk, and Prospector Gehn gather dwarven and gnomish recruits there to drive back the beasts and reclaim the pit.

subzone:gol-bolar-quarry-mine.text: Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine. Troggs hold Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine, deep beneath Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. Ironforge dwarves once worked its tunnels for stone and rich ore, until they broke into trogg caverns and the creatures overran the site. Hammerspine leads the warband in the deepest shafts. Ironforge dwarves once mined stone and rich ore beneath Dun Morogh's craggy peaks. Their work ended when pickaxes broke through a wall into caverns inhabited by troggs. The creatures poured from the darkness, overwhelmed the crews, and drove them from the mine. Troggs then spread across the surrounding quarry pit. Younger, weaker troggs roam the quarry's sunlit terraces, while the mine shelters the warband's fiercest fighters. Hammerspine, their vicious chieftain, lurks deep in the cramped tunnels. Local mountaineers still need to reclaim the valuable quarry, but that means entering the mine's deepest reaches and cutting off the troggs at their source.

subzone:gold-coast-quarry.text: Gold Coast Quarry. In southwestern Westfall, the Gold Coast Quarry has fallen to the Defias Brotherhood. The mine once supplied Stormwind with stone, minerals, and gold; now the Brotherhood draws on its remaining resources for its insurrection. The Gold Coast Quarry once supplied Stormwind with stone and gold for the kingdom's rebuilding. After royal troops withdrew from Westfall, Defias highwaymen and renegade laborers seized the mine. Brotherhood patrols watch from its terraced ramps, which overlook the coast, and take what minerals remain to fund their rebellion.

subzone:goldshire.text: Goldshire. Goldshire sits where Elwynn’s roads meet, linking Stormwind City with Westfall, Redridge, and the southern frontier. Rebuilt after the First War, the town now offers travelers the Lion’s Pride Inn, while a hard-pressed Stormwind Guard defends it. Goldshire stands where the king’s highways meet, the civic and commercial heart of rural Elwynn. Threats press closer as Stormwind’s forces stretch thin and King Varian Wrynn remains mysteriously absent. Marshal Dughan relies on passing adventurers instead of regular troops to hold the surrounding borders. Riverpaw gnolls push in from the west, while hostile murlocs claim the shores of Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake. Their attacks have killed royal guards and brought danger close to the town center. Goldshire and Moonbrook were the last strongholds to fall in the First War. Warchief Blackhand cut King Llane Wrynn I off from his realm before sacking Stormwind Keep, and the Orcish Horde overwhelmed both towns. Goldshire was reduced to ash and lay barren until its rebuilding after the Second War.

subzone:grand-vestibule.text: Grand Vestibule. The Grand Vestibule is the monumental entrance hall of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Lined with crimson pillars and stone effigies of fallen crusaders, it serves as the threshold where adventurers prepare to breach the monastery's inner halls. Past the heavy outer gates of the Monastery lies the Grand Vestibule, an expansive marble hall dedicated to the martial pride of the Scarlet Crusade. Statues of armored champions stand vigil beside vaulted stone pillars, and zealous sentries, disciples, and augurs patrol the flagstones to strike down anyone daring to enter without the order's crimson tabard. For trespassers, it is the first taste of the Crusade's unrelenting discipline and fanaticism. Because the vestibule sits directly outside the secured inner wings of the monastery, it is the first chamber any intruder must cross. Champions of the Alliance sent north and Horde forces pushing out from the nearby Undercity alike must fight past the Crusade's defenders under these high arches before anyone breaches the inner cloisters.

subzone:great-forge.text: Great Forge. At Ironforge’s center, the Great Forge burns as the heart of the dwarven capital. Its furnaces and Great Anvil keep smiths at work, while the chamber draws people from across the mountain city. The Great Forge was the first structure the early dwarves built beneath Ironforge Mountain. The capital grew in rings around it. Molten stone and slag flow from giant foundries into glowing channels, lighting the cavern with amber haze. At the center, Master of the Forge Myolor Sunderfury oversees the massive Great Anvil. Masters of metalwork gather around its rim, hammering armor, tools, and weapons day and night. Smithing is only part of the Great Forge’s work. Guild offices, supply shops, and the city’s main gryphon roost ring the chamber. Gryth Thurden maintains the roost, where travelers from across the Alliance mingle amid the hammer blows.

subzone:great-lift.text: Great Lift. The Great Lift is a massive, tauren-engineered elevator system perched on the southern edge of the Barrens. It serves as the primary route lowering travelers and supplies hundreds of feet into the sheer canyon basin of Thousand Needles. Despite its strategic value, aggressive quilboar encroaching through the southern wastes have made approaching the rim increasingly perilous. Spanning the sheer cliff edge between the southern Barrens and the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, the Great Lift stands as a marvel of practical tauren construction. Built using heavy timber, braided rope, and counterweighted pulleys, its paired platforms carry caravans, couriers, and warriors safely across a vertical precipice that would otherwise break any wagon. At the top and bottom platforms, tauren like Brave Moonhorn and Grish Longrunner maintain watch, keeping travelers informed of the road ahead and ensuring cargo passes smoothly. Operating the lift has become increasingly hazardous due to the hostile territory above it. Aggressive quilboar tribes in the southern Barrens have expanded aggressively southward, choking the road toward the lift and threatening to cut off Thousand Needles from the northern trails entirely. Those who make the long journey south must constantly fend off razorfen raiders before they can ever step foot onto the wooden platforms.

subzone:greatwood-vale.text: Greatwood Vale. The Grimtotem have seized Greatwood Vale in the eastern foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains. The perilous Webwinder Path leads into the forested valley, which the tribe now uses to launch bloody assaults on nearby settlements. Greatwood Vale has become a violent frontier off the Webwinder Path. Grundig Darkcloud leads the Grimtotem who have moved into the vale in force. They block safe passage and terrorize the surrounding foothills. From Greatwood Vale, Grimtotem raiders swept into nearby Camp Aparaje and slaughtered nearly every tauren there. Makaba Flathoof escaped the attack. Now she directs vengeful Horde warriors into the heart of the vale to kill the renegade Grimtotem and end Grundig Darkcloud's rule.

subzone:greenpaw-village.text: Greenpaw Village. Greenpaw Village lies between Raynewood Retreat and Silverwind Refuge, where the Foulweald furbolgs remain hostile. Chief Murgut and Shaman Oakpaw lead the corrupted tribe, and Alliance and Horde forces clash with them in Ashenvale. Greenpaw Village lies south of Raynewood Retreat and northeast of Silverwind Refuge. Since the Third War, the Foulweald furbolgs who live there have fallen to the corruption tainting Ashenvale’s soil and spirits. Chief Murgut leads them, with Shaman Oakpaw as their corrupted spiritual guide. The tribe attacks travelers who enter its forest territory. The Foulweald’s attacks draw fighting from every side of Greenpaw Village. Alliance sentinels and night elf druids seek to purge the furbolgs to protect nearby outposts and sacred moonwells. Horde forces advancing through Ashenvale also clash with them as both factions press through the woodland.

subzone:grim-batol.text: Grim Batol. Grim Batol's gates remain sealed above the eastern Wetlands. The Wildhammer dwarves abandoned the fortress after a curse during the War of the Three Hammers, and the Dragonmaw orcs later used it as a dragon-breeding lair. Thane Khardros Wildhammer carved Grim Batol from the jagged mountains east of the marsh after the ancient civil war among the three clans. During the War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud laid siege to the fortress. Khardros struck her down, but before she died, Modgud cast a foul shadow across its stones. The lingering taint made the halls uninhabitable, and the surviving Wildhammer dwarves abandoned their kingdom and migrated north into the Hinterlands. During the Second War, Orgrim Doomhammer sent the Dragonmaw clan to claim Grim Batol. The warlock Nekros Skullcrusher led the orcs, who used the ancient artifact called the Demon Soul to enslave the red Dragonqueen Alexstrasza deep beneath the mountain. Chained there, Alexstrasza was forced to hatch broods for the Horde's war effort until a small band of heroes shattered the artifact. Freed, the enraged Dragon Aspect incinerated the orcs within. Grim Batol was left a desolate ruin, watched closely by surviving red dragons.

subzone:grizzled-den.text: Grizzled Den. Wendigo packs make their lair in Grizzled Den, southwest of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Grizzled Den cuts into the crags southwest of Kharanos, where Dun Morogh’s wendigo packs make their home. These aggressive, ape-like beasts breathe frost at intruders and band together to defend their hollows. Hunters brave the cavern for the thick wendigo manes, which craftsmen use to line cold chairs and carriage seats with insulated fur. Prospectors enter Grizzled Den to work copper veins in its frozen stone walls, and scouts search its darker corners for discarded footlockers. The deeper tunnels hold the den’s largest and most vicious predators, waiting in the shadows.

subzone:grizzlepaw-ridge.text: Grizzlepaw Ridge. Bears claim Grizzlepaw Ridge, the rough hills south of Thelsamar in Loch Modan. Ol' Sooty prowls among them, feared by local hunters. Grizzlepaw Ridge rises above the road south of Thelsamar, with Stonesplinter Valley along its western edge. Territorial bears claim the rough slopes and threaten travelers who skirt the mountains. Deep within the ridge lives Ol' Sooty, a massive, unusually fierce bear feared by local hunters. Travelers between the dwarven settlements watch the tree line and rocky terraces above.

subzone:grove-of-the-ancients.text: Grove of the Ancients. Nature spirits and kaldorei gather at the Grove of the Ancients, beside old temple ruins in southeastern Darkshore. Onu, an Ancient of Lore, watches over this sacred sanctuary near the Wildbend River. In southeastern Darkshore, old temple stones surround the Grove of the Ancients. The Wildbend River runs through its heart, a quiet refuge amid a coastline troubled by corruption and restless wildlife. Nature spirits and kaldorei gather here as the Circle of Ancients, tending to the forest’s balance. Onu, a towering Ancient of Lore, watches the land’s changing fortunes and offers wisdom to travelers. Wandering merchants and slumbering druids rest beneath the boughs. Territorial furbolg camps lie to the southeast, and Alliance sentinels and druids watch the southern reaches of Darkshore from this frontier outpost.

subzone:gryphon-roost.text: Gryphon Roost. Gryphons take travelers from Stormwind’s eastern ramparts across the Eastern Kingdoms. Dungar Longdrink, a human gryphon master, manages the roost beside the Trade District. From the eastern ramparts, gryphons carry travelers from Stormwind to Alliance garrisons and settlements across the Eastern Kingdoms. Dungar Longdrink, the seasoned gryphon master, coordinates flights to Ironforge, Lakeshire, Sentinel Hill, and other destinations. Gryphons and their handlers bring a trace of Hinterlands tradition within Stormwind’s walls. The Wildhammer clan has long revered gryphons as partners and introduced aerial warfare and transport to the broader Alliance during the Second War. Leather, feed, and fresh winds mark the roost amid the city’s stonework.

subzone:hall-of-arms.text: Hall of Arms. Dwarven warriors and hunters train at the Hall of Arms in Ironforge’s Military Ward. Its command staff oversees the city’s forces, while steam tanks and flying machines are prepared for battle. The Hall of Arms commands Ironforge’s armed forces from the southeastern corner of the Military Ward. Warriors and hunters train there under veteran instructors, while the facility stores and stages machines of war. Steam tanks are assembled and maintained on site for Alliance battlefields. Gyrocopters and flying machines travel up industrial conveyor belts, then launch through shafts in the cavern ceiling toward the Ironforge Airfield above.

subzone:hall-of-arms-northshire.text: Hall of Arms (Northshire). In Northshire Abbey, recruits train with the Stormwind Army in the Hall of Arms, south of the Main Hall. The Hall of Arms rings with blunted steel and the measured cadence of instruction. South of Northshire Abbey’s Main Hall, the wing trains human fighters and devout aspirants who take up arms for the Stormwind Army. Veteran battle instructors and paladin mentors teach the postures and disciplines needed to defend Elwynn Forest from kobolds, Defias bandits, and gnoll raiders. Across the courtyard, clerics and scholars study ancient tomes in the Library Wing.

subzone:hall-of-explorers.text: Hall of Explorers. Explorers gather relics and records in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. The dwarven Explorers' League studies Azeroth's past here, seeking the origins of the dwarven race. The Hall of Explorers fills a cavern in northeastern Ironforge. High Explorer Muninn Magellas directs scholars and field agents as they coordinate digs across distant lands. Relics, ancient titan machinery, and prehistoric bones return from those expeditions. At the hall's center, the Library holds historical lore, with displays open to visitors and other records kept under restriction.

subzone:hall-of-gears.text: Hall of Gears. Beyond the Clockwerk Run, the Hall of Gears lies in ruin inside Gnomeregan. Toxic sludge fills its lower floor, while oozes and irradiated troggs roam the chamber. The Hall of Gears lies beyond the Clockwerk Run, deep in Gnomeregan’s ruined machinery halls. Its two levels show how completely the gnome capital has fallen. Irradiated troggs claw through collapsed access shafts and prowl the upper catwalks. Below, radioactive pools cover the floor, where corrosive slimes and living poison elementals thrive in the toxic runoff. The Hall of Gears links parts of Gnomeregan’s operational quarters. From the upper walkways, paths lead to contaminated dead ends, the Clean Zone, and the Dormitory. Below, winding maintenance passages lead toward the Launch Bay. Both levels remain dangerous because of the horrors left by Mekgineer Thermaplugg’s venting scheme.

subzone:hall-of-mysteries.text: Hall of Mysteries. In Ironforge’s Mystic Ward, the Hall of Mysteries brings faith and arcane study together. Dwarven and gnomish practitioners read ancient texts, learn the Holy Light, and weave enchantments within its blue-lit halls. Blue and purple light marks the Hall of Mysteries amid Ironforge’s stone, iron, and heavy plate. Five soaring pillars shelter scholars in flowing robes. The hall is headquarters for the dwarven priesthood and the Order of the Silver Hand within Khaz Modan, joining arcane study with devotion to the Holy Light. Young clerics and knights study texts such as the Tome of Divinity here. They receive guidance before traveling onward to Stormwind’s Cathedral of Light.

subzone:helm-s-bed-lake.text: Helm's Bed Lake. In southeastern Dun Morogh, Helm's Bed Lake lies frozen beneath the hills. Dwarves keep a hole open in its ice for fresh water, while beasts, troggs, and hostile Dark Iron dwarves threaten the shore. Helm's Bed Lake lies beneath winter ice in southeastern Dun Morogh. Local dwarves keep an opening chopped through the frost so they can draw clean, fresh water. The frozen surface is stable enough to cross, but the banks are dangerous. Wild beasts roam the edges, displaced troggs scavenge along the ridges, and hostile Dark Iron dwarves have taken an abandoned lodge just south of the water. They ambush travelers who pass through.

subzone:heroes-vigil.text: Heroes' Vigil. On Stone Cairn Lake’s central island, Heroes' Vigil lies neglected and overrun by renegade wizards. Its Stone of Remembrance honors those who fell in the First War. Heroes' Vigil stands on an island in Stone Cairn Lake, centered on the Stone of Remembrance. Erected after the First War, its inscribed stone circle honors the soldiers and citizens slaughtered when the Old Horde sacked Goldshire and the surrounding valleys. Once revered as a sacred place of faith and sacrifice, the vigil has slipped from Stormwind's attention. Its grounds now lie overgrown, with no soldiers sent to tend them. With no kingdom garrison on the island, outcasts have taken the memorial. Rogue wizards control Stone Cairn Lake and the grounds, practicing wild, undisciplined magic beyond the oversight of the Kirin Tor and the Academy of Arcane Sciences. Near the stones lies Henze Faulk's body among other tragic casualties. Travelers can only wonder whether the shrine will ever know peace again.

subzone:high-seat.text: High Seat. King Magni Bronzebeard holds court in High Seat, between the Commons and the Great Forge. His royal advisors and historians gather in the chamber, where a sealed passage leads down to Old Ironforge. King Magni Bronzebeard hears petitioners and meets with his advisors in High Seat. Royal Historian Archesonus and Senator Barin Redstone stand among those at his side as he directs the defense of the Alliance's northern bastions. The chamber is the seat of power for the kingdom of Khaz Modan, and Magni leads from here amid troubling times across Azeroth. A heavy doorway at the back of the throne room leads down into Old Ironforge. The lower ruins are the ancestral halls the dwarves carved before the city was reconfigured around the Great Forge. The passage is sealed and guarded, keeping general traffic from the ancient halls beneath the capital.

subzone:highperch.text: Highperch. Highperch is an elevated plateau in western Thousand Needles, towering high above the canyon floor. It is renowned as a primary nesting ground for wild wyverns and wind riders. The roost is home to fierce prides defending their young among the windswept crags. Rising sharply out of the canyon floor, Highperch is a rugged sanctuary for Kalimdor's native wyverns. The plateau provides natural defense against predators and an unobstructed launch point for their hunting flights across Thousand Needles. Within its reaches, wyvern prides live under the protection of watchful patriarchs and matriarchs, guarding their nests. The beasts fiercely defend their territory against any intruders who manage to climb into their high domain. While hostile to outsiders, the high cliffs occasionally attract travellers and hunters willing to brave the dangerous ascent. The tauren scout Pao'ka Swiftmountain is stranded on these perilous heights and needs help reaching Whitereach Post. For adventurers journeying through the canyon, scaling the ramp to Highperch means contending with dozens of razor-sharp talons and venomous tails.

subzone:hillsbrad-fields.text: Hillsbrad Fields. In Hillsbrad Fields, farmers and militia face constant attacks from nearby Tarren Mill. The settlement in western Hillsbrad Foothills is one of the few human communities in former Lordaeron to resist the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. Hillsbrad Fields stretch from Darrow Hill to the Azurelode Mine, where orchards, pumpkin patches, and pastures supply Southshore and the surviving Alliance resistance. The people endured while much of Lordaeron fell to undeath, keeping the royal tabard and heraldry of their fallen kingdom. Magistrate Burnside and the Council of Hillsbrad lead the township as an independent civic body under constant siege. Verringtan, the local blacksmith, and his apprentices arm the people, so farmers and laborers can defend their land. High Executor Darthalia and the Forsaken forces at Tarren Mill target Hillsbrad's fertile fields. The Undercity sees the thriving human settlement as a threat on its southern flank and directs constant raids against its crops, livestock, councilors, and farmers. Hillsbrad's defenders have formed a hardened militia in response. Farmer Ray and Farmer Getz organize ambushes and fight the undead to protect their homes.

subzone:howling-vale.text: Howling Vale. The Terrowulf worgen howl through Howling Vale in north-central Ashenvale, near the Felwood border. Their caves hide an ancient shrine to Elune, bound to the worgen’s origins on Kalimdor. North of the road to Felwood, Ashenvale’s calm gives way to the howls of the Terrowulf. Ancient trees still fill the vale, but corrupted packlords and aggressive wildlife roam among them. A cave at its heart holds the shrine of Mel'Thandris, an ancient night elf priestess. Once a place of quiet devotion, the shrine now lies in ruins, defiled by feral wolf-men whose origin puzzles the nearby Sentinels.

subzone:hushed-bank.text: Hushed Bank. Along Duskwood’s western river, Hushed Bank runs from Three Corners toward Stranglethorn Vale. Beasts prowl its quiet shore, where dark mysteries linger. At Hushed Bank, Duskwood’s western edge follows the river that divides the forest from Westfall. The covered wooden bridge carries travelers west out of the grim wood. Near it, the land shifts from open plains and sunlit farms into unnatural twilight. Thick underbrush and creeping fog crowd the riverbanks. Large spiders and hungry forest wolves stalk wayfarers who stray from the path.

subzone:iceflow-lake.text: Iceflow Lake. At Iceflow Lake, dwarves keep fishing holes open through the ice. The lake lies in western Dun Morogh, directly north of Brewnall Village. Snow-covered islands rise from its center, where winter wolves and their alpha, Timber, prowl. Iceflow Lake lies in western Dun Morogh, just north of Brewnall Village. Bitter cold keeps thick sheets of ice creeping across its surface, so local residents such as Paxton Ganter clear holes for fishing and drinking water. The shore offers sustenance, but the islands in the lake’s center are dangerous ground. A fierce pack of wild wolves prowls those icy mounds, led by Timber, a savage gray worg.

subzone:iris-lake.text: Iris Lake. In north-central Ashenvale, Iris Lake lies east of Astranaar, its waters turned yellow-green by corruption from Felwood. Bog beasts prowl its shores. Iris Lake lies between Astranaar and the moonwell tended by Shael'dryn, its waters fouled since the Third War. Fel energies drift south from the tainted heights of Felwood and poison the basin, turning clear water into a yellow-green mire. The corruption has twisted the native plants and water spirits, and aggressive bog beasts lash out at travelers who come near. Pollution chokes Iris Lake, yet sacred remnants of the past linger along its edges. Rare crystalline stones called Elune's Tears sometimes rest on the muddy banks. Keepers of elven traditions, including Shael'dryn, seek the holy stones to help purify tainted moonwells and resist the demonic blight spreading across Ashenvale.

subzone:ironband-s-compound.text: Ironband's Compound. Dark Iron dwarves hold Ironband's Compound south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh. Once Sturgy Ironband's camp, it now threatens travelers and nearby settlements. Dark Iron dwarves hold the compound south of Helm's Bed Lake. Sturgy Ironband first established the camp as a staging post in Dun Morogh's snowy wilderness. Dark Iron infiltrators pushed deep into Bronzebeard territory and seized it. Now their forces threaten travelers and nearby settlements, close to Ironforge. The Dark Iron camp stands within Dun Morogh's borders, a serious provocation to Ironforge. The city keeps watch and sends seasoned warriors to recover fallen scouts and secure vital intelligence about the Dark Iron threat in the mountain kingdom.

subzone:ironband-s-excavation-site.text: Ironband's Excavation Site. Prospector Ironband’s dig lies south of the Loch, where troggs have driven the miners from their trenches. The excavation in southeastern Loch Modan, southwest of Farstrider Lodge, has been halted. Prospector Ironband’s dig in southeastern Loch Modan began with a search into the dwarves’ ancient Titan origins. The work ended in disaster when the miners disturbed an unusually fierce, large breed of subterranean troggs. The creatures surged from the earth, drove the miners back, and made camp among scattered tools, broken carts, and half-excavated relics. The troggs hold the site, while surviving prospectors wait at the edge of the perimeter. Like efforts in the Badlands, Wetlands, and Uldaman, this dig is caught in danger. The prospectors hope to reclaim their stolen gear and guard exposed artifacts, including strange ancient statues left by long-forgotten builders, from the ravenous troggs.

subzone:ironbeard-s-tomb.text: Ironbeard's Tomb. West of the road to Dun Modr, Ironbeard's Tomb lies defiled and overrun by acidic oozes. A stone statue watches over the outdoor graveyard, where travelers search the slime for lost possessions. Ironbeard's Tomb overlooks the marshes beside the road north to Dun Modr. A great stone statue, believed to show Ironbeard, watches over the burial plot. Black and crimson oozes have overrun the crypt below, tainting the resting place. Dwarves no longer bring their dead here. Those who enter the vaults search among the remains swallowed by the slimes.

subzone:ironclad-cove.text: Ironclad Cove. Deep beneath Westfall, Ironclad Cove holds a hidden shipyard and dock. The Defias Brotherhood builds its war juggernaught here, with a passage to the sea. Ironclad Cove lies at the deepest point of the Deadmines, where a vast sea cavern has become a fortified dockyard. Edwin VanCleef and the Defias Brotherhood have built an enormous warship here, the juggernaught. Wooden scaffolding, islets, and loading catwalks fill the cavern, watched by Defias pirates, deckhands, and overseers. VanCleef aims to do more than raid Westfall's farmsteads: he plans to assemble a private naval force capable of bombarding Stormwind's shores.

subzone:ironforge-airfield.text: Ironforge Airfield. High above Dun Morogh, gnome flying machines and dwarven mountaineers hold a remote airfield northeast of Ironforge. Its plateau overlooks jagged crags and the steep descent toward the Wetlands. High above Dun Morogh's trails, gnome flying machines line open landing strips among the mountain peaks. Dwarven masonry anchors the ridgelines, and mountaineers watch the perimeter. Nearby, engineers tend the machines and inspect their engines in the cold. The valley around the airfield is contested ground. Frostmane trolls dwell in nearby caves and harass the dwarven sentries. Across frozen waters beneath the peaks, dwarven defenders and Stormpike patrols clash with troll raiders, keeping the outpost on guard.

subzone:jangolode-mine.text: Jangolode Mine. In Westfall’s rolling hills, the Defias Brotherhood works Jangolode Mine for itself. The mine once supplied Stormwind City with ore and raw materials. Before Westfall declined, Jangolode Mine sent metals to Stormwind City for its reconstruction and supply. As civil order weakened and the kingdom withdrew its garrisons, the Defias Brotherhood seized the mine to support its own operations. The bandits now work its rich veins and defend the shafts fiercely.

subzone:jansen-stead.text: Jansen Stead. Jansen Stead lies just west of the Elwynn border, where Defias bandits and mechanical Harvest Watchers now roam its fields. Jansen Stead lies beside the road from Elwynn into Westfall. The farm once fed the kingdom, but unrest has driven its family from the land. Now Harvest Watchers, mechanical constructs associated with the Defias Brotherhood, patrol the fields alongside brigands. Couriers and travelers between Goldshire and Sentinel Hill pass close by.

subzone:jasperlode-mine.text: Jasperlode Mine. In north-central Elwynn, Jasperlode Mine lies lost to kobolds and giant spiders. Its shafts once supplied Stormwind City with vital iron and minerals, but the resource-strapped kingdom cannot reclaim them. Jasperlode Mine once supplied Stormwind with a steady wealth of minerals, alongside nearby Fargodeep. With the kingdom's forces stretched thin by outside threats and unrest, local garrisons cannot protect the shafts. Kobolds seized their chance, drove out the human miners, and hoarded stolen gold and tallow candles. Deep within Jasperlode Mine, mine spiders have taken hold beneath the timber supports. A massive matriarch called Mother Fang leads them. The spiders prey on trespassing kobolds and unwary prospectors, making any attempt to salvage the mine dangerous.

subzone:jerod-s-landing.text: Jerod's Landing. Defias smugglers hold Jerod's Landing on the Elwynn Forest bank of the Nazferiti River. The dock gives them a hidden route for illicit shipments across the kingdom's waterways. Defias outlaws now control the river dock at Jerod's Landing, where Elwynn Forest meets the waters of the Nazferiti River. Once an ordinary boat dock, it now receives goods plundered from the Redridge Mountains under a Defias dockmaster's watch. The outlaws move the cargo discreetly downstream toward holdings such as Klaven's Tower in Westfall.

subzone:kargathia-keep.text: Kargathia Keep. Warsong overseers hold the eastern edge of their lumber camp at Kargathia Keep. The fortified stronghold guards the Southfury River border in Ashenvale and links the outpost to Orgrimmar. Kargathia Keep anchors the eastern edge of the Warsong Lumber Camp, just west of the Southfury River. Spiked barricades fortify the outpost, where Overseer Gorthak and his officers direct the Horde’s logging operations. From the river border, the Warsong clan watches for incursions. When night elf skirmishers strike, reinforcements can come swiftly from Durotar and Orgrimmar. Kargathia Keep shares its namesake with Kargath in the Badlands and Bladefist Bay on Durotar’s coast: the famed chieftain Kargath Bladefist. For Warsong orcs facing Ashenvale’s hostile woodlands, its imposing architecture speaks of martial resilience and Horde defiance in lands claimed by the night elves.

subzone:kharanos.text: Kharanos. Kharanos is a bustling mountain settlement nestled in the snowy heart of Dun Morogh, just down the road from Ironforge. Serving as the primary hub for travelers leaving Coldridge Valley, the town hosts a forge, gnomish workshops, and the famous Thunderbrew Distillery. Situated along the central road of Dun Morogh, Kharanos is the first true town welcoming recruits arriving from Anvilmar. Despite the biting cold and biting winds, the settlement thrives thanks to local dwarven grit and gnomish ingenuity. It centers around a roaring public forge and the Thunderbrew Distillery, renowned across the eastern mountains for producing some of the finest ale in Khaz Modan. Between bustling crafters and weary travelers seeking warmth, the town stands as the essential staging ground for business in the lower peaks. Behind its cozy hearths, Kharanos serves as a vital military outpost tasked with keeping the mountain passes secure. Fierce indigenous wendigo prowl the frozen caverns directly to the west, while aggressive Frostmane trolls remain entrenched atop Shimmer Ridge to the northwest. With Ironforge's regular forces stretched thin across the realm, the town relies heavily on visiting adventurers and local watchmen to drive back raiding parties, cull dangerous predators, and ensure the trade routes remain open.

subzone:lake-al-ameth.text: Lake Al'Ameth. South of Dolanaar, Lake Al'Ameth's shores have turned perilous as the local plant life grows violent. Once a quiet haven with little more than a wooden jetty, the lake is one of Teldrassil's largest freshwater bodies. At Lake Al'Ameth, swarms of timberlings and timberling sprouts prowl the water's edge. The lake lies just south of Dolanaar, where its calm waters and sparse settlement offer little sign of the danger ashore. An unnatural sickness spreading through Teldrassil has driven the plant life into a frenzy. Druids and researchers from Dolanaar send travelers to gather seeds and kill the aggressive creatures before the corruption spreads deeper into the forest. Oakenscowl, once a noble timberling, spreads corruption from a cave on Lake Al'Ameth's southern bank. A gargantuan tumor has swollen his body, and other timberlings lash out at anyone who approaches. The woodland spirits have lost their balance, and the Cenarion Circle faces an urgent test: can the rot around the lake be diagnosed and treated, and can Teldrassil's unblessed creation be sustained?

subzone:lake-everstill.text: Lake Everstill. Murlocs and lake beasts now make Lake Everstill dangerous beside Lakeshire. Once known for calm fishing and clear mountain runoff, its waters and shores have grown perilous. Lake Everstill fills Redridge's central basin beside Lakeshire. Its clear waters run east toward Stonewatch, and a bridge crosses the lake at the heart of town. The lake has long supported local trade and drawn anglers seeking quiet. Now, wilderness threats have broken that calm along the shore. Hostile murlocs have made camps along the northern and eastern shallows, disrupting trade and harrying fishermen. Dangerous threshers patrol the deeper waters below.

subzone:lake-falathim.text: Lake Falathim. At Lake Falathim, murlocs now overrun the western Ashenvale shore southwest of Maestra's Post. Night elves once came here to swim and fish, drawn by Elune's moonlight said to touch the water day and night. Lake Falathim lies southeast of the Zoram Strand, where the Kaldorei once swam and fished in peace. Local lore says Elune's gentle light rests on the water at every hour, by day and by night. Now ferocious murlocs have surged inland and seized the shores. Their numbers drive away travelers and scholars. Murlocs have made Lake Falathim dangerous for anyone wandering alone. The night elf scholar Teronis recently went missing near the water while pursuing his inquiry. Sentinels fear for anyone who approaches the moonlit pool alone, with hostile murlocs lurking along the banks and in the shallows.

subzone:lakeridge-highway.text: Lakeridge Highway. Travelers on Lakeridge Highway face ruin and danger along Lake Everstill's southern shore. Before the First War, this vital, heavily traveled road carried trade through Redridge; now gnolls and Blackrock orcs make passage perilous. Before the First War, Lakeridge Highway carried goods and travelers through Redridge as a busy trade route along Lake Everstill's southern shore. In those peaceful days, travelers crossed between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under Stormwind's protection. The Horde's march shattered that safety, leaving eastern Redridge contested and desolate. After Blackrock orcs seized Stonewatch Keep, regular road repairs and patrols stopped. Lakeridge Highway soon crumbled into an overgrown track, contested by savage gnoll packs. Stormwind's forces are spread thin and cannot reinforce Lakeshire, leaving the highway officially unsafe. Travelers bound for the eastern ridges must face gnoll ambushes along the way.

subzone:lakeshire.text: Lakeshire. Lakeshire's defenders face attacks from orcs, gnolls, and murlocs along Lake Everstill. Magistrate Solomon leads the town, while Marshal Marris commands its guard. Lakeshire once offered peace in the foothills east of Stormwind. Now it is the kingdom's hardest-pressed frontier. Blackrock clan orcs swept down from the north and overran the garrison at Stonewatch Keep. Dark wizardry stirred Shadowhide gnolls into organized raiding parties. Blackrock saboteurs also broke parts of the Everstill Bridge. Foreman Oslow and his crew struggle to mend the span under threat of attack. Murlocs crowd the lake's shores, while gnolls stalk the high passes. Lakeshire's defenders are close to breaking.

subzone:lakeshire-inn.text: Lakeshire Inn. At Lakeshire Inn, travelers and townsfolk seek shelter as danger closes around Lakeshire. On Lake Everstill, the inn offers food, drink, and a place to hear news amid the town’s troubles. On the shore of Lake Everstill, Lakeshire Inn offers a short rest from the gnoll bands and Blackrock orcs pressing against the town. Though Lakeshire’s military position grows more desperate, the tavern remains warm and welcoming. Barkeep Daniels and Innkeeper Brianna serve ale, wine, and hot meals to locals and travelers. Townspeople gather to trade news, ease their sorrows, and seek hired blades to defend the kingdom’s eastern border. Wiley the Black watches the room from a table, keeping his thoughts to himself and an eye on dangers in the region. Traveling brewers such as Yorus Barleybrew stop at the inn, and Darcy Parker and other townsfolk visit the common room. For those bound for the jagged peaks or south toward Duskwood, Lakeshire Inn is the last safe haven before the contested wilderness.

subzone:lakeshire-town-hall.text: Lakeshire Town Hall. At Lakeshire Town Hall, Magistrate Solomon directs Redridge's affairs from the heart of Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs and gnolls bring relentless threats to the lakeside settlement. Lakeshire Town Hall, an aging stone building, has been refurbished many times over the years. It stands prominently in Lakeshire and houses Magistrate Solomon, a kind and dedicated civil leader who maintains order in the eastern reaches of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Stormwind's military is stretched thin, and royal aid is scarce. The hall has changed from a quiet administrative office into an active command center, where desperate appeals for volunteer defenders and mercenaries are processed daily. Gnoll incursions and the encroaching Blackrock orcs have driven Magistrate Solomon to desperation. With aid scarce, he readily accepts help from independent adventurers who come through the town hall doors.

subzone:library-ironforge.text: Library (Ironforge). In Ironforge's Library, the Explorers' League keeps its histories and recovered relics. The eastern wing of the Hall of Explorers holds books and artifacts gathered from across Azeroth. Dwarven scholars study relics and field reports from across the world in a great chamber of the Hall of Explorers. The Explorers' League keeps the Library, where shelves hold chronicles of the War of the Three Hammers, the ancient Troll Wars, and the origins of the dwarven race. Librarian Mae Paledust helps visitors find rare books and records. Curator Thorius oversees the Library's displays of physical finds from deep excavations, abandoned ruins, and distant shorelines. League members study, preserve, and display these objects. The collection ranges from crude murloc idols and carved knives to relics recovered frozen in northern ice. Curators record each find as they piece together the history of the Titans and early Azeroth.

subzone:library-wing-northshire.text: Library Wing (Northshire). In Northshire Abbey, the Library Wing gathers scholars and new priests and mages. Its quiet southern rooms offer instruction for those joining Stormwind’s defense. The Library Wing branches south from Northshire Abbey’s Main Hall. Dusty shelves, study lecterns, and quiet alcoves fill its rooms, where aspiring mages and priests learn the Arcane and the Holy Light. Across the abbey, martial recruits drill in the Hall of Arms. Priestess Anetta guides novice priests in faith and healing, while Khelden Bremen teaches budding mages to shape primal elemental energy.

subzone:lion-s-pride-inn.text: Lion's Pride Inn. Travelers gather at the Lion's Pride Inn, Goldshire's tavern and community center in Elwynn Forest. Innkeeper Farley keeps the inn, a place to rest, meet others, and find work just south of Stormwind City. The Lion's Pride Inn anchors Goldshire at the crossroads of Elwynn Forest. Innkeeper Farley keeps it by the old motto, “Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold.” Inside, warm hearths, strong drinks, and rooms welcome weary travelers from Northshire. Goldshire sits on trade routes between Stormwind, Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood, making the inn an indispensable gathering place. Town marshals, local crafters, and seasoned trainers meet there to share news and hire passing mercenaries.

subzone:long-wash.text: Long Wash. Along Darkshore, Long Wash runs south from Auberdine toward Ameth'Aran beneath a gray sky. Murlocs now make its shore dangerous. Long Wash is Darkshore's shortest distinct stretch of coast, despite its name. Beneath the region's perpetual overcast skies, damp sand lies strewn with flotsam, driftwood, and sea creatures washed up by the Veiled Sea. Crabs comb the surf, but travelers heading south from Auberdine must watch for murloc tribes camped along the water's edge. The murlocs attack anyone who enters the territory where they scavenge.

subzone:longshore.text: Longshore. Along Westfall’s western edge, Longshore’s broad sands are claimed by hostile murlocs and broken ships. Longshore runs along Westfall’s western coast, a wide stretch of unbroken sand. Travelers find little peace there. Murlocs dominate the surf, with Old Murk-Eye among the feared leaders, and sunken ships, including ruined elven destroyers, lie in the shallows. Near the south, Daphne Stilwell’s isolated farm faces Defias bandits. Across the water, the Westfall Lighthouse stands within sight.

subzone:lordamere-lake.text: Lordamere Lake. Lordamere Lake lies between Tirisfal Glades, Silverpine Forest, and the Alterac Mountains, its waters now shadowed by the undead. Once the northern heart of human life, its cold waters and islands are haunted by Scourge necromancers and feral murlocs. Lordamere Lake once joined the centers of human power in the north. The Capital City of Lordaeron guarded its northern shores, Dalaran rose near the southern reach, and Alterac lined the eastern edge beneath its mountains. Merchant vessels and fishing boats crossed the broad lake without fear. After the devastation of the Third War, the lake became a natural barrier between the Forsaken-held lands of Tirisfal and Silverpine and the treacherous heights of Alterac.

subzone:maclure-vineyards.text: Maclure Vineyards. In southern Elwynn, Maclure Vineyards sends grapes and wine to Stormwind. The Maclure family's estate is known as much for its bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefields as for its harvest. The Maclure Vineyards should be a peaceful haven of farming and winecraft in southern Elwynn Forest. Instead, the feud with the Stonefields down the road overshadows the family's daily labor. Accusations of theft and old resentment keep tempers high between the households. Hungry boars prowl the land, while kobolds press toward both homesteads.

subzone:maestra-s-post.text: Maestra's Post. Along the road through western Ashenvale, Maestra's Post watches the way between Astranaar and the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. Night elven Sentinels guard the settlement, where a few humans serve the Alliance. Maestra's Post keeps watch beneath the trees of western Ashenvale. A slender night elven tower and an open lodge mark the settlement along the road between the coast of Darkshore and Astranaar. Sentinels scan the surrounding wilds as corrupted furbolg stir nearby. Horde movements also threaten Alliance supply lines. Maestra's Post brings a handful of human allies to live among the night elven Sentinels. Feero Ironhand and Delgren the Purifier lend their martial strength and devotion to the holy Light in service of the Alliance. This remote campsite is an early meeting place between the eastern kingdoms and Kalimdor's ancient defenders.

subzone:mage-quarter.text: Mage Quarter. The Mage Quarter forms the arcane heart of Stormwind City, resting across the canals in the capital's southwestern corner. Towering over its cobblestone streets and esoteric specialty shops stands the Wizard's Sanctum, where the kingdom's conjurers hone their craft. Beneath the district's scholarly surface also lie shadowy recesses, harboring practitioners of far darker arts. Reachable by bridges crossing the canals from Cathedral Square or the Trade District, the Mage Quarter caters entirely to the mystical needs of the Alliance. Centered around the spire of the Wizard's Sanctum, human and allied spellcasters gather to study the weave of arcane magic and train apprentices. The surrounding streets are crowded with purveyors of tailoring cloth, reagents, alchemical supplies, and enchanted staves, creating an insular district dedicated to research and the defense of the kingdom.

subzone:main-hall-northshire.text: Main Hall (Northshire). Newcomers report in the Main Hall at Northshire Abbey in western Elwynn. From there, they reach the Hall of Arms, the Library Wing, and the abbey tower, then receive their first assignments defending Stormwind. Trainees and clerics pass through the Main Hall after entering Northshire Abbey. The chamber links the Hall of Arms, where recruits prepare for battle, with the Library Wing and the stairs to the abbey tower. Strife in the valley reaches even this quiet place, and officers rally able newcomers to defend the kingdom's borders.

subzone:malaka-jin.text: Malaka'jin. Malaka'jin shelters Horde hunters in the lower Stonetalon hills, south of Grimtotem Post. Darkspear trolls make the camp a waystation for travelers climbing from the Barrens into the mountains. Malaka'jin sits beside the main trail into the Stonetalon Mountains. Horde travelers find a small camp of troll hunters living off the crags and scrublands. The hunters trade supplies and fresh game with those passing through, while watching for mountain predators and Grimtotem tauren farther up the trails. Malaka'jin marks an early Horde foothold in Stonetalon, near the Barrens boundary. Sun Rock Retreat is a larger stronghold farther north, while this quiet camp gives Horde trackers a place to watch tribal unrest and guard the winding roads against threats.

subzone:manor-mistmantle.text: Manor Mistmantle. In Duskwood's shadowed northeastern hills, Manor Mistmantle lies north of Darkshire. Once a family homestead, the estate has fallen into ruin, where ghouls prowl under the command of its infamous master. West of Beggar's Haunt, Manor Mistmantle's ruined grounds are choked with decay. Vicious ghouls prowl there, guarding the broken house. In the untended garden, a solitary, sorrowful blossom called the Tear of Tilloa is the only sign of living beauty on the entire property.

subzone:mast-room.text: Mast Room. Timber from Westfall reaches the Mast Room, deep in the Deadmines, where goblin woodcarvers shape it for the Defias.

subzone:master-s-glaive.text: Master's Glaive. In southwestern Darkshore, the Master's Glaive rises from an ancient, unsettling site. Night elves once revered it as a sacred mystery, but Twilight's Hammer cultists now swarm around the colossal weapon, drawn by the malevolence that lingers there. At the Master's Glaive, an adamantine blade pierces a colossal petrified skull. No record names the creature or the hand that drove the blade home. Onu, the Ancient of Lore, says only that an old, old lord of the earth fell here. Night elves long believed that only the titans could wield a weapon so vast. The blade and skull remain a monument to that forgotten clash. Night elves held the Master's Glaive in solemn reverence for generations. Now Twilight's Hammer fanatics have camped around the sunken carcass, digging trenches and uncovering petrified ribs. Whispers beneath the stone draw them to study the remains obsessively and commune with the malevolent power that clings to them. They seek to revive or harness whatever fell essence sleeps within the earth.

subzone:menethil-harbor.text: Menethil Harbor. Menethil Harbor links the Eastern Kingdoms to Kalimdor from its island off the Wetlands' western shore. Stone battlements and Menethil Keep's towers guard the port, where merchants, off-duty soldiers, and salty adventurers gather. Menethil Harbor honors King Terenas Menethil II of Lordaeron and offers the Alliance a haven on the Wetlands coast. Its remote marshland setting leaves it exposed, so massive walls, a single bridged causeway, and Menethil Keep's four stone watchtowers guard the town. Menethil Harbor is a crossroads for Alliance ships crossing the ocean to Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh and, by way of Southshore, Auberdine in Darkshore. The ships carry trade and diplomats, while off-duty Kul Tiran marines spend their wages at the Deepwater Tavern. Peace remains fragile. The Dragonmaw clan contests inland supply paths through Dun Algaz, and Dark Iron raiders press the northern marshes. Captain Stoutfist and the harbor garrison stay on constant alert.

subzone:military-ward.text: Military Ward. Red banners mark the Military Ward, where Ironforge's defenders gather and train. Its command halls, weapons masters, barracks, siege engines, and flying machines serve the mountain city's military. The Military Ward gathers Ironforge's defenses in a busy staging ground along the northern edge of the mountain fortress. At its center, the Hall of Arms holds warrior and hunter trainers and battlemasters, with hangars for dwarven flying machines and steam tanks. Around the drill squares and training dummies, supply shops include Craghelm's Plate and Chain, Goldfury's Hunting Supplies, and Timberline Arms. The ward is Ironforge's main staging point for mountaineers and city defenders. Red banners cover the Military Ward, setting it apart from the Commons' pale blue and the Great Forge's fiery orange. Between drills and weapons inspections, soldiers and off-duty guards gather for ale at Bruuk's Corner. Weapon Master Buliwyf Stonehand teaches recruits the ancient martial traditions of the dwarves.

subzone:mirage-raceway.text: Mirage Raceway. The Mirage Raceway is an impromptu engineering proving ground situated in the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles. Founded on the heated rivalry between goblin tinkerer Pozzik and gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts, it pits high-speed rocket cars against one another across the baked earth. The track serves as a neutral gathering place where members of both the Alliance and Horde come to wager, tinker, and cheer on their favored machines. Sprawled across the vast white desert floor of the Shimmering Flats, the Mirage Raceway was born out of an unrelenting grudge match between two master tinkerers: the goblin Pozzik and the gnome Fizzle Brassbolts. Determined to settle once and for all whose race possesses superior technical ingenuity, the two constructed custom rocket-powered drag cars and recruited rival crews to pit them against each other in daily high-velocity showdowns. The relentless competition has turned the barren flats into a bustling hub of invention, sabotage, and testing as each crew desperately looks for any mechanical advantage. The raceway draws supporters from both the Horde and Alliance. Spectators gather from across Kalimdor to cheer on either gnome precision or goblin firepower, while gamblers and shady opportunists thrive on the constant wagers placed on the results. Beyond the roar of rocket thrusters, the camps serve as a busy trading depot for travelers journeying between Thousand Needles and the blazing sands of Tanaris.

subzone:mirkfallon-lake.text: Mirkfallon Lake. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Mirkfallon Lake fills a basin beneath Windshear Crag. Native wildlife crowds its waters and banks, from aggressive slimes to thunder lizards and wyverns. Mirkfallon Lake lies at the center of the Stonetalon range, between the passes to Webwinder Path in the south and Stonetalon Peak in the north. Runoff from the highlands feeds its waters, drawing thunder lizards down to drink and wyverns from their high roosts. Strange slimes bubble in the lake, making the crossing hazardous for travelers. Paths cross the lake basin in every direction. To the east, rocky tracks climb into Windshear Crag and the logging operations deep in its forested valleys. North of the lake, travelers climb toward night elven sanctums and tauren heights. Southward, the route skirts venomous spider hollows. Explorers and scouts crossing the contested mountains must reckon with the shifting dangers around the lake.

subzone:mirror-lake.text: Mirror Lake. Water spills into Mirror Lake beneath Stormwind's cliffs in northwestern Elwynn Forest, near an orchard. Defias bandits prowl the surrounding orchards, while mages watch for trouble in the forest's arcane currents. Mirror Lake lies beneath Stormwind City's walls, where fishermen and weary travelers might seek a quiet rest. Defias Brotherhood brigands stalk the surrounding orchards, making a long stay perilous for locals. Mystical disturbances across Azeroth have also begun to warp the forest's natural channels of arcane energy. Mages from the Wizard's Sanctum watch the lake closely. They send practitioners to sample its currents and guard against chaotic arcane runoff poisoning communities downstream.

subzone:mirror-lake-orchard.text: Mirror Lake Orchard. Defias bandits now hold Mirror Lake Orchard, on Mirror Lake's southern shore in western Elwynn Forest. The quiet homestead near Thunder Falls has fallen to outlaws while Stormwind's guards are stretched thin. Mirror Lake Orchard once fed a peaceful farmstead with the clean waters of Mirror Lake. Now Defias Brotherhood bandits have seized the cottage and grounds near Thunder Falls. With Stormwind's military stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn missing, rural homes across Elwynn are easy targets for outlaws seeking shelter.

subzone:mist-s-edge.text: Mist's Edge. North of Auberdine, Mist's Edge follows Darkshore's western shore beneath ocean fog. Gray beaches hold shipwrecks, great sea creature remains, crabs, and murlocs. Mist's Edge runs along Darkshore's western edge, where damp sand and rocky tidepools lie beneath coastal fog. Shattered vessels, drift timber, and the remains of huge sea creatures litter the beach. Crabs forage along the shore, while murloc tribes make their homes in the surf. Wreckage and discarded cargo line the sands where vessels have been lost in the waters off Darkshore. Night elf sentinels and scavengers watch the coast, as murloc encampments menace travelers making their way along the shore from Auberdine.

subzone:misty-pine-refuge.text: Misty Pine Refuge. At Misty Pine Refuge, the Argent Dawn keeps a small outpost in central Dun Morogh. Misty Pine Refuge is an unassuming Argent Dawn outpost among Dun Morogh's windswept hills. Ironforge mountaineers patrol the surrounding crags, while Father Gavin, the order's lone agent here, keeps a quiet hearth amid the bitter cold and dangers of the mountain roads.

subzone:mo-grosh-stronghold.text: Mo'grosh Stronghold. Mo'grosh Stronghold looms over the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. The fortified ogre den is dug among ancient ruins, and its inhabitants threaten the dwarven settlements below. Mo'grosh ogres raid supply caravans in northeastern Loch Modan. From their caves and outer camps, they threaten travelers and the peace of Thelsamar. Rugged stonework scattered around the camp points to an older settlement. The ogres claimed the site and raised their distinctive mounds.

subzone:molsen-farm.text: Molsen Farm. Molsen Farm is an abandoned homestead located in the breadbasket region of Westfall. Once a fertile piece of farmland feeding Stormwind, it has fallen into ruin following the rise of the Defias Brotherhood and the prowling mechanical harvest golems left in their wake. Like many homesteads across Westfall, Molsen Farm stands as a casualty of the kingdom's neglect and criminal uprising. When the Defias Brotherhood took control of the countryside, the resident farmers were driven out or worse, abandoning their crops and buildings. Now, instead of laborers gathering grain, hostile mechanical Harvest Watchers and wandering outlaws scour the untended fields, making the farm a hazard to anyone traveling through the province.

subzone:moonbrook.text: Moonbrook. In southwestern Westfall, Moonbrook lies under Defias control, its streets emptied of peaceful residents. The Brotherhood uses the town as a guarded screen for its hidden headquarters in the Deadmines. Before the First War, Moonbrook stood at the heart of Westfall’s breadbasket, supporting farming families and the gold shafts of the Deadmines. The Old Horde razed the town, but it was rebuilt after the Second War. Its peace did not last. The House of Nobles in Stormwind neglected the settlement, and its military protection was stripped away. Unable to resist the red-masked bandits, Moonbrook’s people were driven from their homes. Citizens and teachers fled toward Sentinel Hill and Elwynn Forest.

subzone:moonbrook-schoolhouse.text: Moonbrook Schoolhouse. In Moonbrook's northwestern corner, the schoolhouse stands abandoned under Defias occupation. A small graveyard lies behind the hall where Stalvan Mistmantle once taught local children. Moonbrook's schoolhouse once welcomed children before ruin and bandits overtook the town. After Stalvan Mistmantle began tutoring local children, the mayor commissioned him to run a school. Students filled the hall in Moonbrook's brighter days, when the town prospered. Now outlaws occupy the abandoned building, and weathered headstones in its rear cemetery look out over Westfall's decline.

subzone:moonshrine-ruins.text: Moonshrine Ruins. Deep in Blackfathom Deeps, the Moonshrine Ruins lie flooded and seized by the Twilight's Hammer. Their halls once honored Elune, but the cult now carries out dark rituals among the ancient stones. Beyond the cavernous Pool of Ask'ar, the Moonshrine Ruins lie along the Ashenvale coast. These partly submerged halls once echoed with chants to Elune, the Moon Goddess. The Great Sundering shattered the temple and drowned its lower levels in seawater. Now murky waters churn with aggressive crabs and serpentine threshadons. The Twilight's Hammer cult holds the stones and performs dark rituals that mock the shrine's sacred origins.

subzone:moonspray.text: Moonspray. Moonspray carries travelers between Darkshore and Teldrassil. The Alliance transport sails across the waters separating mainland Kalimdor from the great World Tree. Moonspray sails between Auberdine and Rut'theran Village. Across the Veiled Sea, the vessel carries adventurers, couriers, and provisions between Darkshore's coast and the night elf sanctuary at Teldrassil's crown.

subzone:moonwell-ashenvale.text: Moonwell (Ashenvale). This secluded shrine, known to the night elves as the Moonwell of Purity, rests in central Ashenvale east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat. Its blessed waters channel the grace of Elune to nourish the ancient forest and cleanse creeping foulness from the land. Alliance travelers following Raene Wolfrunner's research often seek out Shael'dryn, who keeps watch beside its tranquil basin. Tucked away beneath the canopy of central Ashenvale, this moonwell serves as a spiritual anchor for the kaldorei. Its luminescent waters tap into nature's latent magic and the light of the Moon Goddess. As the surrounding forest suffers from satyr corruption, fel taint, and logging incursions, pure shrines like this one become vital lifelines for those trying to heal the woods.

subzone:mor-shan-rampart.text: Mor'shan Rampart. At Mor'shan Rampart, the Horde guards the northern end of the Gold Road and the way into Ashenvale. The Warsong clan built the barricade to shield Horde territory from night elf counterattacks and stage raids into the forest. Mor'shan Rampart guards the northern end of the Gold Road, where the Barrens meet Ashenvale. Its timber walls and watchtowers were raised against night elf strikes over the Horde's logging. From here, raiding parties head north toward Astranaar. Warsong fighters and sentries keep Mor'shan Rampart ready for battle. They watch the tree line for night elf scouts and archers, while the post keeps supply lines open between Ashenvale's frontline outposts and Horde settlements to the south.

subzone:mortwake-s-tower.text: Klaven's Tower. Klaven's Tower, also called the Defias Tower, is a fortified watchtower standing near the river in southeastern Westfall. Commanded by the rogue Klaven Mortwake, it serves as a critical waypoint for smuggling stolen goods across kingdom borders. Perched on the borderlands north of the Dagger Hills, Klaven's Tower is a vital hub for Defias Brotherhood operations in southern Westfall. Together with Jerod's Landing across the river in Elwynn Forest, the site acts as a receiving post and staging ground for contraband plundered from the Redridge Mountains. Its commanding vantage over the waterways allows the Brotherhood to slip supplies past Kingdom patrols, shielding their logistical network from the crown's eyes.

subzone:mystic-ward.text: Mystic Ward. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, faith and arcane study share the city's quieter quarter. Pale blue banners mark its halls, and the Hall of Mysteries gathers priests, paladins, and mages beneath stone arches. The Mystic Ward carries Ironforge's quieter pursuits of faith and learning. Pale blue banners mark the quarter between the Commons, the Forlorn Cavern, and the Great Forge. Shops such as The Fighting Wizard and Maeva's Mystical Apparel supply scholars and spellweavers with regalia, scrolls, and alchemical reagents. At the Hall of Mysteries, followers of the Holy Light and practitioners of arcane magic find guidance in wielding powers unseen in defense of the Alliance.

subzone:mystral-lake.text: Mystral Lake. Travelers from both factions reach Mystral Lake in south-central Ashenvale. Its deep waters draw them beneath the watch of the night elves. Mystral Lake draws travelers to its shores in southern Ashenvale. The vast lake lies south of Silverwind Refuge and east of Talondeep Vale, the largest lake in the forest. Night elves keep watch from their outpost on its northern shore. Travelers from both the Horde and the Alliance often find their journeys bringing them to its banks. Horde shaman come to Mystral Lake during trials of elemental communion. In its deep waters, they seek to understand the element of water. The lake’s raw primal resonance makes it an essential pilgrimage site for those learning to bind and respect the tidal spirits.

subzone:night-run.text: Night Run. In east-central Ashenvale, Night Run crowns a cliff-ringed bluff among the ancient elven ruins. Felmusk satyr dwell there, and dark soul magic gathers within the outpost. Night Run is Ashenvale’s smallest and most isolated of its three major satyr strongholds, alongside Xavian and Satyrnaar. Crumbling elven stonework and broken pillars shelter the settlement on a high ridge bounded by steep, impassable cliffs. Travelers can reach it by following the Falfarren River near the waters of Xavian, then turning west up the ridge, or by taking a precarious northern ledge above Raynewood Retreat. Though small, the enclave is dangerous. The Felmusk satyr work with the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand, anchoring twisted soulgems to gather demonic essence within the forest.

subzone:nightsong-woods.text: Nightsong Woods. In eastern Ashenvale, Nightsong Woods runs from Raynewood Retreat toward Azshara. Night elves and the Warsong clan fight over the forest as the Horde harvests lumber, while demonic corruption lingers among its groves. Nightsong Woods is Ashenvale’s eastern battleground. The Falfarren River cuts through its western reaches, marking a tense boundary between Alliance settlements and Horde incursions. Farther east, Splintertree Post directs Horde campaigns against the Silverwing Sentinels. Warsong orcs fell the southern groves for lumber to fuel the Horde’s expansion, angering the Kaldorei. Satyr strongholds at Satyrnaar and Xavian, along with demonic remnants at Demon Fall Canyon and Felfire Hill, taint the eastern forest.

subzone:north-gate-outpost.text: North Gate Outpost. Mountaineers guard the road through North Gate Outpost, where Dun Morogh meets Loch Modan. Their patrols keep travelers safe from the beasts in the crags. Dwarven mountaineers guard the road through North Gate Pass. From North Gate Outpost, they keep the route clear of prowling beasts and watch travelers heading through the mountain tunnels into Loch Modan. The pass is Dun Morogh’s northeastern threshold, but its harsh weather and steep ravines make patrols dangerous. When a patrol goes missing or a predator threatens the road, the garrison calls on travelers to scout the surrounding ridges.

subzone:north-gate-pass.text: North Gate Pass. North Gate Pass carries travelers between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan through the Khaz Modan peaks. A fortified dwarven outpost watches this northern corridor, used by travelers bound for the Wetlands. North Gate Pass cuts through Khaz Modan between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. From the west, travelers emerge from steep mountain tunnels into the broad loch valley. Roads lead down toward the Wetlands, bringing dwarven messengers, merchants, and wandering adventurers through the pass. North Gate Outpost gives the route its strategic value, with mountaineers watching for troggs and mountain predators.

subzone:northshire-valley.text: Northshire Valley. Northshire Valley shelters Stormwind's newest defenders in northern Elwynn Forest. Natural barriers guard the peaceful valley, where ancient Northshire Abbey, fertile vineyards, and the rich Echo Ridge Mine sustain a pocket of the kingdom. Bandits, kobolds, and displaced predators now trouble its quiet pastures. Northshire Valley lies behind mountain ridges, with one road south through a fortified gatehouse toward Goldshire and the rest of Elwynn Forest. A clear river crosses the pastures and flows into Crystal Lake. At the valley's heart, ancient Northshire Abbey teaches the Holy Light and trains recruits under the Knights of the Silver Hand and seasoned veterans. Beyond its walls, the fertile Northshire Vineyards and Echo Ridge Mine make this a self-sustaining pocket of Stormwind territory, far from the wars beyond its ridges. Stormwind's overextended defenses have strained even this sheltered valley. Marshal McBride and his detachment of the Stormwind Guard struggle to maintain order across it. Wolves driven north from blighted Duskwood prowl the woods, while kobolds have overrun Echo Ridge Mine's tunnels. Masked thugs aligned with the Defias Brotherhood harass the vineyards and threaten the abbey grounds, so local commanders recruit every able-bodied civilian who arrives at the gates.

subzone:northshire-vineyards.text: Northshire Vineyards. At Northshire Vineyards, Defias brigands have seized the fields east of Northshire Abbey. The grapes once supplied wine to the clerics, but now the thieves plunder the harvest and threaten local farmers. Northshire Vineyards lie east across the stream from Northshire Abbey, where workers such as Milly Osworth once tended the fields. Defias Brotherhood brigands now hold the acreage, led by Garrick Padfoot. The thieves plunder the harvest and strip local farmers of their livelihood. Their occupation gives new Brotherhood recruits a foothold close to the abbey.

subzone:old-ironforge.text: Old Ironforge. Old Ironforge, also called the Assembly of Thanes, is an ancient subterranean chamber lying directly beneath the High Seat of Ironforge. Carved deep into the mountain's roots above glowing magma veins, it represents the ancestral heart of the dwarven capital. In the present day, its heavy access gates in the royal throne room remain sealed and vigilantly guarded. Beneath King Magni Bronzebeard's throne in the High Seat rests the cavernous hall known as Old Ironforge or the Assembly of Thanes. Deep inside these fiery subterranean foundations, winding stone bridges cross pools of subterranean lava. Long before the bustling halls of the Great Forge and the Commons echoed with modern dwarven commerce, early thanes gathered in these cavernous depths to deliberate and govern the mountain kingdom. Currently, entrance to Old Ironforge from the throne room is securely barred. The Ironforge royal guard keeps strict watch over the thresholds leading down into the old vaults.

subzone:old-town.text: Old Town. In Old Town, soldiers train beside weathered tenements and crowded alleys. The quarter largely survived the First War and remains home to Stormwind’s military Command Center and the covert headquarters of SI:7. Old Town keeps much of the shape of Stormwind before the First War. While the Stonemasons rebuilt the rest of the city from the ground up, this quarter escaped total ruin. It never gained the pristine marble facades and grand canals found in the Trade District and Cathedral Square. Working folk, laborers, and the city’s poorest residents live among its crowded tenements. Its cobbled streets are narrower, dirtier, and more chaotic than those elsewhere in the capital, preserving the feel of the old kingdom. Old Town holds Stormwind’s military officers, barracks, and combat trainers in the Command Center. Nearby, the Champions’ Hall gathers the Alliance’s finest warriors. At the district’s edge, SI:7 keeps its covert compound under the leadership of Master Mathias Shaw. Off-duty footmen and shadowy operatives meet at the Pig and Whistle Tavern, one of the city’s liveliest watering holes.

subzone:oracle-glade.text: Oracle Glade. Bloodfeather harpies harry Oracle Glade in northwestern Teldrassil. The sacred woodland holds the ancient Oracle Tree and Teldrassil’s first and most potent moonwell. Between Darnassus and Wellspring Lake, the Oracle Glade shelters a place of communion with nature. At its heart stands the ancient Oracle Tree, magically nurtured, its great boughs shaped like an eagle perched atop a bear. Nearby lies the first and most potent of Teldrassil’s sacred moonwells, bright with Elune’s grace. The Circle of the Ancients and the Oracle Tree watch over the island boughs. The tree sheds bark marked with messages for Archdruid Fandral Staghelm about the World Tree’s health. Bloodfeather harpies have made roosts in the glade’s high branches. The aggressive avian scavengers threaten the sacred tree and harass traveling druids, disturbing the moonwell’s quiet. Sentinels from Darnassus struggle to drive them out. As you pass through the northern boughs, tread carefully; harpies strike swiftly near their roosts.

subzone:park.text: Park. In Stormwind's western edge, Park offers visiting night elves a haven amid the stone city. It lies between Cathedral Square and the Mage Quarter, with greenery and quiet for rest. Druid trainers here are the only ones in the Eastern Kingdoms. Stormwind's Park brings a quiet stretch of wilderness into the stone capital. Once a place for the city's people to seek recreation, it became an enclave for night elf emissaries and travelers from across the Great Sea. Shaded canopies shelter the district, and a central Moonwell stands amid its grounds. The grove offers a glimpse of Kalimdor's sacred glades in the heart of the human kingdom. Night elves have a foothold in foreign lands within the Park. Kaldorei priests such as Nara Meideros tend visiting pilgrims, while druidic mentors guide those devoted to the wild. Weary travelers can also rest from the clatter of the Trade District and the solemn duties of the Cathedral.

subzone:petitioner-s-chamber.text: Petitioner's Chamber. Petitioners wait for the crown in a chamber just inside Stormwind Keep. Nobles, church dignitaries, and visiting subjects spend the time mingling, drinking, or awaiting an audience. The Petitioner's Chamber lies just to the right as you enter Stormwind Keep. Count Remington Ridgewell and Bishop DeLavey wait there for audiences with boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Between formal visits, the chamber gives nobles and clergy room to mingle, trade gossip, and quietly press their concerns. Who holds influence in the realm can often be seen in who speaks with whom.

subzone:pig-and-whistle-tavern.text: Pig and Whistle Tavern. In Stormwind City's Old Town, the Pig and Whistle Tavern welcomes travelers and local laborers. Veterans gather there to remember the kingdom's past conflicts. In Old Town's winding alleys, the Pig and Whistle Tavern offers warmth, ale, and lodging. Common citizens, working folk, and travelers fresh from the road gather there. Merchants such as recipe vendor Kendor Kabonka share the room with grizzled veterans, who trade memories of the First and Second Wars over their tankards.

subzone:pool-of-ask-ar.text: Pool of Ask'ar. Naga invaders and aquatic beasts crowd the Pool of Ask'ar, deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Its submerged halls hold night elven stonework and passages into the corrupted sanctuary. Past the Drowned Sacellum, cold, murky water fills the Pool of Ask'ar beneath a vast cavern vault. Oversized snapping turtles and deep-sea crabs nest among natural caverns and ancient stonework, watched over by Ghamoo-ra, an enormous ancient chelonian. Naga have seized the temple and use this flooded threshold to guard the approaches leading deeper into the complex, toward Lady Sarevess and the Moonshrine Ruins. The Pool of Ask'ar hides relics from the shrine's past before the Sundering, beyond its dangerous creatures and naga patrols. Submerged ledges and hidden alcoves along the cavern's edges hold lost artifacts, including the Lorgalis Manuscript sought by Gerrig Bonegrip, a dwarven scholar from Ironforge. Swim through the flooded southern passages to reach dry tunnels guarded by vile murlocs and Old God cultists. The pool remains a vital waterway through Blackfathom Deeps.

subzone:pools-of-arlithrien.text: Pools of Arlithrien. South of Darnassus, the Pools of Arlithrien have grown dangerous and neglected. Their moonwell once drew night elves to a quiet sanctuary, but beasts and nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs now threaten the springs. The Pools of Arlithrien lie beneath Teldrassil’s shaded boughs, south of Darnassus. A stone moonwell rests at their heart, holding waters touched by Elune’s grace. Though the sanctuary lies near the night elven capital, danger has driven the night elves to leave it untended. Agitated beasts roam the shallows, and the Gnarlpine furbolgs nearby remain hostile. What was meant to be a peaceful retreat now reflects the growing troubles across the island.

subzone:raven-hill.text: Raven Hill. In western Duskwood, Raven Hill lies in ruins beneath the shadow of its vast cemetery. Frightened squatters and invisible spirits are all that remain of the once lively human settlement. Raven Hill stands along Duskwood’s western road, just north of Addle’s Stead, a shell of its former self. When dark magic and undead horrors swept through the Grand Hamlet region, the living fled east toward Darkshire or left the territory. Now ruined timber homes decay beneath the gloom. Travelers avoid them, fearing restless dead from the neighboring cemetery and the invisible Unseen among the crumbling walls. Only a handful remain among Raven Hill’s ruins. Jitters, a nervous adventurer, hides in the abandoned structures, terrified of the horrors stalking the woods. In a dilapidated attic, the goblin Bliztik ekes out a solitary living by selling supplies to wary passersby. They share the ruins with the invisible spirits called the Unseen, at the edge of the sprawling burial grounds.

subzone:raven-hill-cemetery.text: Raven Hill Cemetery. At Raven Hill Cemetery, the dead rise from their graves in western Duskwood. The burial ground once served nearby hamlets, but now undead, spiders, and grave robbers roam among the tombs. Raven Hill Cemetery was once the burial ground for the settlements around the Dawning Wood. When dark sorceries fell upon the region, the dead began clawing out of their plots. Skeletons, ghouls, and shambling horrors now crowd the graveyard. Rotting abominations and giant spiders prowl among the tombs, while desperate grave robbers plunder ancestral crypts beyond the reach of local authorities. Raven Hill remains one of Duskwood's most dangerous places.

subzone:ravenholdt-manor.text: Ravenholdt Manor. Ravenholdt Manor watches over Hillsbrad from high in the mountains.
