Lord Jorach Ravenholdt leads its guild of thieves and assassins, where practitioners of stealth hone their craft beyond the authorities’ reach. Northwest of Durnholde Keep, a narrow pass and winding cave lead to Ravenholdt Manor. The estate stands isolated on the borderlands of the Alterac Mountains, and belongs to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. He keeps a disciplined enclave of rogues, assassins, and intelligence operatives. A tranquil garden and outdoor training arena give them space to practice lockpicking, poison-crafting, and close-quarters combat under martial experts like Master Kang. Those with a talent for skullduggery are welcome, but watchful sentries greet clumsy outsiders and unwanted visitors with cold suspicion. Before the First War, the land around Ravenholdt Manor belonged to the kingdom of Alterac, a past recalled by the manor’s weathered orange roof tiles. After Alterac fell, its displaced nobles in the Syndicate sought control of the region, bringing them into conflict with Ravenholdt. Jorach’s followers fight across Hillsbrad and Alterac to preserve their sovereign haven.

subzone:raynewood-retreat.text: Raynewood Retreat. Raynewood Retreat watches the northern approaches to Felwood from a great tree in Ashenvale. Dryads and Cenarion protectors guard the outpost, where Keeper Ordanus makes his home. At Raynewood Retreat, the great tree rises between Shael'dryn's moonwell and the satyr-infested ruins of Night Run. Cenarion Protectors, faerie dragons, and Laughing Sisters guard the outpost. Their watch turns north, toward the taint spreading from Felwood.

subzone:razorfen-downs.text: Razorfen Downs. Razorfen Downs is the ancestral capital and sacred burial labyrinth of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal brambles bordering the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. Once their holiest sanctuary, it has fallen under the sway of the undead Scourge, transforming into a festering bastion of necromancy. Long revered as the ancestral capital city and burial grounds of the quilboar race, Razorfen Downs rests within the colossal petrified briars sprung from the fallen demigod Agamaggan. Legend holds that its arched entryway was carved directly from the Great Boar's very maw. For centuries, the high priests of the Death's Head tribe tended these deep, winding burrows and honored their revered dead. Yet despite its sacred standing among the boar-folk, the maze of bone and bramble has recently suffered a catastrophe far darker than any squabble over Barrens water.

subzone:remtravel-s-excavation.text: Remtravel's Excavation. At Remtravel's Excavation, Prospector Remtravel's dig has broken into ancient ruins. Prospector Remtravel came to southern Darkshore seeking relics from the distant past. He established a large dig far from Auberdine's safety. As his team cut through ancient layers of earth, they uncovered Gravelflint troggs and hulking stone golems buried below. The creatures overran the quarry, scattering the miners. Remtravel now scrambles to recover his most promising finds.

subzone:render-s-rock.text: Render's Rock. Blackrock orcs hold Render's Rock above Redridge, near the pass to the Burning Steppes. From this cave, they prepare attacks on the valleys below. North of Lakeshire, Blackrock orcs guard a cave cut into the Redridge heights. The stronghold lies near the mountain pass leading to the Burning Steppes, where veteran orcs direct attacks against Redridge's defenders. Their guards make any attempt to enter perilous, whether to disrupt the orcs' supply lines or recover captives lost in the fighting.

subzone:render-s-valley.text: Render's Valley. Blackrock orcs hold a small camp in the southeastern Redridge Mountains at Render's Valley. It threatens nearby travelers and keeps captives taken from surrounding lands. Render's Valley lies among rocky ridges southeast of Lake Everstill, where Blackrock orcs keep an auxiliary camp for their operations in Redridge. Unlike the fortified keeps and stone towers on the northern cliffs, this camp gathers around war tents, banners, and sentry posts. Its warriors are smaller in number and less armed than the clan's core forces, but they still raid local roads and harass travelers. Captured prisoners remain in crude cages under guard. Scouts who reach Render's Valley find unexpected points of interest beyond the war parties roaming its dirt paths. Human prisoners have been seen in the camp, including a servant connected to the Tower of Azora who traded specialist goods under his captors' noses. Unmarked paths cross the high southern bluffs behind the valley, letting daring travelers slip into the murky bogs of the Swamp of Sorrows.

subzone:rethban-caverns.text: Rethban Caverns. Rethban Caverns wind through the northwestern cliffs of the Redridge Mountains. Aggressive Redridge gnolls infest this extensive cave system, the only source of uncommon Rethban ore. Deep in the northwestern mountains above Lake Everstill, Rethban Caverns shelter the local gnolls as a fortified redoubt. Their cunning leader, Ardo Dirtpaw, commands a pack that fiercely guards the twisting passages and chambers below. Wanderers who stray too close to the hillside entrance face attack. Rethban ore is a distinct mineral found in these winding, dangerous tunnels and carried by the Dirtpaw pack. Blacksmiths and researchers in Lakeshire often send travelers into the caverns to recover samples of this rare mountain ore.

subzone:ridgepoint-tower.text: Ridgepoint Tower. Stormwind guards watch the eastern frontier from Ridgepoint Tower. They keep vigil over the perilous corridors, valleys, and roads leading into neighboring wilderness. At Ridgepoint Tower, the garrison watches the valleys and roads of eastern Elwynn. The tower stands on high ground, where Stormwind's authority reaches its eastern border and the wilds begin. Its guards keep watch over the routes before threats can reach the farms and settlements nearer Northshire and Goldshire. Ridgepoint Tower faces threats from several directions. East lie the Redridge Mountains, where aggressive gnoll packs and blackrock orc raiders test human defenses. Across the southern river, undead horrors prowl the timberline of Duskwood. Rogue Defias Brotherhood bandits also haunt nearby wilderness camps, looking for gaps in the guard's defenses.

subzone:roland-s-doom.text: Roland's Doom. Nightbane worgen hold Roland's Doom, east of the Rotting Orchard in southeastern Duskwood. The mine is abandoned, and its tunnels are a dangerous den. Roland's Doom lies in the ridges east of the Rotting Orchard, where the mine has long stood idle. Nightbane worgen now use its tunnels as a staging ground, under leaders such as Gutspill and Nefaru. Snarls carry through the dark shafts, and the damp earth is stained with blood. Travelers who enter face one of Duskwood's most perilous places.

subzone:rotting-orchard.text: Rotting Orchard. Rotting Orchard lies in southern Duskwood, where ravenous lupine predators of the Nightbane pack have overrun the abandoned grove. Once it supplied fruit to nearby Darkshire, but now its trees and buildings lie in ruin. In the Rotting Orchard, Nightbane worgen have made camps among the ruined barns and outbuildings. The orchard lies east of the ruined Yorgen Farmstead and west of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Withered fruit hangs from its trees, and Nightbane Stalkers prowl the twisted brush. Nightbane Shadow Weavers practice their dark magic among the decaying timber. The fierce worgen Gutspill and Nefaru lead the pack from their lair in the nearby mine of Roland's Doom.

subzone:royal-gallery.text: Royal Gallery. Stormwind Keep's Royal Gallery honors figures from the kingdom's history and the Grand Alliance. Past the courtyard garden, its statues and works of art fill a quiet hall of remembrance. The Royal Gallery lies beyond Stormwind Keep's interior garden, beside the Royal Library. Its statues honor King Llane Wrynn, the fallen ruler of Stormwind; Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras; and Lady Mara Fordragon, patron of the refugees who fled to Lordaeron after the First War. Courtly visitors such as Lady Dena Kennedy come to this quiet hall, where the kingdom's noble heritage is remembered.

subzone:royal-library.text: Royal Library. Scholars come to the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep for the kingdom’s records and histories. Head Librarian Milton Sheaf watches over its scrolls and treatises, from ancient wars to accounts of realms beyond the sea. The Royal Library offers quiet among Stormwind Keep’s guarded halls and courtly intrigues. Milton Sheaf oversees its shelves of southern human history, from surviving texts written before the First War to recent military chronicles and recovered tomes. Alliance scholars, priests, and travelers may browse its treatises. They cover the founding of the Alliance of Lordaeron and the recent arrival of Thrall’s Horde in Kalimdor.

subzone:ruins-of-mathystra.text: Ruins of Mathystra. Stormscale naga guard Mathystra's broken halls along Darkshore's northern coast. Ghost Sabers stalk the ruins of the ancient night elven city, shattered during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Mathystra once housed high-ranking Highborne nobility on Darkshore's northern coast. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, great waves shattered the city, toppled its marble arches, and swept much of its stonework into the sea. The surviving night elves left for smaller woodland villages farther south. Sunken courtyards and cracked foundations remain, battered by the coast. Stormscale naga guard Mathystra's broken halls, driving away travelers who venture north past the Tower of Althalaxx. Ancient Highborne relics lie half-buried among the flagstones, sand, and seafoam. Young night elves sometimes brave the naga to recover remnants of their heritage, while spectral Ghost Sabers stalk the broken streets.

subzone:ruins-of-ordil-aran.text: Ruins of Ordil'Aran. In northwestern Ashenvale, the Ruins of Ordil'Aran lie between Maestra's Post and Bathran's Haunt. Thistlefur furbolgs have overrun the ancient night elf settlement, once a hidden refuge for shadow cultists. Weathered pillars and cracked arches are all that remain of Ordil'Aran's Kaldorei buildings. The Cult of the Dark Strand once hid among the stones, ambushing travelers on Ashenvale's northwestern paths. Recently, Thistlefur furbolgs drove the cultists out in a bloody takeover. Fallen Dark Strand practitioners still litter the ground, while the furbolgs patrol the perimeter and guard the ancient Heartswood tree within the ruins.

subzone:ruins-of-stardust.text: Ruins of Stardust. On an island south of Astranaar, the Ruins of Stardust lie under Felwood's spreading corruption. Bog beasts prowl the fallen sanctuary, but stardust shrubs still grow among its stones with healing power. South of Astranaar, you find the Ruins of Stardust on a solitary island. The night elves once held this holy place in reverence. Now a sickly yellow-green hue clouds the water, stained by demonic rot draining south from Felwood, as at nearby Iris Lake. Local plant life has twisted into hostile bog beasts. They prowl the fallen masonry, their temperaments warped by the tainted lake. Stardust shrubs still bloom among the ruins, untouched by the corruption in the soil and along the shore. Their leaves and blossoms can cleanse and heal. Shamans, herbalists, and local night elf defenders seek them for remedies against Ashenvale's encroaching decay.

subzone:rut-theran-village.text: Rut'theran Village. At Teldrassil's southern shore, Rut'theran Village links Darnassus to Kalimdor by sea and sky. Ferries and hippogryphs carry travelers between the World Tree and the mainland. Rut'theran Village meets the water below Teldrassil's towering heights. Darnassus rests in the boughs above, while the village handles its needs beyond the tree. A mystical portal beneath the trees carries travelers between the shore and Darnassus in an instant. Ferries leave the docks for Auberdine on the mainland coast of Darkshore, and flight masters tend roosts of trained hippogryphs.

subzone:saldean-s-farm.text: Saldean's Farm. At Saldean's Farm, the Saldeans hold Westfall's only homestead not completely overrun and abandoned to the Defias Brotherhood. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma keep the farmhouse as a rare safe haven amid the region's turmoil. The Saldean family stayed on their soil as neighboring lands fell to banditry and mechanical sabotage. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma still offer hot food and a kind word to travelers. Rogue harvest golems deployed across the plains plague their fields, so the family keeps close to the farmhouse walls. Stormwind's crown has largely neglected Westfall, leaving law enforcement thin. A handful of Sentinel Hill and Stormwind guards patrol the periphery, but the Saldeans rely chiefly on their own grit and help from passing travelers. Salma's famous Westfall stew and goretusk liver pie, and the shelter of the farmhouse, offer small comforts against the Defias threat.

subzone:satyrnaar.text: Satyrnaar. Satyrnaar lies in ruin under the Bleakheart satyrs in northeastern Ashenvale. The ancient night elf settlement sits beside the road from Splintertree Post toward Azshara, intact enough to be one of the forest’s easiest satyr strongholds to reach. You find Satyrnaar northeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of Forest Song, among Ashenvale’s three chief satyr settlements with Xavian and Night Run. Its elven buildings remain more intact than those deep in the wilderness, though tents now stand among the broken stone. The Bleakheart satyrs occupy the camp, making the trade road east toward Azshara dangerous for travelers. They have also allied with the Cult of the Dark Strand, whose soulgem lies among the corrupted stones.

subzone:scarlet-raven-tavern.text: Scarlet Raven Tavern. In Darkshire, the Scarlet Raven Tavern is the town’s primary inn and social center. Tavernkeep Smitts welcomes beleaguered locals, passing adventurers, and frightened travelers seeking shelter from the horrors beyond town. At the Scarlet Raven Tavern, the hearth burns in the heart of Darkshire as eternal dusk hangs over the forest. Years ago, it was a busy stop where Marshal Haggard and the Stormwind Guard shared pints after patrols. Since then, business has withered alongside the town’s security. Tavernkeep Smitts tends the bar for a somber, anxious crowd huddled against cold and fear. The inn remains a crossroads for rumors and a starting point for travelers seeking answers to the dark phenomena consuming the region.

subzone:sentinel-hill.text: Sentinel Hill. In Westfall, Sentinel Hill remains the Alliance's main stronghold and the People's Militia's command post. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and hostile outlaws surround the rise, the only secure foothold for lawful citizens in the region. Sentinel Hill rises above central Westfall, with a barracks-style inn, a gryphon roost linking travelers to Stormwind and beyond, a forge, and a lumber mill around Sentinel Tower. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and outlaws crowd the surrounding land. The encampment keeps a fragile perimeter where travelers, beleaguered farmers, and recruits can regroup under the watchful eyes of veteran defenders. With the royal army detained in Stormwind and unable to spare soldiers for outlying territories, Gryan Stoutmantle established the People's Militia on Sentinel Hill. Volunteer fighters organize scouts, coordinate strikes against the Riverpaw gnolls, and investigate the organized banditry tearing through Westfall's abandoned farmsteads. The camp is neither an opulent fort nor a comfortable refuge; it is a working frontline camp determined to reclaim the kingdom's former breadbasket.

subzone:sentinel-tower.text: Sentinel Tower. Defenders watch Westfall from Sentinel Tower atop Sentinel Hill. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia organize resistance against bandits, gnolls, and the Defias Brotherhood. Sentinel Tower rises above the unsettled plains of Westfall. With Stormwind's official army largely absent and aid withheld, local volunteers and veterans joined together around this central stronghold. From its stone heights, lookouts can see across the dusty plains, from abandoned pumpkin patches to the misty shores. They watch for highwaymen and gnoll raiding parties moving through the region. Gryan Stoutmantle and the local leadership direct the militia from Sentinel Tower. Makeshift defenses surround the stronghold, where wounded refugees and weary soldiers gather, and homesteaders driven from their lands find emergency shelter. Militia members piece together reports about the Defias Brotherhood and organize volunteers into strikes against the syndicate that has brought Westfall to ruin.

subzone:shadowthread-cave.text: Shadowthread Cave. Shadowthread Cave lies beneath the northwest cliffs of Shadowglen, where its spiders have grown dangerous. Their brood now threatens young kaldorei near Aldrassil. Shadowthread Cave opens in Shadowglen’s shaded northwest, a lair for Teldrassil’s giant spiders. In earlier years, the spiders lived quietly alongside the World Tree’s young boughs. Now they guard their territory fiercely. Webwood silk chokes the stone corridors, and the brood threatens young kaldorei venturing beyond Aldrassil. Githyiss the Vile rules the deepest recesses of Shadowthread Cave. The monstrous broodmother is far more ferocious than the common webwood crawlers. Young night elf sentinels and druids go into the cave to curb the infestation and slay Githyiss, keeping the corruption touching Teldrassil’s wildlife from overrunning Shadowglen’s sanctuary.

subzone:shimmer-ridge.text: Shimmer Ridge. Frostmane trolls hold Shimmer Ridge in northern Dun Morogh, west of the Gates of Ironforge. Its two camps span a chasm, and the ridge is the only place shimmerweed grows. Frostmane trolls hold the high ground west of Ironforge's gates. Two camps sit on opposite sides of a chasm, joined by a wooden bridge. Troll scavengers and their tamed mountain boars guard the camps. The ridge lies near the main road and the dwarven capital, so travelers and mountain patrols face raids from above. Frostmane trolls grow shimmerweed on the ridge. Dwarven brewmasters prize the plant for potent, flavorful highland ales, and it cannot easily be gathered elsewhere. Mountaineers and young recruits brave troll ambushes and tusked beasts to gather it from the trolls' plots.

subzone:shimmering-flats.text: Shimmering Flats. The Shimmering Flats is an expansive salt flat lying at the southeastern tip of Thousand Needles, bordering the desert of Tanaris. Once the bed of an ancient lake, this sun-baked expanse is now famous for the high-speed mechanical rivalries of the Mirage Raceway and a harsh population of desert beasts. Stretching out under the blinding southern sun, the Shimmering Flats is a vast dried lakebed devoid of vegetation, dotted with the sun-bleached bones of turtles and even the wooden wreck of an ancient sailing vessel. Its sheer, unbroken level surface makes it the premier testing ground on Kalimdor for experimental vehicles. At the center of the flats lies the Mirage Raceway, where gnome and goblin tinkerers constantly clash to see whose rocket cars, gyrocopters, and engines can achieve the highest speeds—often resulting in fiery crashes and smoking craters across the white crust. Beyond the roaring engines of the raceway, the basin is far from peaceful. Hardened basilisks, aggressive scorpids, and circling vultures prey upon anything that slows down on the open expanse. Further south, the ground grows treacherous around the Rustmaul Dig Site. Originally excavated by dwarven prospectors before being contested by the Horde, the quarry was entirely abandoned when picks cracked into subterranean tunnels, unleashing a swarm of vicious silithid into the southern edge of the flats.

subzone:shrine-of-aessina.text: Shrine of Aessina. At the Shrine of Aessina, night elves honor an ancient spirit of nature and wild creatures. The sacred place lies in southwestern Ashenvale, between Maestra's Post and Astranaar, amid growing border friction. West of Astranaar, the Shrine of Aessina honors a Wild God who embodies the heart and spirit of the deep forests. For generations, night elves and their woodland kin have revered this quiet place and communed with nature away from the main roads. The Horde is pushing into Ashenvale to gather timber and establish footholds, and sacred grounds across the territory face an uncertain peace.

subzone:si-7-stormwind-city.text: SI:7 (Stormwind City). Tucked away in the eastern corner of Old Town, this unassuming stone manor houses the headquarters of SI:7, the kingdom of Stormwind's elite intelligence and espionage service. Behind its heavy doors, spymaster Master Mathias Shaw and his senior operatives quietly monitor threats to the realm, coordinating undercover agents across the kingdom. To the casual passerby in Old Town, this fortified stone structure looks little different from a standard manor or military barracks. In truth, it serves as the nerve center for Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7. Directed by Master Mathias Shaw, SI:7 gathers intelligence, conducts surveillance, and executes covert operations to protect the kingdom from subversion. While the city guard patrols the open cobblestones and the Royal Guard defends Stormwind Keep, SI:7 works in the margins, training handlers and dispatching stealthy operatives against foreign enemies, saboteurs, and domestic unrest alike.

subzone:silver-stream-mine.text: Silver Stream Mine. In northern Loch Modan, Silver Stream Mine lies between Algaz Station and the Stonewrought Dam, its silver veins exhausted. The Miners' League made the hollow a supply depot, but Tunnel Rat kobolds now occupy its tunnels and hoard stolen equipment and rare minerals. Silver Stream Mine once yielded rich silver for Ironforge. Dwarf miners dug until the main veins ran dry, leaving broad underground chambers. The Miners' League kept the hard-won shafts in use as a guarded storehouse for tools, mining crates, and regional equipment. The mine is also the only known source of Charged Rift Gems, which draw arcanists seeking delicate tailoring reagents. Tunnel Rat kobolds came in large numbers and drove the Miners' League caretakers out into the cold of Loch Modan. Now the kobolds guard the stolen dwarf crates with manic fervor. Outside the rear entrances, shattered orcish catapults and wagons lie forgotten, reminders of older frontier skirmishes.

subzone:silverwind-refuge.text: Silverwind Refuge. Silverwind Refuge shelters travelers in south-central Ashenvale, just north of Mystral Lake. Sentinels guard this night elven settlement along the forest trails. Silverwind Refuge rests between Mystral Lake and Iris Lake, to the north. Alongside Astranaar, it is one of central Ashenvale’s major night elven waystations. Craftsmen and wilderness trainers teach herbalism, alchemy, skinning, and hunting. Sentinels guard the refuge, where allies traveling through the ancient woods can rest.

subzone:silverwing-grove.text: Silverwing Grove. Silverwing Sentinels gather at Silverwing Grove in south-central Ashenvale, near Fallen Sky Lake. From this fortified hollow, night elf warriors muster Alliance forces against the Warsong Clan loggers cutting through the forest. At Silverwing Grove, Silverwing Sentinels gather beneath the canopy southwest of Silverwing Outpost. The night elves use the post to oppose the Horde's lumbering in Warsong Gulch. Alliance officers, provisions, and scouts assemble here to organize skirmishes and muster champions. They defend Ashenvale against orcish expansion.

subzone:silverwing-outpost.text: Silverwing Outpost. Silverwing Outpost guards the eastern bank of the Falfarren River in south-central Ashenvale. Duriel Moonfire commands the garrison, the Alliance's easternmost hold against the Horde in the contested woodland. Silverwing Outpost lies southwest of Splintertree Post and just north of the Barrens border. Its place on the eastern bank of the Falfarren River puts it in territory the Horde contests and patrols. From here, the garrison shields night elf holdings deeper in the forest. Duriel Moonfire and her Silverwing Sentinels face constant attacks from nearby orcs seeking to drive night elf forces from the area.

subzone:sishir-canyon.text: Sishir Canyon. Sishir Canyon runs east through the Stonetalon Mountains, crowded with Deepmoss spiders. Webs choke the gorge on the dangerous approach to the Ruins of Eldre'thar, where travelers face venomous spiders and their matriarch. Sishir Canyon cuts through the Stonetalon Mountains toward the ancient Ruins of Eldre'thar. Deepmoss spiders have overrun the gorge, covering its stone floor and walls with sheets of web and clusters of egg sacs. Travelers and sentinels heading for the night elven ruins must fight their way through swarms of aggressive webspinners. Besseleth lurks in the deepest recess of Sishir Canyon as matriarch of the Deepmoss brood. Her great size and venom make her a danger to anyone trying to secure the pass. Local forces in Stonetalon keep watch and warn travelers that the webbed depths hold more than scattered spiders: Besseleth fiercely guards her brood.

subzone:slaughtered-lamb.text: Slaughtered Lamb. Tucked away in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, the Slaughtered Lamb appears to be nothing more than a quiet, seedy tavern. Beneath its floorboards, however, sprawling catacombs hide the sanctum and training grounds of the Alliance's illicit warlocks. On the surface, the Slaughtered Lamb offers little more than dark corners and sparse patronage, attended by barkeep Jarel Moor, who warns casual visitors to stay away from the shadows. That warning is literal. Descending through the back passages reveals a subterranean complex of crypts and summoning circles, where human warlocks and transfer practitioners from Khaz Modan openly study fel arcana sheltered from the disapproving eyes of the Church of the Holy Light and the Kirin Tor.

subzone:south-gate-outpost.text: South Gate Outpost. Travelers stream through South Gate Outpost, a fortified post on the pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Its mountaineers guard the southern road between Ironforge's frigid heights and the Loch's temperate valley. South Gate Outpost marks the frontier between Dun Morogh's snowy slopes and Loch Modan's basin. Ironforge mountaineers patrol the rocky switchbacks and keep dangerous wildlife off the main highway. Unlike their hard-pressed kin at North Gate Outpost, these defenders have largely secured their stretch of road. Travelers, pilgrims, and trade wagons can journey toward Thelsamar in relative safety.

subzone:south-gate-pass.text: South Gate Pass. South Gate Pass carries travelers between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Its guarded road links Ironforge with Thelsamar. South Gate Pass cuts through the Khaz Modan range, joining the high mountains of Dun Morogh to Loch Modan's valley in the east. Stone archways mark the way from the cold slopes into the warmer dwarven heartlands. The road leads toward Thelsamar, carrying mountaineers, couriers, and newly trained adventurers setting out from the capital. Dwarven mountaineers keep watch at South Gate Outpost, guarding the pass against wild beasts and prowling troggs. The road is safer than the untamed parts of the valley, but hostile wildlife and roving threats still test its approaches. Travelers are advised to stay on the road.

subzone:southshore.text: Southshore. Southshore is a coastal human port in the Hillsbrad Foothills and one of the Alliance's few surviving strongholds in fallen Lordaeron. Once a sleepy fishing village, it now stands as an embattled bastion facing constant hostility from the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill, rogue Syndicate bandits, and shoreline monsters. Southshore first rose to prominence during the First War when refugee boats carrying survivors from the fallen kingdom of Stormwind landed upon its beaches. Though contested and overrun during the Second War, it was rebuilt and later endured the horrors of the Third War. Today, while the rest of Lordaeron lies in ruins or under the rule of the Forsaken, Southshore remains fiercely loyal to the Grand Alliance. It offers shelter to displaced human survivors, veteran paladins of the Silver Hand, and scholars of the Kirin Tor. Despite its scenic docks, where the ship between Menethil Harbor and Auberdine calls, and its famous turtle bisque, life in Southshore is perilous. Led by Magistrate Henry Maleb and Marshal Redpath, the town struggles against relentless pressure. To the north, the Forsaken of Tarren Mill wage a bitter border conflict for dominance over Hillsbrad. Inland, the aristocratic outlaws of the Syndicate raid supply lines and assassinate local leaders, while ogres, murlocs, and naga constantly harass the town's borders.

subzone:splintertree-post.text: Splintertree Post. Splintertree Post holds the Horde’s eastern Ashenvale frontier, northwest of Felfire Hill. Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan established it during the Third War as a fortified base against the night elves and a staging ground for expansion. Splintertree Post anchors the Horde’s military and supply lines across eastern Ashenvale. Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan founded it when the orcs first entered the forest during the Third War. Orcish and tauren scouts and warriors still defend the armed outpost. An inn, a flight master, and steady supplies from Orgrimmar support the Horde’s contested hold beneath the trees. Splintertree Post remains ready for attack. The night elves have neither forgotten nor forgiven Grommash’s actions during the war. They also oppose the Horde’s continued logging and raids on Astranaar. Sentinels hide in the surrounding woods and launch constant retaliatory guerrilla strikes, testing the post’s watchmen at all hours.

subzone:splithoof-crag.text: Splithoof Crag. Splithoof Crag is a fortified settlement of the Galak centaur, tucked along the northern cliffs of Thousand Needles. It serves as one of the tribe's major enclaves alongside the high mesas, guarding the entrance to Splithoof Hold. Travelers traversing the canyon floor must contend with aggressive Galak patrols roaming near the bluffs. Nestled against the sheer northern rock face of Thousand Needles, Splithoof Crag sits just east of the towering Darkcloud Pinnacle. It is an established enclave of the Galak centaur, complete with crude tent encampments and dirt pathways cutting through the crags. At the heart of the village against the cliffside lies Splithoof Hold, a subterranean cavern holding the Cloven Hoof, an ancient relic of the centaur safeguarded by a sacred brazier. The Galak fiercely contest this corner of the canyon, clashing with any travelers, Horde expeditions, or tauren scouting parties wandering beneath their bluffs. While the Grimtotem occupy the soaring pinnacles nearby, the centaur hold firm control of this canyon ravine and the caverns burrowed deep beneath the stone.

subzone:splithoof-hold.text: Splithoof Hold. Splithoof Hold is a deep cavern stronghold carved into the stone of Splithoof Crag in Thousand Needles. Held by the Galak centaur tribe, the cavern serves as a fortified den and houses the Ancient Brazier, a site holding an eternally burning sacred flame. Tucked away inside Splithoof Crag, Splithoof Hold serves as a fortified redoubt for the Galak centaur. Unlike the windswept canyon floor, this enclosed cave offers them shelter, defensible chokepoints, and a secure sanctuary from rival tribes and travelers passing through the Needles. Deep within the shadowed recesses of the hold lies an ancient brazier cradling the Sacred Flame. This mystic fire burns incessantly, serving as a focal point of power and ritual reverence for the centaur and an object of deep curiosity for spiritual wanderers across the canyon.

subzone:starbreeze-village.text: Starbreeze Village. Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Starbreeze Village, east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a quiet night elf hamlet, it now lies in ruins beneath the spreading corruption of the World Tree. Starbreeze Village lies southeast of Shadowglen, just down the road from Dolanaar. Peaceful night elf families once lived beneath Teldrassil’s boughs, but the village now lies in shambles. Aggressive Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun its wooden homes. Driven wild by corruption afflicting the World Tree’s boughs, they drove out the elven residents and fiercely defend the ruined grounds.

subzone:steelgrill-s-depot.text: Steelgrill's Depot. East of Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot keeps Alliance vehicles and machinery in working order. Beldin Steelgrill and his crew handle repairs, tinker supplies, and salvage efforts. Steelgrill's Depot rings with clanking metal, hissing steam vents, and the hum of experimental engines. Just off the snowy road east of Kharanos, dwarven miners and eccentric gnome engineers gather among heavy machinery, mechanized walking frames, and stockpiles of raw ores hauled from nearby quarries. Trogg disruptions and shortages of mechanical supplies trouble Dun Morogh. Beldin Steelgrill and his crew keep Alliance machinery in working order, making the depot an indispensable stop for travelers seeking spare parts or technical guidance in the bitter cold.

subzone:stendel-s-pond.text: Stendel's Pond. Gnolls prowl Stendel's Pond southwest of Sentinel Hill, where anglers still seek fresh fish. Southwest of Sentinel Hill, Stendel's Pond draws anglers despite the danger along its muddy banks. Gnolls roam nearby, and scattered skeletons with two lone graves show that the shore is perilous. The water may be foul, or the beasts may be to blame, but the cause is unknown. Schools of sagefish still bring anglers to the pond.

subzone:stone-cairn-lake.text: Stone Cairn Lake. At Stone Cairn Lake in northeastern Elwynn, hostile murlocs hold the southern shore and renegade wizards camp on the island. Heroes' Vigil honors those lost in the First War. Families and pilgrims once crossed the calm waters to honor the dead at Heroes' Vigil. The stone memorial was raised on the lake's central island to mark the heavy loss of human life in the First War against the Orcish Horde. Now renegade wizards have made camp beside the monument, and the island has become a hostile place. Aggressive murlocs have claimed the southern banks of Stone Cairn Lake. Their crude huts line the water, and they harass anyone who comes near. The hills and rocky outcrops around the lake hold rich mineral veins, drawing prospectors and miners despite the dangers along the shore.

subzone:stonefield-farm.text: Stonefield Farm. The Stonefield family works the fields in southern Elwynn Forest. Their long feud with the neighboring Maclures keeps the two households at odds. Stonefield Farm lies south of Goldshire, where the family grows crops for the realm. For decades, the Stonefields have quarreled with the nearby Maclure Vineyards. The households trade accusations of theft and trespassing, and even small disputes keep tensions high. Gramma Stonefield, Ma Stonefield, and young Tommy Joe Stonefield make their home here.

subzone:stonefire-tavern.text: Stonefire Tavern. Travelers gather at Stonefire Tavern in Ironforge’s Commons, just north of the city gates. The inn offers a hearth, dwarven ale, and a place to rest for those arriving from across Khaz Modan. Stonefire Tavern welcomes travelers in Ironforge’s Commons, just north of the fortress gates. Innkeeper Firebrew runs the inn with his daughter Gwenna. Weary wayfarers can find meals, local brews, and lodging beneath the mountain. Travelers come in from across the Alliance to rest from Dun Morogh’s mountain snows, trade tales, or gather supplies before exploring the city. Its hearth draws them together at the heart of the Commons.

subzone:stonesplinter-valley.text: Stonesplinter Valley. Stonesplinter troggs have fortified a mountain vale in southwestern Loch Modan. Their chieftain, Grawmug, leads the tribe from the valley. Stonesplinter Valley lies among the crags of southwestern Loch Modan. Troggs clawed up from underground across Khaz Modan, ending the quiet that once filled the hollow. The Stonesplinter tribe claimed the valley and carved crude defenses into its rocky passes, digging dens and raising barricades. They hunt anything that comes too close. Their numbers threaten the roads through southern Loch Modan, and Mountaineers from Thelsamar hire mercenaries to thin their ranks and bring down Grawmug, the towering warlord who leads them.

subzone:stonetalon-peak.text: Stonetalon Peak. At Stonetalon Peak, kaldorei Sentinels and druids keep watch over an ancient sanctuary. The sheltered valley is sacred to the night elves and remains the Alliance’s main foothold in the high mountains. Stonetalon Peak opens into a green valley high above the dry lower ranges. Its ruins reach back millennia, to temples that honored Queen Azshara before the Great Sundering. Night elven Sentinels and druids now care for the sanctuary. They keep a barrow den and an Alliance flight roost here. During the Third War, Jaina Proudmoore’s human expedition and Thrall’s Horde climbed Stonetalon Peak, each seeking the Oracle in the mountain’s deep caverns. Medivh’s visions had guided them there. Their encounter brought mortal enemies together, and they set aside their blades. That uneasy pact helped them stand against the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal. Sentinel patrols still guard the peak, while Horde incursions in the lowlands keep its defenders alert.

subzone:stonewatch.text: Stonewatch. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch above the approaches from the Burning Steppes, threatening Lakeshire. The fortress once guarded Redridge against northern invasions. Stonewatch overlooks the cliffs near Stonewatch Falls, where its tower and keep guard the approaches from the Burning Steppes. Lakeshire's defenders first held the fortress. Then Morganth, a rogue warlock, allied with the Blackrock clan. Dark magic helped the orcs overwhelm the 12th Sabre Regiment and seize the keep. Morganth later turned against his allies and withdrew to the nearby Tower of Ilgalar with an army of Shadowhide gnolls. The Blackrock orcs kept their hold under Warlord Gath'Ilzogg and Lieutenant Tharil'zun. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch, leaving Lakeshire exposed to conquest. Stormwind's House of Nobles has provided no substantial military reinforcements, whether through indifference or paralysis. Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have had to hire mercenaries and call for volunteers. Their best hope of lifting the threat over the region is to strike at the fortress's leaders, Tharil'zun and Gath'Ilzogg.

subzone:stonewatch-falls.text: Stonewatch Falls. At Stonewatch Falls, water pours from Lake Everstill into a pool claimed by murlocs. The falls lie beneath Stonewatch in the eastern Redridge Mountains. Stonewatch Falls rushes down the slope beneath Stonewatch, the Blackrock orc stronghold. Its water flows from Lake Everstill’s eastern river and gathers in a deep pool against the mountainside. Murlocs have claimed the shore, raising crude reed hovels and preying on travelers who come too close to the water.

subzone:stonewatch-keep.text: Stonewatch Keep. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch Keep in eastern Redridge Mountains, turning it against Lakeshire. The Kingdom of Stormwind built and manned the fortress before the invaders seized it as a base for their warlords. Stonewatch Keep once guarded the eastern ridges and the settlers of Lakeshire from hostile incursions. That changed when the renegade warlock Morganth allied with the Blackrock clan. Strengthened by dark magic, the orcs stormed the fortress and overcame its human defenders. After their victory, Morganth abandoned the Blackrock clan to raise the nearby Tower of Ilgalar and subjugate local gnolls. The invaders kept Stonewatch, turning a former Alliance bastion into a staging ground for assaults on the valley. A heavy garrison of Blackrock warriors holds Stonewatch Keep under the command of the orc warlord Gath'Ilzogg and his lieutenant, Tharil'zun. From the ramparts, they direct raids across Redridge and take prisoners, including Stormwind's Corporal Keeshan. Stormwind's forces are spread thin, leaving the kingdom unable to send a full regiment to reclaim the fortress. Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have hired mercenary champions to enter the stronghold and kill the Blackrock leaders before Lakeshire is overrun.

subzone:stonewatch-tower.text: Stonewatch Tower. Blackrock sentinels hold Stonewatch Tower in northeastern Redridge. Once Lakeshire's outpost, it now helps the clan watch the ridges and guard its mountain stronghold. Stonewatch Tower rises above Lake Everstill, guarding the high mountain passes. The Kingdom of Stormwind built it as a forward scout for Stonewatch Keep. From its heights, sentries watched the eastern ridges and warned Lakeshire of threats coming from the Burning Steppes. Warlord Gath'Ilzogg's Blackrock orcs swept down from the heights, overcame the human defenders, and seized the stronghold for their war effort. Blackrock sentinels now watch the tower, keeping Alliance scouts from reaching the fortress unnoticed.

subzone:stonewrought-dam.text: Stonewrought Dam. Waters gather behind Stonewrought Dam along Loch Modan’s northern rim. The dwarven barrier holds back the Loch and drains the Wetlands below into habitable marshes. Stonewrought Dam stretches across the canyon east of Dun Algaz, one of the great works of dwarven craft. Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright designed it and pioneered the stonewrought technique used to build it. By trapping water in the mountain basin, the dam doubled the Loch’s surface area and steadily lowered the waters to the north. The Wetlands emerged from a valley once completely flooded. Stonewrought Dam now serves Ironforge, though Dark Iron saboteurs from the southern mountains target it. After recent assaults and attempts to infiltrate the dam, Ironforge placed a garrison here under Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Guards and engineers patrol the masonry day and night. A breach could drain the Loch and unleash a devastating flood across the Wetlands below.

subzone:stormwind-gate.text: Stormwind Gate. At Stormwind Gate, sentries watch the road between Elwynn Forest and Stormwind City. The passage opens onto the Valley of Heroes, where the city’s stone monuments rise beyond the arch. Stormwind Gate guards the southern road from Elwynn Forest into the capital. The Stormwind City Guard watches from the stone portal, while patrols move between the outer arch and the Valley of Heroes. Unrest lingers in Elwynn, yet the massive iron and stone gates stay open. Travelers, merchants, and returning defenders pass through into the heart of the Alliance.

subzone:stormwind-keep.text: Stormwind Keep. Stormwind Keep stands high above the capital as the stone fortress and seat of power for the Kingdom of Stormwind. Rebuilt after its ruin in the First War, it currently houses the royal court of the young boy-king Anduin Wrynn and his regent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Perched upon a plateau overlooking the entire city, Stormwind Keep serves as both a palace and a military bastion. The original stronghold was burned to the ground by the Old Horde when King Llane was assassinated near the end of the First War. Raised anew upon the old foundations after the Alliance reclaimed the kingdom, the reconstructed keep houses not only the grand throne room and the War Room, but peaceful garden courtyards and the expansive Royal Library.

subzone:stormwind-stockade.text: Stormwind Stockade. Stormwind Stockade holds the city’s most dangerous prisoners beneath the canals near the Mage Quarter. A coordinated revolt has driven the guards from the lower cells, leaving the prison in chaos. Warden Thelwater oversees the Stockade, where Stormwind keeps cutthroats, Defias operatives, captured Blackrock orcs, and Dark Iron dwarves. Now a violent uprising led by the Defias conspirator Bazil Thredd has forced the guards from the lower cells. The prisoners roam freely through the corridors. Thelwater has managed to secure the entrance, but the revolt still threatens to reach the canals. He depends on adventurers to enter the prison and put down the uprising.

subzone:stormwind-stockade-classic.text: Stormwind Stockade (Classic). Prisoners now control the Stormwind Stockade beneath Stormwind City's canal district. A revolt has driven the guards from its halls. The Stockade lies off the canals between Old Town and the Mage Quarter, holding Stormwind's most dangerous prisoners. Warden Thelwater oversees the underground prison. Its inmates include Defias Brotherhood cutthroats, a Blackrock orc, an ogre, and a Dark Iron dwarf. Bazil Thredd recently led a coordinated riot that overwhelmed the garrison. The surviving guards fled, leaving the prisoners in control of the halls.

subzone:stoutlager-inn.text: Stoutlager Inn. In Thelsamar, Stoutlager Inn gives travelers a warm hearth and a place to gather in western Loch Modan. Stoutlager Inn anchors community life in western Loch Modan, within Thelsamar. Miners, mountaineers, and travelers between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands stop to trade rumors, find lodging, and share dwarven ale. Troggs and kobolds make the wilderness beyond Thelsamar more dangerous, while the inn’s stone walls and fires offer shelter.

subzone:strahnbrad.text: Strahnbrad. Strahnbrad is a ruined human settlement nestled in the northeastern heights of the Alterac Mountains, near the border of the Western Plaguelands. Once famous as the site of Prince Arthas Menethil's early defense against Blackrock orc raiders, the town has since fallen into decay and serves as a fortified stronghold for the criminal Syndicate. Originally a holding of the Kingdom of Alterac before being absorbed into Lordaeron following the Second War, Strahnbrad's misfortune began on the eve of the Third War. Blackrock clan orcs raided the settlement to take human sacrifices for the Burning Legion, leading Prince Arthas Menethil and the Knights of the Silver Hand to ride to its defense. Though Arthas drove the raiders away and slew their slave master, the town was heavily bloodied. When Lordaeron crumbled beneath the Scourge shortly thereafter, Strahnbrad was abandoned to the elements. Today, Strahnbrad has become a crucial operations hub for the Syndicate, the organization of displaced Alteraci nobility and outlaws plotting to reclaim their fallen realm. Patrolled by human rogues and brigands, its abandoned town hall and blacksmith now serve as hideouts and staging grounds. The Syndicate uses the ruined town to house supplies and captive labor, including unfortunate prisoners like the orc Gol'dir, whom Horde scouts from Tarren Mill actively seek to liberate.

subzone:sun-rock-retreat.text: Sun Rock Retreat. Atop the central Stonetalon peaks, Sun Rock Retreat shelters the Horde south of Mirkfallon Lake. Tauren hold the mountain sacred, while orcs and tauren use the settlement as a base and supply post. Sun Rock Retreat lies in a mountain basin south of Mirkfallon Lake, on ground the tauren have long held sacred. Ancient tradition says An'she, the Sun, kissed the peak above the village. For generations before the Horde came, tauren shamans and pilgrims traveled here for rites that crossed the mortal veil. They drew strength from the land's close bond with the spirit world. Orcs and tauren now hold Sun Rock Retreat as the Horde's chief base across the Stonetalon Mountains. Together they seek a secure foothold against hostile harpy broods, local night elf sentinels, and the Venture Company's industrial pillaging. Trade and flight routes link the retreat with Thunder Bluff, the Crossroads, and the borders of Ashenvale. The outpost offers shelter, provisions, and spiritual guidance to those who brave the crags.

subzone:talondeep-path.text: Talondeep Path. Talondeep Path cuts beneath the ridge between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. The quiet tunnel links the woods west of Mystral Lake to Windshear Crag. Talondeep Path runs beneath the ridge between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. The tunnel links the woods west of Mystral Lake to the northwestern reaches of Windshear Crag. Surface trails cross dangerous country, with predators and warring factions, but the passage is calm and has no hostile beasts or encampments. Twisting side pockets, crevices, and natural alcoves break up the rock. Above ground, faint traces of an old road remain along the peaks, where travelers once crossed before the sheltered route through the stone.

subzone:talondeep-vale.text: Talondeep Vale. In south-central Ashenvale, Talondeep Vale lies between familiar landmarks and the road to the mountains. Talondeep Vale lies beneath the trees of south-central Ashenvale. Silverwind Refuge stands to the east, and the Ruins of Stardust lie nearby. To the south, the land rises toward the Stonetalon Mountains. Travelers cross this wooded valley between the heart of Ashenvale and the high crags beyond.

subzone:tarren-mill.text: Tarren Mill. Tarren Mill holds the Horde's line in the northern Hillsbrad Foothills, beneath the Alterac Mountains. Once a peaceful human farming village, it is now a Forsaken outpost locked in conflict with Southshore to the south. Tarren Mill's fields and mill have fallen silent since the Third War. Before then, it was a thriving farming town loyal to Lordaeron. During the Second War, Alliance forces near the town freed captured high elven archers from orc encampments, securing Quel'Thalas's full commitment to the Alliance of Lordaeron. The town's living inhabitants are gone, replaced by the Forsaken. Its buildings are weathered, its fields barren, and its mill quiet. The Forsaken fortify Tarren Mill against mountain beasts, Syndicate outlaws, and Alliance skirmishers. Tarren Mill is the Horde's forward base in Hillsbrad. Southshore, the Alliance port, lies directly across from it, and the road between the towns has become a warzone. From Tarren Mill, Horde travelers push back against the human farmers and soldiers occupying Hillsbrad, coordinate strikes against dwarven excavators at Dun Garok, and secure the dangerous roads that climb into the snowy crags of the Alterac Mountains.

subzone:temple-gardens.text: Temple Gardens. Temple Gardens gather the waters and bridges at Darnassus's heart, with the city bank on their main island. The Temple of the Moon borders them to the south, and a glowing tree portal carries travelers to Teldrassil's base. Water and wooden bridges cross the center of Darnassus, linking the Temple Gardens' islets to the Cenarion Enclave in the north, the terraces to the east, and the Temple of the Moon to the south. Night elves tend the flowing waters and foliage, making a quiet place of rest for travelers and priestesses. The main island holds Darnassus's central vault and bank. On the western bank, a massive glowing pink tree portal carries travelers through the boughs to Rut'theran Village at Teldrassil's base. From there, the coastal docks and flight paths connect the World Tree to other destinations.

subzone:temple-of-the-moon.text: Temple of the Moon. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind guides her people from the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. The sanctuary is the seat of government on Teldrassil and home to the Sisterhood of Elune, whose priestesses tend a sacred moonwell. Built soon after the Third War, the Temple of the Moon rose as the night elves settled Teldrassil. It is among the largest stone structures made by modern kaldorei hands. Its marble came from quarries on the Kalimdor mainland and crossed the sea by magical means. At the heart of the temple, a broad moonwell rests beneath the statue of Haidene. Pilgrims come to worship and reflect beside its consecrated waters. The temple also holds Darnassus's highest seat of government, where High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind guides her people through a new age. The priestesses of the Sisterhood of Elune serve their goddess from the temple's terraces, in worship and in the field. Emissaries and dispatched sisters travel across northern Kalimdor to investigate threats or aid local sentinels. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, for example, makes inquiries along the Darkshore coastline. Novices and veteran priestesses gather beneath the starry vaulted ceiling to learn divine spellwork, tend the wounded, and guard the sanctum from outside corruption.

subzone:the-loch.text: The Loch. The Loch’s waters are held back by the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. The lake is the largest body of water on Khaz Modan and sustains the surrounding dwarven settlements. The Loch spans the center of Loch Modan, among the largest inland lakes in the known world. Only Lordamere Lake and Darrowmere Lake in the north rival its size. Its waters support local fishermen and give Thelsamar and nearby hunting lodges a peaceful setting. Aggressive threshadons and freshwater beasts prowl beneath the calm surface, making a swim across perilous. The Stonewrought Dam keeps The Loch in its tranquil state. This massive dwarven structure crosses the mountain cleft to the north and prevents the lake from flooding into the Wetlands below. Maintaining it is essential to preserving the valley’s ecosystem and keeping Khaz Modan secure.

subzone:thelsamar.text: Thelsamar. Thelsamar keeps watch over the western bluffs above Loch Modan's great lake. The town lies on the road between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands, offering shelter and trade while troggs and ogres press in nearby. Thelsamar gathers dwarven life in the valley beneath stout stone and timber roofs. Travelers find the Stoutlager Inn, a gryphon roost, crafting stations, and supply merchants. The town sits on the road from the South Gate Pass into Dun Morogh to the Algaz Pass toward the Wetlands, so travelers crossing the region pass through its doors. Threats close in on Thelsamar from several sides. Troggs pour from Stonesplinter Valley to the south, and bears and other predators haunt Grizzlepaw Ridge. Ironforge's regular forces are stretched thin across the realm, leaving the local magistrate and Mountaineers to depend on travelers and mercenaries to patrol the trade roads and drive back hostile forces.

subzone:thistlefur-hold.text: Thistlefur Hold. Corruption has turned the furbolgs of Thistlefur Hold against every outsider who draws near. Their cavern den lies at the northern end of Thistlefur Village in west-central Ashenvale. Thistlefur Hold lies at the northern end of Thistlefur Village, at the heart of the Thistlefur tribe's territory. Corruption has driven its furbolgs mad, and they attack travelers and neighbors who draw near. In the winding caverns, the tribe hoards scavenged relics, including troll charms sought by the Darkspear. Captives are kept in wooden cages deep within, among them Ruul Snowhoof, a tauren brave.

subzone:thistlefur-village.text: Thistlefur Village. Thistlefur furbolgs attack outsiders from their village north of Astranaar. The tribe has fallen to corruption and now threatens travelers who approach its dens. North of Astranaar, Thistlefur Village lies among Ashenvale’s woodland communities. Corruption has taken hold of the Thistlefur tribe, leaving its furbolgs maddened and hostile. They guard the paths through their settlement and attack travelers who draw near. Two fierce chieftains, Dal Bloodclaw and Rorgish Jowl, lead the clan. Their aggression threatens those on the roads and in nearby settlements.

subzone:thistlefuzz-arcanery.text: Thistlefuzz Arcanery. East of the Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery draws enchanters and scholars. Gnome practitioners run this prominent workshop and academy, a haven for those who weave magic into metal and parchment. Its chambers hum with arcane energy beside the fires of dwarven industry. East of the Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery contrasts with the clanging anvils of dwarven smiths. Across its two levels, scholars, practitioners, and apprentices gather to study enchanting and the arcane arts. Dwarves reshape steel with muscle and fire; the gnomes here show how raw arcane energy can be bound into weapons, armor, and curious tools. For spellcasters making their way through the mountain stronghold, the Arcanery remains an essential sanctuary.

subzone:three-corners.text: Three Corners. At Three Corners, roads meet at the western edge of the Redridge Mountains. The routes link Goldshire, Lakeshire, and Darkshire, while Stormwind guards watch for gnolls threatening travelers and supply wagons. At Three Corners, three roads link the southern settlements of Stormwind. Goldshire lies west in Elwynn Forest, Lakeshire northeast in Redridge, and Darkshire south in Duskwood. Stormwind built Tower Watch at the junction, where guards and scouts try to keep the roads clear. Gnolls from Redridge threaten travelers and supply wagons moving between the regions.

subzone:thunder-falls.text: Thunder Falls. Thunder Falls lies in Elwynn Forest’s northwestern heights, where bandits have taken a riverside cottage. Thunder Falls cuts through the ridges above Mirror Lake, where a mountain stream rushes between steep cliffs. It enters over an unreachable cascade in the north, then spills away in waterfalls on both sides. One fall empties into Mirror Lake; the stream’s downstream course runs west toward Westfall’s rugged border. A cottage, dock, and outdoor forge sit beside the water. Bandits now claim the clearing.

subzone:thunderbrew-distillery.text: Thunderbrew Distillery. Travelers find the Thunderbrew Distillery at the heart of Kharanos, where ale and shelter await. Its brewhouse and tavern draw mountain travelers, while mentors and tradesfolk offer their skills within. The Thunderbrew Distillery anchors Kharanos in southern Dun Morogh. Arkilus Thunderbrew founded the brewhouse, and his kin have kept it in the family. Across Khaz Modan, its strong ales are known for warming those who face the mountain cold. Innkeeper Belm manages the inn, where weary mountaineers find a fire, hearty food, and beds beyond the blizzards outside. Kharanos is the first major settlement travelers reach after leaving Coldridge Valley, and the distillery gathers many kinds of instructors beneath its timber rafters. Teachers offer lessons in martial arts, holy rites, arcane studies, and roguecraft, alongside cooking and first aid. The hall pours its well-known stouts, but also gives travelers a place to prepare for the road ahead.

subzone:tinker-town.text: Tinker Town. In Tinker Town, gnomes make a home in exile beneath Ironforge. After Gnomeregan fell, the district became the seat of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque's government and the Ironforge terminus of the Deeprun Tram. Tinker Town shelters the gnomes who fled Gnomeregan. When troggs overran their high-tech city, Ironforge's dwarves opened their gates, setting aside a cavern that had housed dwarves and held the Deeprun Tram entrance. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his council lead the refugees here. Around a massive spherical contraption, the gnomes have rebuilt a semblance of their civilization amid whirring gears, experimental alchemy, and gadgetry. Though cramped guests in a stone city, they remain determined to reclaim their subterranean homeland. Tinker Town connects Ironforge to Stormwind by tram. The district holds the Ironforge entrance to the Deeprun Tram, an engineering wonder that swiftly links the dwarven capital with Stormwind.

subzone:tinkers-court.text: Tinkers' Court. In Gnomeregan's heart, Tinkers' Court once gathered the city's leaders. Now Mekgineer Thermaplugg holds it. Before disaster drove the gnomes from Gnomeregan, its leaders met in Tinkers' Court. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque gathered there with advisors and master inventors, including Tinkmaster Overspark. They debated new technology, governed civic matters, and guided gnomish society. The chamber stood beyond the Engineering Labs and the Launch Bay, at the center of gnomish government and invention.

subzone:tower-of-althalaxx.text: Tower of Althalaxx. Dark sorcery stirs within the Tower of Althalaxx on northern Darkshore's coast. Once Athrikus Narassin's retreat, the ancient Highborne spire now shelters demonic cultists and warlocks. Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne servants in Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran ten thousand years ago, placing the powerful sorcerer Athrikus Narassin in authority over them. As he grew distant from civic governance, Athrikus chose to isolate himself in the nearby Tower of Althalaxx. The Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, but the tower endured on Darkshore's desolate coastline, a quiet ruin of forgotten elven magic.

subzone:tower-of-azora.text: Tower of Azora. At the Tower of Azora, Archmage Theocritus leads a scholarly outpost in eastern Elwynn Forest. The slender spire stands north of the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where its human master keeps watch over a silent magical feud with a hostile tower in the Redridge Mountains. The Tower of Azora stands beside the eastern road to the Redridge Mountains, staffed almost entirely by gnome spellcasters. Archmage Theocritus guides their studies of strange curiosities and teaches wandering spellweavers. A wild magical aura surrounds the spire and sometimes warps nearby wildlife. Within the tower, gnome servants contend with enchanted household items and mutated insects that creep past the doorway.

subzone:tower-of-ilgalar.text: Tower of Ilgalar. In eastern Redridge, Morganth holds the Tower of Ilgalar and commands the Shadowhide gnolls. The banished sorcerer practices dark magic there, far from Stormwind. Morganth holds the Tower of Ilgalar above eastern Redridge. Cast out of Stormwind's Mage Quarter for forbidden magic, the sorcerer retreated to these rugged heights to pursue the dark arts beyond imperial interference. He rules the local Shadowhide gnoll clan, whose members guard the spire's base. Inside, conjured demonic hounds stalk the tower, and shadowy power threatens Lakeshire below. The Tower of Ilgalar draws comparisons to the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest. Who built Ilgalar remains a mystery, and the towers face one another in quiet magical opposition. In Elwynn, the archmage Theocritus watches Ilgalar through enchanted scrying devices such as the Eye of Azora. He monitors Morganth's experiments and seeks to stop the sorcerer's corruption from spreading through the kingdom.

subzone:trade-district.text: Trade District. Past the Valley of Heroes, Trade District draws Stormwind’s merchants and travelers. Its bank, Auction House, guild registry, and shops serve citizens and adventurers alike. You pass beneath the stone arches from the Valley of Heroes into Trade District. The open plaza is Stormwind’s main marketplace and a hub for goods and travel. The Auction House stands at its center, with the Stormwind Counting House, the city’s main bank, and The Gilded Rose nearby. From here, routes lead to Old Town, the Cathedral Square, and the Mage Quarter. Coin, raw goods, and supplies for adventurers pass through the district on their way across the realm. Shops line the paved avenues and canals, offering goods for daily needs and travel. Weller’s Arsenal and Lionheart Armory sell blades and mail, while The Empty Quiver offers bows. Stalls sell fresh flowers and aged vintages from the Gallina Winery. Just inside the gates, the Stormwind Visitor’s Center handles newly registered guild charters and tabard designs. On the eastern side, an elevated ramp leads to the Gryphon Roost, connecting Stormwind’s markets with Alliance territories.

subzone:tradesmen-s-terrace.text: Tradesmen's Terrace. Tradesmen's Terrace gathers Darnassus's merchants and craftspeople along the city's southern edge. Its auction house and shops connect travelers with goods from Teldrassil and beyond. Tradesmen's Terrace fills the southern stretch of Darnassus with shops and merchants. Here, kaldorei and travelers from the wider Alliance find provisions, crafting supplies, and the city's central auction house. Paths lead north to the Warrior's Terrace and west toward the Temple Gardens and the Temple of the Moon. For journeys into the wilds, this is where travelers gather what they need. Kaldorei shops favor quiet stone, timber, and woven goods, shaped to live in harmony with nature. The terrace has none of the roaring furnaces or smog found in dwarven and human workshops. Adventurers seeking trade contracts, repairs, or materials gathered from Teldrassil's boughs find the principal center of business in northern Kalimdor here.

subzone:train-depot.text: Train Depot. Beneath Gnomeregan's surface entrances in Dun Morogh, the Train Depot lies overrun by leper gnomes and troggs. Once a center of gnomish rail travel, it now stands in ruin. The Train Depot lies below the grand elevator from Dun Morogh, where rail lines once carried gnomes through Gnomeregan. Its platforms and tracks now lie in ruin. The radiation that swept through the city changed the workers who remained into crazed leper gnomes, and troggs from below have overrun the rails. You must cross the depot to reach deeper parts of the city, including Clockwerk Run, the Loading Room, and the inner engineering facilities.

subzone:tranquil-gardens-cemetery.text: Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Southeast of Darkshire, Tranquil Gardens Cemetery is overrun by shambling skeletons and ghouls. The former burial site has become an immediate hazard for the nearby town. Tranquil Gardens Cemetery was once a quiet resting place for the departed of Grand Hamlet. Dark curses settled over Duskwood, and the dead buried here began clawing their way out of their plots. Skeletal warriors, skeletal mages, and wandering undead haunt the gravestones. Though relatively weak beside the horrors deeper in the woods, they pose a relentless threat to townsfolk so close to Darkshire. Tranquil Gardens Cemetery lies close to Darkshire's edge, making it the Night Watch's frontline. The Watch often sends fresh recruits and arriving adventurers to cull the rising dead before they reach the settlement. More dangerous threats, such as the Insane Ghoul, lurk among the tumbled headstones and the ruined chapel.

subzone:tundrid-hills.text: Tundrid Hills. Snowbound ridges cut across the Tundrid Hills in south-central Dun Morogh, west of the Gol'Bolar Quarry. Dangerous wildlife keeps travelers to the rocky passes at their peril. The Tundrid Hills offer a rough route from Coldridge Valley to eastern Dun Morogh, away from the main roads through Kharanos. Jagged, snowy slopes make the crossing dangerous. Ferocious predators prowl the hills, so travelers who leave the beaten path face peril without a drawn weapon.

subzone:twilight-grove.text: Twilight Grove. Tucked away in the center of Duskwood, the Twilight Grove is a stunning enclave of lush Kalimdor flora contrasting the grim, blighted forest around it. Beneath its towering great tree and ancient night elf architecture sits a moonwell and a massive emerald gateway connected directly to the Emerald Dream. Hidden behind steep crater ridges in the heart of Duskwood, the Twilight Grove looks utterly alien to the Eastern Kingdoms. Ancient night elf gazebos, vibrant green meadows, and a serene moonwell frame an unnamed great tree that towers over the gloomy canopy. The tree stands as a conduit of nature, filtering the raw vigor of the Emerald Dream into the waking world and allowing this crater to thrive even beneath the eternal gloom of Duskwood. At the base of the great tree looms a massive stone portal, one of four known gateways across Azeroth linking the physical realm directly to the Emerald Dream. While traditionally watched over by Ysera's green dragonflight, dark whispers claim that malevolent forces have begun twisting the tranquil realm beyond. The gateway stands largely silent for now, but its emerald swirl serves as a grim reminder that cosmic corruption can spill forth into Duskwood from paths far deeper than the Scourge or the local worgen.

subzone:twilight-shore-darkshore.text: Twilight Shore (Darkshore). Murloc tribes and hungry sea creatures crowd the Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore. The rugged coast runs from the Long Wash to Ashenvale, where misty beaches meet cliffs, islets, and dangerous surf. The Twilight Shore runs south from the Long Wash, past Ameth'Aran's ruins, toward Ashenvale. Gray beaches give way to sharp cliffs and rocky islands. Threshadons and sea crawlers prowl the waters, while aggressive murloc camps line the shore.

subzone:twilight-vale.text: Twilight Vale. In Twilight Vale, beasts and furbolgs prowl the dark woods between Darkshore and Ashenvale. The southern forest is a perilous threshold between Darkshore’s tainted coast and Ashenvale’s sacred canopies. Twilight Vale stretches from south of Ameth'Aran to the Ashenvale border, where dusk holds over Darkshore’s southern woods. Corruption has reached deep into the wildlife. Rabid bears roam beside feral nightsabers, while hostile furbolg tribes stalk the trees. Sentinels and travelers advise you to keep to the main road. Even a few paces into the woods can bring a swift, deadly ambush.

subzone:valley-of-heroes.text: Valley of Heroes. Stone statues watch over the Valley of Heroes, where Stormwind's southern road crosses the moat into the city. They honor the leaders of the Alliance Expedition to Draenor, and guards hold this fortified entrance. You cross the moat beneath statues honoring the commanders of the Alliance Expedition. Stormwind's rebuilding after the Second War raised these monuments along the causeway. The champions marched through the Dark Portal into Draenor to seal the rift forever, giving their lives so Azeroth might survive. As you head north toward the Trade District, you pass Archmage Khadgar, Kurdran Wildhammer, Ranger-Captain Alleria Windrunner, Force Commander Danath Trollbane, and High General Turalyon. General Marcus Jonathan watches Stormwind's gates from horseback, overseeing the guards and the traffic in and out. The valley is the city's main defense against an overland invasion. Major Mattingly, Field Marshal Stonebridge, and rows of seasoned guards keep watch beside him, guarding the capital from threats beyond its walls.

subzone:valley-of-kings.text: Valley of Kings. At the Valley of Kings, stone kings watch the southern road into the Searing Gorge. The canyon lies in southwestern Loch Modan, south of the passage to Dun Morogh. Blackrock forces and troggs threaten travelers beneath the dwarven monuments. Two immense statues of King Madoran Bronzebeard and High Thane Khardros Wildhammer watch over the southern pass. After the kings died, their sons jointly commissioned the carvings. The statues honor the allied victory in the War of the Three Hammers and face the Dark Iron clan. Beyond them, the southern lands still bear the ruin left by Ragnaros's summoning. The valley links South Gate Pass with Stonesplinter Valley and holds an iron gate into the Searing Gorge. Hostile Blackrock orcs, Dark Iron dwarves, and volcanic dangers make the passage perilous, so Ironforge mountaineers keep the gate locked and guarded. Mountaineer Pebblebitty watches the threshold. Only the hardiest travelers who can show they have the strength to survive beyond it may pass.

subzone:vault-of-ironforge.text: Vault of Ironforge. In Ironforge's Commons, citizens and Alliance travelers bring their wealth to the Vault. It is the city's primary bank and treasure house, overseen by Dinita and the Stonemantle family. You find the Vault in the Commons, where travelers, soldiers, and merchants bring coin, relics, and provisions for safekeeping. City guards and tellers watch over its work. Dinita and the Stonemantle family oversee the bank, where citizens and Alliance visitors keep their wealth secure.

subzone:vul-gol-ogre-mound.text: Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. In southern Duskwood, Vul'Gol Ogre Mound lies under the Splinter Fist ogres and their chieftain, Zzarc'Vul. Ruined farmhouses and a cavern beneath the basin hold the clan's carcasses and scavenged plunder. Southwest of the fork toward Stranglethorn Vale, the basin is home to the Splinter Fist clan. Human families once farmed here, but they fled or perished, leaving hollow cabins that the ogres use for shelter. In the cavern beneath the rise, slaughtered black bears lie in piles. Zzarc'Vul rules the encampment, keeping odd trinkets beside ordinary goods the clan has scavenged. Darkshire's Night Watch is stretched thin, guarding the town from rabid worgen and restless dead. Commander Althea Ebonlocke and her militia rely on outside mercenaries to thin the Splinter Fist ranks before the ogres push north. The clan has also raided the recluse Abercrombie, stealing a crate of his alchemical tools. Inquisitive mages seek arcane lenses that Zzarc'Vul is rumored to possess.

subzone:war-room.text: War Room. Deep inside Stormwind Keep, the War Room gathers the arms, records, and charts used to plan the Alliance’s defense. Beyond Stormwind Keep’s grand chambers, commanders turn to military logistics and high-level campaign planning. Swords, blunderbusses, and heavy artillery cannons line the stone walls. Military treatises and chronicles of past wars fill nearby tables. At the center, a large map lets commanders assess Alliance deployments across Azeroth, while the royal court handles affairs of state just steps away.

subzone:warrior-s-terrace.text: Warrior's Terrace. At Darnassus's eastern edge, Sentinels patrol the Warrior's Terrace and its fortified gate. The district houses battlemasters and warrior trainers, with open plazas for drills and duels overlooking the road into greater Teldrassil. Sentinels guard Darnassus at the Warrior's Terrace, also called the Hall of Justice. Mounted on nightsabers, they watch the high arched gates for travelers coming from the Teldrassil wilds. In the open-air plazas, aspiring combatants drill beside seasoned veterans on dueling grounds and target ranges. Weapon smiths and armorers meet practical military needs, while battlemasters coordinate night elf forces across the wider world.

subzone:warsong-labor-camp.text: Warsong Labor Camp. Warsong Labor Camp cuts Ashenvale timber for the growing Horde. Its Warsong loggers and orcish sentries work in southeastern Ashenvale, far from help and under threat from the forest's defenders. East of Fallen Sky Lake and southwest of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, Warsong loggers cut Ashenvale's dense timber. Durotar's dry plains offer little wood for building cities such as Orgrimmar, so the Warsong clan has pushed into these contested woods. Loggers and orcish guards work far from other Horde settlements, felling ancient trees while night elf scouts and Alliance warbands threaten the camp. Warsong Labor Camp lies far from the main road and fortified bases such as Splintertree Post. Alliance raiders strike its working peons and watchmen, knowing help may be slow to arrive. Night elves see each felled tree as a desecration, and the camp remains a point of conflict in the war.

subzone:warsong-lumber-camp.text: Warsong Lumber Camp. Warsong Lumber Camp cuts timber from Ashenvale for the Horde, keeping its conflict with the night elves alive. Kargathia Keep anchors the fortified operation. Warsong Lumber Camp cuts into eastern Ashenvale's dense canopy for the Horde. Orc peons and hired goblin engineers use whirring shredders to turn towering trunks into lumber for nearby Splintertree Post and the fledgling nation of Durotar. Kargathia Keep's stockades anchor the defenses against night elf counterattacks, and the camp keeps war wolves in an active kennel. For the Warsong, each felled tree means survival and strength. For the native Sentinels, each saw blade is an act of sacrilege. Warsong clan warriors first entered these woods with Grom Hellscream during the Third War, seeking timber for the Horde. Their clearing of the forest enraged the demigod Cenarius and drew the ancient wrath of the night elves. The camp now flies the banners of Thrall's Horde, but old hatreds still burn. Untamed timber, hostile elves, and demonic corruption around neighboring Felfire Hill surround the camp. Its defenders stay armed around the clock, axes in hand as they harvest, ready to abandon their timber when the next ambush comes.

subzone:weathered-nook.text: Weathered Nook. Tucked away along the northern cliffside of Thousand Needles, the Weathered Nook is a secluded cleft and shelter perched high above the canyon floor. Overlooking the vast sea of stone spires, it serves as a modest home and retreat for solitary tauren dwellers seeking quiet contemplation away from bustling settlements. Carved into the sheer sandstone wall north of Freewind Post, the Weathered Nook is easily missed by travelers passing along the canyon basin below. A natural ramp winds up the cliff face, leading to a sheltered ledge and cave out of the prevailing winds. Rather than housing a military outpost or large settlement, the nook serves as a humble homestead for solitary wanderers like Dorn Plainstalker and Prate Cloudseer, offering safety, seclusion, and a sweeping view across the windswept needle plateaus.

subzone:webwinder-path.text: Webwinder Path. Webwinder Path winds through the lower Stonetalon Mountains, linking Malaka'jin with Mirkfallon Lake. Spiders and native beasts roam its crags and woods. Webwinder Path runs from Malaka'jin toward Mirkfallon Lake through the lower Stonetalon Mountains. Thick webs hang among the trees and along the jagged cliffs. Mountain spiders prowl the road, while thunder lizards and territorial rams roam nearby. Travelers must watch their step along the winding route.

subzone:wellspring-lake.text: Wellspring Lake. At Wellspring Lake, springs feed the river while corruption stirs the wildlife. The lake lies northeast of Darnassus, where night elf fishermen once found a quiet retreat. Wellspring Lake lies between Darnassus and the Oracle Glade, beneath Teldrassil’s canopy. Night elves once came to its clear waters to fish and sit in quiet thought. Springs deep within the World Tree feed the lake, and its waters flow north through the Wellspring River. Now a blight troubles the surrounding wilds. Aggressive spiders, prowling nightsabers, and agitated timberlings roam the banks, making the shore dangerous for travelers.

subzone:wellspring-river.text: Wellspring River. In Teldrassil, Wellspring River carries fresh water north from Wellspring Lake before plunging to the ocean below. Its banks have grown dangerous as the timberlings turn hostile. Wellspring River runs north from Wellspring Lake through Teldrassil's forest before falling from the great tree into the sea below. Its banks are no longer safe. The timberlings living there have grown crazed and attack travelers and druids who come near the water.

subzone:westbrook-garrison.text: Westbrook Garrison. At Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer's few guards hold Elwynn's western road against gnolls and bandits. The outpost is short on soldiers and supplies, with danger rising near the Westfall border. Westbrook Garrison watches the road where Elwynn Forest thins toward Westfall. Deputy Rainer and a handful of guards patrol the western roads with too few soldiers to cover them. Much of the Stormwind Army serves abroad, while political indecision in the capital leaves the outpost without needed support. Thieves grow bolder, and Riverpaw gnolls have overrun the southern woods. Marshal Dughan in Goldshire has not sent formal reinforcements, so the guards depend on travelers to help secure the highway.
